1.47.s:
sanandana uvāca
etadadhyātmamānāḍhyaṃ vacaḥ keśidhvajasya saḥ /
khāṇḍikyo 'mṛtavacchratvā punarāha tamīrayan //
1.47.d:
सनन्दन उवाच
एतदध्यात्ममानाढ्यं वचः केशिध्वजस्य सः ।
खाण्डिक्यो ऽमृतवच्छ्रत्वा पुनराह तमीरयन् ॥
1.47.m:
Sanandana said:
Having heard these words of Keśidhvaja, rich in the science of the Self, like nectar,
Khāṇḍikya spoke again, addressing him:

1.47.s:
khāṇḍikya uvāca
tad brūhi tvaṃ mahābhāga yogaṃ yogaviduttama /
vijñātayo gaśāstrārthastvamasyāṃ nimisaṃtatau //
1.47.d:
खाण्डिक्य उवाच
तद् ब्रूहि त्वं महाभाग योगं योगविदुत्तम ।
विज्ञातयो गशास्त्रार्थस्त्वमस्यां निमिसंततौ ॥
1.47.m:
Khāṇḍikya said:
“Therefore tell me about yoga, O fortunate one, foremost among knowers of yoga!
You have understood the meaning of the treatises on yoga in this lineage of Nimi.”

1.47.s:
keśidhvaja uvāca
yogasvarūpaṃ khāṇḍikya śrūyatāṃ gadato mama /
yatra sthito na cyavate prāpya brahmalayaṃ muniḥ //
1.47.d:
केशिध्वज उवाच
योगस्वरूपं खाण्डिक्य श्रूयतां गदतो मम ।
यत्र स्थितो न च्यवते प्राप्य ब्रह्मलयं मुनिः ॥
1.47.m:
Keśidhvaja said:
“Hear from me as I speak, Khāṇḍikya, the nature of yoga,
established in which the sage, having attained dissolution in Brahman, does not fall.

1.47.s:
mana eva manuṣyāṇāṃ kāraṇaṃ bandhamokṣayoḥ /
bandhasya viṣayāsaṃgi mukternirviṣayaṃ tathā //
1.47.d:
मन एव मनुष्याणां कारणं बन्धमोक्षयोः ।
बन्धस्य विषयासंगि मुक्तेर्निर्विषयं तथा ॥
1.47.m:
The mind alone is the cause of bondage and liberation for human beings:
attached to sense objects, it leads to bondage; free from sense objects, to liberation.

1.47.s:
viṣayebhyaḥ samāhṛtya vijñānātmā budho manaḥ /
cintayenmuktaye tena brahmabhūtaṃ pareśvaram //
1.47.d:
विषयेभ्यः समाहृत्य विज्ञानात्मा बुधो मनः ।
चिन्तयेन्मुक्तये तेन ब्रह्मभूतं परेश्वरम् ॥
1.47.m:
Having withdrawn the mind from sense objects, the wise one, of the nature of understanding,
should meditate with it upon the Supreme Lord who is Brahman, for the sake of liberation.

1.47.s:
ātmabhāvaṃ nayettena tadbrīhyadhyāpanaṃ manaḥ /
vikāryamātmanaḥ śaktyā lohamākarṣako yathā //
1.47.d:
आत्मभावं नयेत्तेन तद्ब्रीह्यध्यापनं मनः ।
विकार्यमात्मनः शक्त्या लोहमाकर्षको यथा ॥
1.47.m:
By that means he should bring the mind to the state of the Self, directing it to that Brahman;
as a magnet acts upon iron, it is to be transformed by its own power.

1.47.s:
ātmaprayatnasāpekṣā viśiṣṭā yā manogatiḥ /
tasyā brahmaṇi saṃyogo yoga ityabhidhīyate //
1.47.d:
आत्मप्रयत्नसापेक्षा विशिष्टा या मनोगतिः ।
तस्या ब्रह्मणि संयोगो योग इत्यभिधीयते ॥
1.47.m:
That distinct movement of the mind which depends upon self-effort,
its union with Brahman, is called yoga.

1.47.s:
evamatyantavaiśiṣṭyayuktadharmopalakṣaṇam /
yasya yogaḥ sa vai yogī mumukṣuramidhīyate //
1.47.d:
एवमत्यन्तवैशिष्ट्ययुक्तधर्मोपलक्षणम् ।
यस्य योगः स वै योगी मुमुक्षुरमिधीयते ॥
1.47.m:
He whose yoga is characterized by attributes endowed with such extreme distinction
is indeed designated a yogin, a seeker of liberation.

1.47.s:
yogayuk prathamaṃ yogī yuñjamāno 'bhidhīyate /
viniṣyannasamādhistu parabrahmopalabdhimān //
1.47.d:
योगयुक् प्रथमं योगी युञ्जमानो ऽभिधीयते ।
विनिष्यन्नसमाधिस्तु परब्रह्मोपलब्धिमान् ॥
1.47.m:
First, the yogin joined in yoga is called one who is practicing;
but the one whose absorption is accomplished is one who perceives the Supreme Brahman.

1.47.s:
yadyantarāyadoṣeṇa dūṣyate nāsya mānasam /
janmāntarairabhyasanānmuktiḥ pūrvasya jāyate //
1.47.d:
यद्यन्तरायदोषेण दूष्यते नास्य मानसम् ।
जन्मान्तरैरभ्यसनान्मुक्तिः पूर्वस्य जायते ॥
1.47.m:
If his mind is not corrupted by the fault of obstacles,
liberation comes to the former through practice over other births.

1.47.s:
viniṣpannasamādhistu muktistatraiva janmani /
prāpnoti yogī yogāgnidagdhakarmacayo 'cirāt //
1.47.d:
विनिष्पन्नसमाधिस्तु मुक्तिस्तत्रैव जन्मनि ।
प्राप्नोति योगी योगाग्निदग्धकर्मचयो ऽचिरात् ॥
1.47.m:
The yogin whose absorption is accomplished, however, attains liberation in that very birth,
the heap of his past actions quickly burnt by the fire of yoga.

1.47.s:
brahmacaryamahiṃsāṃ ca satyāsteyāparigrahān /
seveta yogī niṣkāmo yigitāṃ svamano nayan //
1.47.d:
ब्रह्मचर्यमहिंसां च सत्यास्तेयापरिग्रहान् ।
सेवेत योगी निष्कामो यिगितां स्वमनो नयन् ॥
1.47.m:
A yogin should cultivate celibacy, non-violence,
truthfulness, non-stealing, and non-possession, desireless, bringing his mind under control.

1.47.s:
svādhyāyaśaucasaṃtoṣatapāṃsi niyamānyamān /
kurvvīta brahmaṇi tathā parisminpravaṇaṃ manaḥ //
1.47.d:
स्वाध्यायशौचसंतोषतपांसि नियमान्यमान् ।
कुर्व्वीत ब्रह्मणि तथा परिस्मिन्प्रवणं मनः ॥
1.47.m: [He should practice] study of the scriptures, purity, contentment, and austerities as observances, and the restraints; / likewise he should make his mind inclined toward the supreme Brahman.

1.47.s:
ete yamāśca niyamāḥ pañca pañcaprakīrtitāḥ /
viśiṣṭaphaladāḥ kāmyā niṣkāmānāṃ vimuktidāḥ //
1.47.d:
एते यमाश्च नियमाः पञ्च पञ्चप्रकीर्तिताः ।
विशिष्टफलदाः काम्या निष्कामानां विमुक्तिदाः ॥
1.47.m: These restraints and observances are taught to be five each; / when desired with motive they grant distinguished fruits, but to the motiveless they grant liberation.

1.47.s:
evaṃ bhadrāsanādīnāṃ samāsthāya guṇairyutaḥ /
yamākhyairniyamākhyaiśca yuñjīta niyato yatiḥ //
1.47.d:
एवं भद्रासनादीनां समास्थाय गुणैर्युतः ।
यमाख्यैर्नियमाख्यैश्च युञ्जीत नियतो यतिः ॥
1.47.m: Thus seated in bhadrāsana or other postures, endowed with the qualities / called restraints and observances, the restrained ascetic should practice yoga.

1.47.s:
prāṇākhyamavalaṃbasthamabhyāsātkurute tu yat /
prāṇāyāmaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ sabījo 'bīja eva ca //
1.47.d:
प्राणाख्यमवलंबस्थमभ्यासात्कुरुते तु यत् ।
प्राणायामः स विज्ञेयः सबीजो ऽबीज एव च ॥
1.47.m: That which, based on an object of support, one performs through practice upon the breath, / is to be known as prāṇāyāma, both with seed and without seed.

1.47.s:
paraspareṇābhibhavaṃ prāṇāpānau yadā nilau /
kurutaḥ sadvidhānena tṛtīyaḥ saṃyamāttayoḥ //
1.47.d:
परस्परेणाभिभवं प्राणापानौ यदा निलौ ।
कुरुतः सद्विधानेन तृतीयः संयमात्तयोः ॥
1.47.m: When the two winds, prāṇa and apāna, subdue each other / according to the true method, a third [state arises] from the restraint of both.

1.47.s:
tasya cāṃlabanavatsthūlaṃ rūpaṃ dviṣatpate /
ālaṃbanamanantasya yogino 'bhyasataḥ smṛtam //
1.47.d:
तस्य चांलबनवत्स्थूलं रूपं द्विषत्पते ।
आलंबनमनन्तस्य योगिनो ऽभ्यसतः स्मृतम् ॥
1.47.m: Its support is the gross form [of the Lord], O slayer of foes; / the gross form is taught to be the support of the Infinite for the practicing yogī.

1.47.s:
śabdādiṣvanuraktāni nigṛhyākṣāṇi yogavit /
kuryyāñcittānukārīṇi pratyāhāraparāyaṇaḥ //
1.47.d:
शब्दादिष्वनुरक्तानि निगृह्याक्षाणि योगवित् ।
कुर्य्याञ्चित्तानुकारीणि प्रत्याहारपरायणः ॥
1.47.m: Restraining the senses that are attached to sound and the rest, / the knower of yoga, intent upon pratyāhāra, should make them conform to the mind.

1.47.s:
vaśyatā paramā tena jāyate niścalā tmanām /
indriyāṇāmavaśyaistairna yogī yogasādhakaḥ //
1.47.d:
वश्यता परमा तेन जायते निश्चला त्मनाम् ।
इन्द्रियाणामवश्यैस्तैर्न योगी योगसाधकः ॥
1.47.m: Thereby supreme mastery arises for those whose minds are steady; / with senses unsubdued, the yogī cannot accomplish yoga.

1.47.s:
prāṇāyāmena pavanaiḥ pratyāhareṇa cendriyaiḥ /
vaśīkṛtaistataḥ kuryātsthiraṃ cetaḥ śubhāśraye //
1.47.d:
प्राणायामेन पवनैः प्रत्याहरेण चेन्द्रियैः ।
वशीकृतैस्ततः कुर्यात्स्थिरं चेतः शुभाश्रये ॥
1.47.m: With the winds subdued through prāṇāyāma and the senses through pratyāhāra, / he should then make his mind steady upon the auspicious support.

1.47.s:
khāṇḍikya uvāca
kathyatāṃ me mahābhāga cetaso yaḥ śubhāśrayaḥ /
yadādhāramaśeṣaṃ tu hṝnti doṣasamudbhavam //
1.47.d:
खाण्डिक्य उवाच
कथ्यतां मे महाभाग चेतसो यः शुभाश्रयः ।
यदाधारमशेषं तु हॄन्ति दोषसमुद्भवम् ॥
1.47.m:
Khāṇḍikya said:
Tell me, O fortunate one, what is that auspicious support of the mind, / depending upon which it completely removes faults born of [worldly] origin?

1.47.s:
keśidhvaja uvāca
āśrayaścetaso jñānin dvidhā tañca svarūpataḥ /
rūpaṃ mūrtamamūrtaṃ ca paraṃ cāparameva ca //
1.47.d:
केशिध्वज उवाच
आश्रयश्चेतसो ज्ञानिन् द्विधा तञ्च स्वरूपतः ।
रूपं मूर्तममूर्तं च परं चापरमेव च ॥
1.47.m:
Keśidhvaja said:
O wise one, the support of the mind is two-fold according to its nature: / the form [is both] embodied and unembodied, supreme and non-supreme.

1.47.s:
trividhā bhāvanā rūpaṃ viśvametattridhocyate /
brahmākhyā karmasaṃjñā ca tathā caivobhayātmikā //
1.47.d:
त्रिविधा भावना रूपं विश्वमेतत्त्रिधोच्यते ।
ब्रह्माख्या कर्मसंज्ञा च तथा चैवोभयात्मिका ॥
1.47.m: The three-fold conception is its form; this universe is said to be three-fold: / that called Brahman, that termed ritual action, and likewise that which is of the nature of both.

1.47.s:
karmabhāvātmikā hyekā brahmabhāvātmikāparā /
ubhayātmikā tathaivānyā trividhā bhāvabhāvanā //
1.47.d:
कर्मभावात्मिका ह्येका ब्रह्मभावात्मिकापरा ।
उभयात्मिका तथैवान्या त्रिविधा भावभावना ॥
1.47.m: One is of the nature of the conception of action; another is of the nature of the conception of Brahman; / and another is likewise of the nature of both: thus three-fold is the conception of being.

1.47.s:
sanakādyā sadā jñānin brahmabhāvanayā yutāḥ /
karmabhāvanayā cānye devādyāḥ sthāvarāścarāḥ //
1.47.d:
सनकाद्या सदा ज्ञानिन् ब्रह्मभावनया युताः ।
कर्मभावनया चान्ये देवाद्याः स्थावराश्चराः ॥
1.47.m: Sanaka and the others, O wise one, are ever endowed with the conception of Brahman, / while other beings, beginning with the gods down to immobile and mobile creatures, have the conception of action.

1.47.s:
hiraṇyagarbhādiṣu ca brahmakarmātmikā dvidhā /
adhikārabodhayukteṣu vidyate bhāvabhāvanā //
1.47.d:
हिरण्यगर्भादिषु च ब्रह्मकर्मात्मिका द्विधा ।
अधिकारबोधयुक्तेषु विद्यते भावभावना ॥
1.47.m: In Hiraṇyagarbha and the rest, the conception of being exists as two-fold, / consisting of Brahman and action, in those who are endowed with qualification and understanding.

1.47.s:
akṣīṇeṣu samasteṣu viśeṣajñānakarmasu /
viśvametatparaṃ cānyadbhedabhinnadṛśāṃ nṛpa //
1.47.d:
अक्षीणेषु समस्तेषु विशेषज्ञानकर्मसु ।
विश्वमेतत्परं चान्यद्भेदभिन्नदृशां नृप ॥
1.47.m: Until all differentiation of knowledge and action is extinguished, / this universe appears supreme and other to those of divided vision, O king.

1.47.s:
pratyastamitabhedaṃ yatsattāmātramagocaram /
vacasāmātmasaṃtodyaṃ tajjñānaṃ brahmasaṃjñitam //
1.47.d:
प्रत्यस्तमितभेदं यत्सत्तामात्रमगोचरम् ।
वचसामात्मसंतोद्यं तज्ज्ञानं ब्रह्मसंज्ञितम् ॥
1.47.m: That in which differentiation has set, which is pure existence, beyond the range / of words, to be known within oneself—that knowledge is termed Brahman.

1.47.s:
tacca viṣṇoḥ paraṃ rūpamarūpasyājanasya ca /
viśvasvarūpaṃ vairūpyalakṣaṇaṃ paramātmanaḥ //
1.47.d:
तच्च विष्णोः परं रूपमरूपस्याजनस्य च ।
विश्वस्वरूपं वैरूप्यलक्षणं परमात्मनः ॥
1.47.m: And that is the supreme, formless, unborn form of Viṣṇu, / whose own nature is the universe, yet whose characteristic is difference of form from the Supreme Self.

1.47.s:
na tadyogayujā śakyaṃ nṛpa cintayituṃ yataḥ /
tataḥ sthūlaṃ hare rūpaṃ cintyaṃ yañcakṣugocaram //
1.47.d:
न तद्योगयुजा शक्यं नृप चिन्तयितुं यतः ।
ततः स्थूलं हरे रूपं चिन्त्यं यञ्चक्षुगोचरम् ॥
1.47.m: Since that cannot be meditated upon by one practicing yoga, O king, / therefore the gross form of Hari, which falls within the range of the eye, is to be meditated upon.

1.47.s:
hiraṇyagarbho bhagavānvāsavo 'tha prajāpatiḥ /
maruto vasavo rudrā bhāskārāstārakā grahāḥ //
1.47.d:
हिरण्यगर्भो भगवान्वासवो ऽथ प्रजापतिः ।
मरुतो वसवो रुद्रा भास्कारास्तारका ग्रहाः ॥
1.47.m: The lord Hiraṇyagarbha, Indra, Prajāpati, / the Maruts, the Vasus, the Rudras, the suns, the stars, the planets,

1.47.s:
gandharvā yakṣadaityāśca sakalā devayotayaḥ /
manuṣyāḥ paśavaḥ śailāsamudrāḥ sarito drumāḥ //
1.47.d:
गन्धर्वा यक्षदैत्याश्च सकला देवयोतयः ।
मनुष्याः पशवः शैलासमुद्राः सरितो द्रुमाः ॥
1.47.m: the Gandharvas, the Yakṣas, the Daityas, all the divine wombs, / human beings, animals, mountains, oceans, rivers, trees,

1.47.s:
bhūpa bhūtānyaśeṣāṇi bhūtānāṃ ye ca hetavaḥ /
pradhānādiviśeṣāntāścetanāñcetanātmakam //
1.47.d:
भूप भूतान्यशेषाणि भूतानां ये च हेतवः ।
प्रधानादिविशेषान्ताश्चेतनाञ्चेतनात्मकम् ॥
1.47.m: all the beings, O king, and the causes of beings / ending with the specific evolutes beginning with the unmanifest, consisting of both conscious and unconscious,

1.47.s:
ekapādaṃ dvipādaṃ ca bahupādamapādakam /
mūrttametaddhare rūpaṃ bhāvanātritayātmakam //
1.47.d:
एकपादं द्विपादं च बहुपादमपादकम् ।
मूर्त्तमेतद्धरे रूपं भावनात्रितयात्मकम् ॥
1.47.m: one-footed, two-footed, many-footed, and footless— / this is the embodied form of Hari, consisting of the triad of conceptions.

1.47.s:
etatsarvamidaṃ viṃśvaṃ jagadetañcarācaram /
parabrahmasvarūpasya viṣṇoḥ śaktisamanvitam //
1.47.d:
एतत्सर्वमिदं विंश्वं जगदेतञ्चराचरम् ।
परब्रह्मस्वरूपस्य विष्णोः शक्तिसमन्वितम् ॥
1.47.m: All this universe, this moving and unmoving world, / is endowed with the power of Viṣṇu, whose essential nature is the Supreme Brahman.

1.47.s:
viṣṇuśaktiḥ parā proktā kṣetrajñākhyā tathāparā /
avidyākarmasaṃjñānyā tṛtīyā śaktiriṣyate //
1.47.d:
विष्णुशक्तिः परा प्रोक्ता क्षेत्रज्ञाख्या तथापरा ।
अविद्याकर्मसंज्ञान्या तृतीया शक्तिरिष्यते ॥
1.47.m: The power of Viṣṇu is said to be supreme; another is termed the knower of the field; / and a third power is acknowledged, termed ignorance and action.

1.47.s:
yeyaṃ kṣetrajñaśaktiḥ sā ceṣṭitā nṛpa karmajā /
asārabhūte saṃsāre proktā tatra mahāmate //
1.47.d:
येयं क्षेत्रज्ञशक्तिः सा चेष्टिता नृप कर्मजा ।
असारभूते संसारे प्रोक्ता तत्र महामते ॥
1.47.m: This power called the knower of the field, O king, functions as born of action; / it is declared [to abide] there in the worthless saṃsāra, O wise one.

1.47.s:
saṃsāratāpānakhilānavāpnotyanusaṃjñitān /
tayā tirohitatvāttu śaktiḥ kṣetrajña saṃjñitā //
1.47.d:
संसारतापानखिलानवाप्नोत्यनुसंज्ञितान् ।
तया तिरोहितत्वात्तु शक्तिः क्षेत्रज्ञ संज्ञिता ॥
1.47.m: Because it is veiled by that [ignorance], the power called the knower of the field / experiences all the afflictions of saṃsāra, according to its name.

1.47.s:
sarvabhūteṣu bhūpāla tāratamyena lakṣyate /
aprāṇavatsu khalvalpā sthāvareṣu tato 'dhikā //
1.47.d:
सर्वभूतेषु भूपाल तारतम्येन लक्ष्यते ।
अप्राणवत्सु खल्वल्पा स्थावरेषु ततो ऽधिका ॥
1.47.m: In all beings, O protector of the earth, it is perceived in gradations; / it is indeed very small in the lifeless, and greater in the immobile.

1.47.s:
sarīsṛpeṣu tebhyo 'nyāpyatiśaktyā patatriśu /
patatrribhyo mṛgāstebhyaḥ svaśaktyā paśavo 'dhikāḥ //
1.47.d:
सरीसृपेषु तेभ्यो ऽन्याप्यतिशक्त्या पतत्रिशु ।
पतत्र्रिभ्यो मृगास्तेभ्यः स्वशक्त्या पशवो ऽधिकाः ॥
1.47.m: In reptiles it is other than those, and with still greater power in birds; / deer are greater than birds, and domestic beasts are greater than them in their own power.

1.47.s:
paśubhyo manujāścātiśaktyā puṃsaḥprabhāvitāḥ /
tebhyo 'pi nāgagandharvayakṣādyā devatā nṛpa //
1.47.d:
पशुभ्यो मनुजाश्चातिशक्त्या पुंसःप्रभाविताः ।
तेभ्यो ऽपि नागगन्धर्वयक्षाद्या देवता नृप ॥
1.47.m: Men are manifested with exceeding power above beasts, / and above them are the deities, O king, beginning with the Nāgas, Gandharvas, and Yakṣas.

1.47.s:
śakraḥ samastadevebhyastataścātiprajāpatiḥ /
hiraṇyagarbho 'pi tataḥ puṃsaḥ śaktyupalakṣitaḥ //
1.47.d:
शक्रः समस्तदेवेभ्यस्ततश्चातिप्रजापतिः ।
हिरण्यगर्भो ऽपि ततः पुंसः शक्त्युपलक्षितः ॥
1.47.m: Indra is above all the gods, and Prajāpati is beyond him; / and Hiraṇyagarbha beyond him is marked with the power of the Spirit.

1.47.s:
etānyaśeṣarūpāṇi tasya rūpāṇi pārthiva /
yatastacchaktiyogena yuktāni nabhasā yathā //
1.47.d:
एतान्यशेषरूपाणि तस्य रूपाणि पार्थिव ।
यतस्तच्छक्तियोगेन युक्तानि नभसा यथा ॥
1.47.m: All these limitless forms are his forms, O king, / because they are united through connection with his power, like space.

1.47.s:
dvitīyaṃ viṣṇusaṃjñasya yogidhyeyaṃ mahāmate /
amṛrtaṃ brahmaṇo rūpaṃ yatsadityucyate budhaiḥ //
1.47.d:
द्वितीयं विष्णुसंज्ञस्य योगिध्येयं महामते ।
अमृर्तं ब्रह्मणो रूपं यत्सदित्युच्यते बुधैः ॥
1.47.m: The second [form] of the one called Viṣṇu, to be meditated upon by yogīs, O wise one, / is the unembodied form of Brahman, which is called 'the Real' by the wise,

1.47.s:
samastāḥ śaktayaścaitā nṛpa yatra pratiṣṭitāḥ /
nahi svarūparūpaṃ vai rūpamanyaddharermahat //
1.47.d:
समस्ताः शक्तयश्चैता नृप यत्र प्रतिष्टिताः ।
नहि स्वरूपरूपं वै रूपमन्यद्धरेर्महत् ॥
1.47.m: wherein all these powers are established, O king. / Indeed, there is no other great form of Hari than his essential form.

1.47.s:
samastaśaktirūpāṇi tatkaroti janeśvara /
devatiryaṅmanuṣyādiceṣṭāvanti svalīlayā //
1.47.d:
समस्तशक्तिरूपाणि तत्करोति जनेश्वर ।
देवतिर्यङ्मनुष्यादिचेष्टावन्ति स्वलीलया ॥
1.47.m: He produces all forms of power, O ruler of people, / possessing the activities of gods, animals, humans, and the rest, by his own play.

1.47.s:
jagatāmupakārāya tasya karmanimittajā /
ceṣṭā tasyāprameyasya vyāpinyavihitātmikā //
1.47.d:
जगतामुपकाराय तस्य कर्मनिमित्तजा ।
चेष्टा तस्याप्रमेयस्य व्यापिन्यविहितात्मिका ॥
1.47.m: For the welfare of the worlds, his activity is not caused by karma; / the activity of that immeasurable, all-pervading one is autonomous.

1.47.s:
tadrūpaṃ viśvarūpāya cintyaṃ yoga yujā nṛpa /
tasya hyātmaviśuddhyarthaṃ sarvakilbiṣanāśanam //
1.47.d:
तद्रूपं विश्वरूपाय चिन्त्यं योग युजा नृप ।
तस्य ह्यात्मविशुद्ध्यर्थं सर्वकिल्बिषनाशनम् ॥
1.47.m: That form of the Universal Form is to be meditated upon by one joined in yoga, O king; / indeed, for his self-purification, it destroys all sin.

1.47.s:
yathāgnirūddhataśikhaḥ kakṣaṃ dahati sānilaḥ /
tathā cittasthito viṣṇuryogināṃ sarvakilbiṣam //
1.47.d:
यथाग्निरूद्धतशिखः कक्षं दहति सानिलः ।
तथा चित्तस्थितो विष्णुर्योगिनां सर्वकिल्बिषम् ॥
1.47.m: Just as a fire with leaping flames, accompanied by wind, burns up dry grass, / even so Viṣṇu, residing in the mind, burns all the sin of yogīs.

1.47.s:
tasmātsamastaśaktīnāmāndyānte tatra cetasaḥ /
kurvīta saṃsthitaṃ sādhu vijñeyā śuddhalakṣaṇā //
1.47.d:
तस्मात्समस्तशक्तीनामान्द्यान्ते तत्र चेतसः ।
कुर्वीत संस्थितं साधु विज्ञेया शुद्धलक्षणा ॥
1.47.m: Therefore, upon that which is the beginning and end of all powers, / one should establish the mind well; it is to be known as pure by nature.

1.47.s:
śubhāṃśrayaḥ sacittasya sarvagasya tathātmanaḥ /
tribhāvabhāvanātīto muktaye yogināṃ nṛpa //
1.47.d:
शुभांश्रयः सचित्तस्य सर्वगस्य तथात्मनः ।
त्रिभावभावनातीतो मुक्तये योगिनां नृप ॥
1.47.m: That auspicious support of the mind, and likewise of the all-pervading Self, / is beyond the three conceptions of being, for the liberation of yogīs, O king.

1.47.s:
anye tu puruṣavyāghra cetaso ye vyāpā8yāḥ /
aśuddhāste samastāstu devādyāḥ karmayonayaḥ //
1.47.d:
अन्ये तु पुरुषव्याघ्र चेतसो ये व्यापा8याः ।
अशुद्धास्ते समस्तास्तु देवाद्याः कर्मयोनयः ॥
1.47.m: Other supports of the mind, O tiger among men, / are all impure, beginning with the gods, having action as their origin.

1.47.s:
mūrttaṃ bhagavato rūpaṃ sarvāpāśrayanispṛhaḥ /
eṣā vai dhāraṇā jñeyā yañcitaṃ tatra dhāryate //
1.47.d:
मूर्त्तं भगवतो रूपं सर्वापाश्रयनिस्पृहः ।
एषा वै धारणा ज्ञेया यञ्चितं तत्र धार्यते ॥
1.47.m: When one is detached from all other supports, [focusing on] the embodied form of the Lord, / this is indeed to be known as dhāraṇā, wherein the mind is held fixed there.

1.47.s:
tatra mūrttaṃ hare rūpaṃ yādṛk cintyaṃ narādhipa /
tacchrūyatā manādhāre dhāraṇā nopapadyate //
1.47.d:
तत्र मूर्त्तं हरे रूपं यादृक् चिन्त्यं नराधिप ।
तच्छ्रूयता मनाधारे धारणा नोपपद्यते ॥
1.47.m: Hear what kind of embodied form of Hari is to be meditated upon there, O king; / without a support, dhāraṇā is not possible.

1.47.s:
prasannacāruvadanaṃ padmapatrāyatekṣaṇam /
sukapolaṃ suvistīrṇaṃ lalāṭaphalakojjvam //
1.47.d:
प्रसन्नचारुवदनं पद्मपत्रायतेक्षणम् ।
सुकपोलं सुविस्तीर्णं ललाटफलकोज्ज्वम् ॥
1.47.m: One should meditate upon him whose face is serene and handsome, whose eyes are long like lotus petals, / who has beautiful cheeks and a broad, radiant forehead-slab,

1.47.s:
samakarṇāṃsavinya stacārukarṇopabhūṣaṇam /
kambugrīvaṃ suvistīrṇaśrīvatsāṃkitavakṣasam //
1.47.d:
समकर्णांसविन्य स्तचारुकर्णोपभूषणम् ।
कम्बुग्रीवं सुविस्तीर्णश्रीवत्सांकितवक्षसम् ॥
1.47.m: who has lovely ear ornaments resting on symmetrical ears and shoulders, / who has a conch-like neck and a broad chest marked with the Śrīvatsa,

1.47.s:
balitriṃbhāginā bhugnanābhinā codareṇa vai /
pralaṃbāṣṭabhujaṃ viṣṇumatha vāpi caturbhujam //
1.47.d:
बलित्रिंभागिना भुग्ननाभिना चोदरेण वै ।
प्रलंबाष्टभुजं विष्णुमथ वापि चतुर्भुजम् ॥
1.47.m: with an abdomen graced with three folds and a deep navel, / having long, eight arms—or else four arms—namely Viṣṇu,

1.47.s:
samasthitorujaghanaṃ susthirāṅghrikarāṃbujaṃm /
cintayedbūhyabhūtaṃ taṃ pītanirmalavāsasam //
1.47.d:
समस्थितोरुजघनं सुस्थिराङ्घ्रिकरांबुजंम् ।
चिन्तयेद्बूह्यभूतं तं पीतनिर्मलवाससम् ॥
1.47.m: with well-proportioned thighs and hips, with very steady lotus feet and lotus hands, / wearing pure yellow garments, meditated upon as a manifest entity,

1.47.s:
kirīṭacārukeyūrakaṭakādivibhūṣitam /
śārṅgaśaṅkhagadākhaḍgaprakāśavalayāñcitam //
1.47.d:
किरीटचारुकेयूरकटकादिविभूषितम् ।
शार्ङ्गशङ्खगदाखड्गप्रकाशवलयाञ्चितम् ॥
1.47.m: adorned with a diadem, lovely armlets, bracelets, and other ornaments, / and embellished with a brilliant discus, the bow Śārṅga, a conch, a mace, and a sword.

1.47.s:
cintayettanmayo yogī samādhāyātmamānasam /
tāvadyāvad dṛḍhībhūtā tatraiva nṛpa dhāraṇā //
1.47.d:
चिन्तयेत्तन्मयो योगी समाधायात्ममानसम् ।
तावद्यावद् दृढीभूता तत्रैव नृप धारणा ॥
1.47.m: Absorbed in Him, the yogin should concentrate his mind and meditate, / so long, O king, until fixation [of the mind] upon that very [form] becomes firm.

1.47.s:
vadatastiṣṭato yadvā svecchayā karma kurvataḥ /
nāpayāti yadā cittātsiddhāṃ manyeta tāṃ tadā //
1.47.d:
वदतस्तिष्टतो यद्वा स्वेच्छया कर्म कुर्वतः ।
नापयाति यदा चित्तात्सिद्धां मन्येत तां तदा ॥
1.47.m: When it does not depart from the mind while speaking, standing, / or doing actions at will, then he may consider it attained.

1.47.s:
tataḥ śaṅkhagadācakraśārṅgādi rahitaṃ budhaḥ /
cintaye dbhagavadrūpaṃ praśāntaṃ sākṣasūtrakam //
1.47.d:
ततः शङ्खगदाचक्रशार्ङ्गादि रहितं बुधः ।
चिन्तये द्भगवद्रूपं प्रशान्तं साक्षसूत्रकम् ॥
1.47.m: Then the wise man should meditate on the Lord's peaceful form, / holding a rosary, devoid of the conch, mace, discus, bow, and other attributes.

1.47.s:
sā yadā dhāraṇā tadvadavasthānavatī tataḥ /
kirīṭakeyūramukhairbhūṣaṇai rahitaṃ smaret //
1.47.d:
सा यदा धारणा तद्वदवस्थानवती ततः ।
किरीटकेयूरमुखैर्भूषणै रहितं स्मरेत् ॥
1.47.m: When that fixation is likewise firmly established, / then he should remember Him as devoid of ornaments such as diadem, armlets, and the like.

1.47.s:
tadekāvayavaṃ caivaṃ cetasā hi punarbudhaḥ /
kuryāttato 'vayavini prāṇidhānaparo bhavet //
1.47.d:
तदेकावयवं चैवं चेतसा हि पुनर्बुधः ।
कुर्यात्ततो ऽवयविनि प्राणिधानपरो भवेत् ॥
1.47.m: Then the wise man should indeed place his mind upon a single limb of that [form]; / thereafter, he should become intent upon the one possessing limbs.

1.47.s:
tadrūpapratyaye caikasaṃnatiścānyaniḥspṛhā /
taddhyānaṃ prathamairaṅgaiḥ ṣaṅbhirniṣpādyate nṛpa //
1.47.d:
तद्रूपप्रत्यये चैकसंनतिश्चान्यनिःस्पृहा ।
तद्ध्यानं प्रथमैरङ्गैः षङ्भिर्निष्पाद्यते नृप ॥
1.47.m: The continuous flow [of thought] upon the idea of that form alone, without desire for anything else, / is meditation; it is accomplished through the first six limbs, O king.

1.47.s:
tasyaivaṃ kalpanāhīnaṃ svarūpagrahaṇaṃ hi yat /
manasā dhyānaniṣpādyaṃ samādhiḥ so 'bhidhīyate //
1.47.d:
तस्यैवं कल्पनाहीनं स्वरूपग्रहणं हि यत् ।
मनसा ध्याननिष्पाद्यं समाधिः सो ऽभिधीयते ॥
1.47.m: Indeed, that apprehension of the essential nature itself, devoid of mental construction / and brought about by meditation through the mind, is called samādhi.

1.47.s:
vijñānaṃ prāpakaṃ prāpye paraṃ brahmaṇi pārthiva /
prāpaṇīyastathaivātmā prakṣīṇāśeṣabhāvanaḥ //
1.47.d:
विज्ञानं प्रापकं प्राप्ये परं ब्रह्मणि पार्थिव ।
प्रापणीयस्तथैवात्मा प्रक्षीणाशेषभावनः ॥
1.47.m: Wisdom is the means of reaching the goal—the supreme Brahman, O king; / and the self, with all mental constructions destroyed, is that which is to be reached.

1.47.s:
kṣetrajñakaraṇījñānaṃ karaṇaṃ tena tasya tat /
niṣpādya muktikāryaṃ vai kṛtakṛtyo nivartate //
1.47.d:
क्षेत्रज्ञकरणीज्ञानं करणं तेन तस्य तत् ।
निष्पाद्य मुक्तिकार्यं वै कृतकृत्यो निवर्तते ॥
1.47.m: The knowledge to be performed by the knower of the field is the instrument for him; / having thereby accomplished the work of liberation, having done what was to be done, it ceases.

1.47.s:
tadbhāvabhāvanāpannastato 'sau paramātmanaḥ /
bhavatyabhedī bhedaśca tasyājñānakṛto bhavet //
1.47.d:
तद्भावभावनापन्नस्ततो ऽसौ परमात्मनः ।
भवत्यभेदी भेदश्च तस्याज्ञानकृतो भवेत् ॥
1.47.m: Attaining the state of being identical with Him, he then / becomes non-different from the Supreme Self; and difference is created by ignorance.

1.47.s:
vibhedajanake jñāne nāśa mātyantikaṃ gate /
ātmano brahmaṇābhedaṃ saṃmataṃ kaḥ kariṣyati //
1.47.d:
विभेदजनके ज्ञाने नाश मात्यन्तिकं गते ।
आत्मनो ब्रह्मणाभेदं संमतं कः करिष्यति ॥
1.47.m: When the knowledge that causes differentiation has met with absolute destruction, / who will make a differentiation between the Self and Brahman that is acknowledged [as real]?

1.47.s:
ityuktaste mayā yogaḥ khāṇḍikya paripṛcchataḥ /
saṃkṣepavistarābhyāṃ tu kimanyatkriyatāṃ tava //
1.47.d:
इत्युक्तस्ते मया योगः खाण्डिक्य परिपृच्छतः ।
संक्षेपविस्तराभ्यां तु किमन्यत्क्रियतां तव ॥
1.47.m: "Thus has yoga been explained to you by me, O Khāṇḍikya, as you asked, / in brief and in detail. What else, then, may be done for you?"

1.47.s:
khāṇḍikya uvāca
kathito yogasadbhāvaḥ sarvameva kṛtaṃ mama /
tavopadeśātsakalo naṣṭaścittamalo mama //
1.47.d:
खाण्डिक्य उवाच
कथितो योगसद्भावः सर्वमेव कृतं मम ।
तवोपदेशात्सकलो नष्टश्चित्तमलो मम ॥
1.47.m: Khāṇḍikya said: / "The true nature of yoga has been declared, everything has indeed been accomplished for me; / through your teaching, all the impurity of my mind has been destroyed.

1.47.s:
mameti yanmayā proktamasadetanna cānyathā /
naredraṃ gadituṃ śakyamapi vijñeyavedabhiḥ //
1.47.d:
ममेति यन्मया प्रोक्तमसदेतन्न चान्यथा ।
नरेद्रं गदितुं शक्यमपि विज्ञेयवेदभिः ॥
1.47.m: What was spoken of by me as 'mine' is unreal, not otherwise; / it cannot be expressed to a king even by those who know what is to be known.

1.47.s:
ahaṃ mametyavidyeyaṃ vyavahārastathānayoḥ /
paramārthastva saṃlāpyo vacasāṃ gocaro na yaḥ //
1.47.d:
अहं ममेत्यविद्येयं व्यवहारस्तथानयोः ।
परमार्थस्त्व संलाप्यो वचसां गोचरो न यः ॥
1.47.m: 'I' and 'mine'—this is ignorance, and worldly conduct consists of these two. / The supreme truth, however, is beyond conversation, not within the range of words.

1.47.s:
tadguccha śreyase sarvaṃ mamaitadbhavatā kṛtam /
yadvimuktiparo yogaḥ proktaḥ keśidvajāvyayaḥ //
1.47.d:
तद्गुच्छ श्रेयसे सर्वं ममैतद्भवता कृतम् ।
यद्विमुक्तिपरो योगः प्रोक्तः केशिद्वजाव्ययः ॥
1.47.m: Therefore go unto welfare; all this has been done by you for me, / since imperishable yoga oriented toward liberation has been spoken, O Keśidhvaja."

1.47.s:
sanandana uvāca
yathārhapūjayā tena khāṇḍikyena sa pūjitaḥ /
ājagāma puraṃ brahmaṃstataḥ keśidhvajo nṛpaḥ //
1.47.d:
सनन्दन उवाच
यथार्हपूजया तेन खाण्डिक्येन स पूजितः ।
आजगाम पुरं ब्रह्मंस्ततः केशिध्वजो नृपः ॥
1.47.m: Sanandana said: / Honored by that Khāṇḍikya with worship befitting him, / King Keśidhvaja then returned to his city, O brāhmaṇa.

1.47.s:
khāṇḍikyo 'pi sutaṃ kṛtvā rājānaṃ yogasiddhaye /
viśālāmagamatkṛṣṇe samāveśitamānasaḥ //
1.47.d:
खाण्डिक्यो ऽपि सुतं कृत्वा राजानं योगसिद्धये ।
विशालामगमत्कृष्णे समावेशितमानसः ॥
1.47.m: Khāṇḍikya too, having made his son king for the attainment of yoga, / went to Viśālā, his mind firmly fixed on Kṛṣṇa.

1.47.s:
sa tatraikāntiko bhūtvā yamādiguṇasaṃyutaḥ /
viṣṇvākhye nirmale brahmaṇyavāpa nṛpatirlayam //
1.47.d:
स तत्रैकान्तिको भूत्वा यमादिगुणसंयुतः ।
विष्ण्वाख्ये निर्मले ब्रह्मण्यवाप नृपतिर्लयम् ॥
1.47.m: Becoming single-minded there, endowed with virtues such as yama, / the king attained absorption into the pure Brahman called Viṣṇu.

1.47.s:
keśidhvajo 'pi muktayarthaṃ svakarmakṣapaṇonmukhaḥ /
bubhuje viṣayānkarma cakre cānabhisaṃdhitam //
1.47.d:
केशिध्वजो ऽपि मुक्तयर्थं स्वकर्मक्षपणोन्मुखः ।
बुभुजे विषयान्कर्म चक्रे चानभिसंधितम् ॥
1.47.m: Keśidhvaja too, eager to exhaust his karma for the sake of liberation, / enjoyed sense-objects and performed action without selfish motive.

1.47.s:
sa kalyāṇopabhogaiśca kṣīṇapāpo 'malastataḥ /
avāpa siddhimatyantatritāpakṣapaṇīṃ mune //
1.47.d:
स कल्याणोपभोगैश्च क्षीणपापो ऽमलस्ततः ।
अवाप सिद्धिमत्यन्तत्रितापक्षपणीं मुने ॥
1.47.m: And with sins diminished through auspicious experiences, pure thereafter, / he attained the perfection that utterly destroys the threefold suffering, O sage.

1.47.s:
etatte kathitaṃ sarvaṃ yanmāṃ tvaṃ paripṛṣṭavān /
tāpatrayacikitsārthaṃ kimanyatkathayāmi te //
iti śrūbṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge dvitīyapāde saptacatvāriṃśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.47.d:
एतत्ते कथितं सर्वं यन्मां त्वं परिपृष्टवान् ।
तापत्रयचिकित्सार्थं किमन्यत्कथयामि ते ॥
इति श्रूबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे द्वितीयपादे सप्तचत्वारिंशत्तमो ऽध्यायः
1.47.m:
All this has been told to you that you asked me about / for the cure of the threefold suffering; what else shall I tell you?

Thus ends the forty-seventh chapter in the second quarter of the Pūrvabhāga of the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.48.s:
nārada uvāca
śrutaṃ mayā mahāmāga tāpatrayacikitsitam /
tathāpi me mano bhrāntaṃ na sthitiṃ labhateṃ'jasā //
1.48.d:
नारद उवाच
श्रुतं मया महामाग तापत्रयचिकित्सितम् ।
तथापि मे मनो भ्रान्तं न स्थितिं लभतेंऽजसा ॥
1.48.m: Nārada said: / "I have heard the cure for the threefold suffering, O highly fortunate one; / nonetheless, my wandering mind does not readily attain stability.

1.48.s:
ātmavyatikramaṃ brahmandurjanācaritaṃ katham /
soḍhuṃ śakyeta manujaistanmamākhyāhi mānada //
1.48.d:
आत्मव्यतिक्रमं ब्रह्मन्दुर्जनाचरितं कथम् ।
सोढुं शक्येत मनुजैस्तन्ममाख्याहि मानद ॥
1.48.m: How can the violation of one's own self committed by wicked people / be endured by human beings? Tell me that, O giver of honor."

1.48.s:
sūta uvāca
tacchrṛtvā nāradenoktaṃ brahmaputraḥ sanandanaḥ /
uvāca harṣasaṃyuktaḥ smaranbhagharataceṣṭitam //
1.48.d:
सूत उवाच
तच्छ्रृत्वा नारदेनोक्तं ब्रह्मपुत्रः सनन्दनः ।
उवाच हर्षसंयुक्तः स्मरन्भघरतचेष्टितम् ॥
1.48.m: Sūta said: / Having heard that spoken by Nārada, Sanandana, son of Brahmā, / filled with joy, said, remembering the deeds of Bharata:

1.48.s:
sanandana uvāca
atra te kathayiṣyāmi itihāsaṃ purātanam /
yaṃ śrutvā tvanmano bhrāntamāsthānaṃ labhate bhūśam //
1.48.d:
सनन्दन उवाच
अत्र ते कथयिष्यामि इतिहासं पुरातनम् ।
यं श्रुत्वा त्वन्मनो भ्रान्तमास्थानं लभते भूशम् ॥
1.48.m: Sanandana said: / "Here I shall narrate to you an ancient story, / hearing which your wandering mind will greatly attain stability.

1.48.s:
āsītpurā muniśreṣṭha bharato nāma bhūpatiḥ /
ārṣabho yasya nāmnedaṃ bhārataṃ khaṇḍamucyate //
1.48.d:
आसीत्पुरा मुनिश्रेष्ठ भरतो नाम भूपतिः ।
आर्षभो यस्य नाम्नेदं भारतं खण्डमुच्यते ॥
1.48.m: Formerly there was a king named Bharata, O best of sages, / the son of Ṛṣabha, by whose name this land is called Bhārata.

1.48.s:
sa rājā prāptarājyastu pitṛpaitāmahaṃ kramāt /
pālayāmāsa dharmeṇa pitṛbadrañjayan prajāḥ //
1.48.d:
स राजा प्राप्तराज्यस्तु पितृपैतामहं क्रमात् ।
पालयामास धर्मेण पितृबद्रञ्जयन् प्रजाः ॥
1.48.m: Having obtained the kingdom inherited from his father and grandfather in due succession, / that king protected the subjects with righteousness, gladdening them like a father.

1.48.s:
rddaje ca vividhairyajñairbhagavantamadhokṣajam /
sarvadevātmakaṃ dhyāyannānākarmasu tanmatiḥ //
1.48.d:
र्द्दजे च विविधैर्यज्ञैर्भगवन्तमधोक्षजम् ।
सर्वदेवात्मकं ध्यायन्नानाकर्मसु तन्मतिः ॥
1.48.m: He worshiped the Lord, Adhokṣaja, with various sacrifices, / meditating on him as the self of all deities, his mind intent on various rites.

1.48.s:
tataḥ samutpādya sutānvirakto viṣayeṣu saḥ /
muktvā rājyaṃ yayau vidvānpulastyapuhāśramam //
1.48.d:
ततः समुत्पाद्य सुतान्विरक्तो विषयेषु सः ।
मुक्त्वा राज्यं ययौ विद्वान्पुलस्त्यपुहाश्रमम् ॥
1.48.m: Then, having fathered sons, detached from sense-objects, / giving up the kingdom, the wise king went to the hermitage of Pulastya and Pulaha,

1.48.s:
śālagrāmaṃ mahākṣetraṃ mumukṣujanasevitam /
tatrāsau tāpaso tāpaso bhūtvā viṣṇorārādhanaṃ mune //
1.48.d:
शालग्रामं महाक्षेत्रं मुमुक्षुजनसेवितम् ।
तत्रासौ तापसो तापसो भूत्वा विष्णोराराधनं मुने ॥
1.48.m: to the great sacred field Śālagrāma, frequented by seekers of liberation. / Becoming an ascetic there, O sage, he performed the worship of Viṣṇu

1.48.s:
cakāra bhaktibhāvena yathālabdhasaparyayā /
nityaṃ prātaḥ samāplutya nirmale 'bhali nārada //
1.48.d:
चकार भक्तिभावेन यथालब्धसपर्यया ।
नित्यं प्रातः समाप्लुत्य निर्मले ऽभलि नारद ॥
1.48.m: with devotion, through offerings procured as available. / Constantly bathing in the morning in the pure water, O Nārada,

1.48.s:
upatiṣṭedraviṃ bhaktyā gṛṇanbrahmākṣaraṃ param /
athāśrame samāgatya vāsudevaṃ jagatpatim //
1.48.d:
उपतिष्टेद्रविं भक्त्या गृणन्ब्रह्माक्षरं परम् ।
अथाश्रमे समागत्य वासुदेवं जगत्पतिम् ॥
1.48.m: he would worship the sun with devotion, chanting the supreme imperishable Brahman. / Then, returning to the hermitage, [he worshiped] Vāsudeva, the Lord of the universe,

1.48.s:
samāhṛtaiḥ svayaṃ dravyaiḥ samitkuśamṛdādibhiḥ /
phalaiḥ puṣpaiṃstathā patraistulasyāḥ svacchavāribhiḥ //
1.48.d:
समाहृतैः स्वयं द्रव्यैः समित्कुशमृदादिभिः ।
फलैः पुष्पैंस्तथा पत्रैस्तुलस्याः स्वच्छवारिभिः ॥
1.48.m: with materials gathered by himself: sacrificial sticks, kuśa grass, earth, and so forth, / with fruits, flowers, and leaves of tulasī, and with clear water,

1.48.s:
pūjayanprayato bhūtvā bhaktiprasarasaṃplutaḥ /
sacaikadā mahābhāgaḥ snātvā prātaḥ samāhitaḥ //
1.48.d:
पूजयन्प्रयतो भूत्वा भक्तिप्रसरसंप्लुतः ।
सचैकदा महाभागः स्नात्वा प्रातः समाहितः ॥
1.48.m: worshiping with self-restraint, flooded by an outflow of devotion. / And once that illustrious king, having bathed in the morning, composed in mind,

1.48.s:
cakranadyāṃ japaṃstasthau muhurtatrayamaṃbuni /
athājagāma tattīraṃ jalaṃ pātuṃ pipāsitā //
1.48.d:
चक्रनद्यां जपंस्तस्थौ मुहुर्तत्रयमंबुनि ।
अथाजगाम तत्तीरं जलं पातुं पिपासिता ॥
1.48.m: stood in the water of the Cakranadī for three muhūrtas, reciting prayers. / Then a thirsty doe came to that riverbank to drink water,

1.48.s:
āsannapsavā brahmannaikaiva hiṇī vanāt /
tataḥ samabhavattatra pītaprāye jale tayā //
1.48.d:
आसन्नप्सवा ब्रह्मन्नैकैव हिणी वनात् ।
ततः समभवत्तत्र पीतप्राये जले तया ॥
1.48.m: about to give birth, O brāhmaṇa, all alone from the forest. / Then, when the water was almost drunk by her there,

1.48.s:
siṃhasya nādaḥ sumahān sarvaprāṇibhayaṅkaraḥ /
tataḥ sā siṃhasannādādutplutā nimnagātaṭam //
1.48.d:
सिंहस्य नादः सुमहान् सर्वप्राणिभयङ्करः ।
ततः सा सिंहसन्नादादुत्प्लुता निम्नगातटम् ॥
1.48.m: there arose a very great roar of a lion, terrifying to all living beings. / Then she, springing up from the roar of the lion toward the riverbank,

1.48.s:
atyuñcārohaṇenāsyā nadyāṃ garbhaḥ papāta ha /
tamuhyamānaṃ vegena vīcimālāpariplutam //
1.48.d:
अत्युञ्चारोहणेनास्या नद्यां गर्भः पपात ह ।
तमुह्यमानं वेगेन वीचिमालापरिप्लुतम् ॥
1.48.m: due to leaping extremely high, her fetus fell into the river. / Carried away by the current, tossed by a series of waves,

1.48.s:
jagrāha bharato garbhātpatitaṃ mṛgapotakam /
garbhapracyutiduḥkhena prottuṅgākraṇena ca //
1.48.d:
जग्राह भरतो गर्भात्पतितं मृगपोतकम् ।
गर्भप्रच्युतिदुःखेन प्रोत्तुङ्गाक्रणेन च ॥
1.48.m: Bharata caught the fawn that had fallen from the womb. / From the pain of miscarriage and from the high leap,

1.48.s:
munīndra sā tu hariṇī nipapāta mamāra ca /
hariṇīṃ tāṃ vilokyātha vipannāṃ nṛpatāpasaḥ //
1.48.d:
मुनीन्द्र सा तु हरिणी निपपात ममार च ।
हरिणीं तां विलोक्याथ विपन्नां नृपतापसः ॥
1.48.m: that doe fell down and died, O lord of sages. / Then, seeing that doe dead, the royal ascetic,

1.48.s:
mṛgapotaṃ samāgṛhya svamāśramamupāgataḥ /
cakārānudinaṃ cāsau mṛgapotasya vai nṛpaḥ //
1.48.d:
मृगपोतं समागृह्य स्वमाश्रममुपागतः ।
चकारानुदिनं चासौ मृगपोतस्य वै नृपः ॥
1.48.m: taking the young fawn, returned to his hermitage. / And day after day, that king indeed took care of

1.48.s:
poṣaṇaṃ puṣyamāṇaśca sa tena vavṛdhe mune /
cacārāśramaparyantaṃ tṛṇāni gahaneṣu saḥ //
1.48.d:
पोषणं पुष्यमाणश्च स तेन ववृधे मुने ।
चचाराश्रमपर्यन्तं तृणानि गहनेषु सः ॥
1.48.m: the fawn's nourishment, and nourished by him, it grew, O sage. / It grazed on the grasses in the thickets around the hermitage;

1.48.s:
dūraṃ gatvā ca śārdūlatrāsādabhyāyayau punaḥ /
prātargatvādidūraṃ ca sāyamāyātyathāśramam //
1.48.d:
दूरं गत्वा च शार्दूलत्रासादभ्याययौ पुनः ।
प्रातर्गत्वादिदूरं च सायमायात्यथाश्रमम् ॥
1.48.m: having gone far, it returned again out of fear of a tiger; / going far in the morning, it came back to the hermitage in the evening.

1.48.s:
punaśca bharatasyābhūdāśramasyoṭajāntare /
tasyatasminmṛge dūrasamīpaparivartini //
1.48.d:
पुनश्च भरतस्याभूदाश्रमस्योटजान्तरे ।
तस्यतस्मिन्मृगे दूरसमीपपरिवर्तिनि ॥
1.48.m: And again it remained within the hut of Bharata's hermitage. / While that deer wandered far and near,

1.48.s:
āsīñcetaḥ samāsaktaṃ na tathā hyacyute mune /
vimuktarājyatanayaḥ projjhitāśeṣabāndhavaḥ //
1.48.d:
आसीञ्चेतः समासक्तं न तथा ह्यच्युते मुने ।
विमुक्तराज्यतनयः प्रोज्झिताशेषबान्धवः ॥
1.48.m: his mind became attached to it, but not so toward Acyuta, O sage. / Though he had abandoned his kingdom and sons, and cast aside all relatives,

1.48.s:
mamatva sa cakāroñcaistasminhariṇapotake /
kiṃ vṛkaibhakṣito vyāghnaiḥ kiṃ siṃhena nipātitaḥ //
1.48.d:
ममत्व स चकारोञ्चैस्तस्मिन्हरिणपोतके ।
किं वृकैभक्षितो व्याघ्नैः किं सिंहेन निपातितः ॥
1.48.m: he felt intense possessiveness toward that young fawn. / 'Has it been eaten by wolves, by tigers, or struck down by a lion?'

1.48.s:
cirāyamāṇe niṣkānte tasyāsīditi mānasam /
prītiprasannavadanaḥ pārśvasthe cābhavanmṛge //
1.48.d:
चिरायमाणे निष्कान्ते तस्यासीदिति मानसम् ।
प्रीतिप्रसन्नवदनः पार्श्वस्थे चाभवन्मृगे ॥
1.48.m: Such was his thought when it was late in returning after wandering out; / and his face became bright with affection when the deer was at his side.

1.48.s:
samādhibhaṅgastasyāsīnmamatvākṛṣṭamānasaḥ /
kālena gacchatā so 'tha kālaṃ cakre mahīpatiḥ //
1.48.d:
समाधिभङ्गस्तस्यासीन्ममत्वाकृष्टमानसः ।
कालेन गच्छता सो ऽथ कालं चक्रे महीपतिः ॥
1.48.m: There was an interruption of his samādhi, his mind drawn away by possessiveness. / With the passing of time, the king met his death.

1.48.s:
piteva sāstraṃ putreṇa mṛgapotena vīkṣitaḥ /
mṛgameva tadādrākṣīttyajanprāṇānasāvapi //
1.48.d:
पितेव सास्त्रं पुत्रेण मृगपोतेन वीक्षितः ।
मृगमेव तदाद्राक्षीत्त्यजन्प्राणानसावपि ॥
1.48.m: Looked upon by the young deer like a father by a son with tears, / he too looked only upon that deer as he gave up his life-breaths.

1.48.s:
mṛgo babhūva sa mune tādṛśīṃ bhāvanāṃ gataḥ /
jāti smaratvādudvignaḥ saṃsārasya dvijottama //
1.48.d:
मृगो बभूव स मुने तादृशीं भावनां गतः ।
जाति स्मरत्वादुद्विग्नः संसारस्य द्विजोत्तम ॥
1.48.m: He became a deer, O sage, having reached such a state of consciousness. / Distressed by the cycle of rebirth because he remembered his previous birth, O best of brāhmaṇas,

1.48.s:
vihāya mātaraṃ bhūyaḥ śālagrāmamupāyayau /
śuṣkaistṛṇaistathā parṇaiḥ sa kurvannātmapoṣaṇam //
1.48.d:
विहाय मातरं भूयः शालग्राममुपाययौ ।
शुष्कैस्तृणैस्तथा पर्णैः स कुर्वन्नात्मपोषणम् ॥
1.48.m: leaving his mother, he went again to Śālagrāma. / Sustaining himself with dry grass and leaves,

1.48.s:
mṛgatvahetubhūtasya karmaṇo niṣkṛtiṃ yayau /
tatra cotsṛṣṭadeho 'sau jajñe jātismaro dvijaḥ //
1.48.d:
मृगत्वहेतुभूतस्य कर्मणो निष्कृतिं ययौ ।
तत्र चोत्सृष्टदेहो ऽसौ जज्ञे जातिस्मरो द्विजः ॥
1.48.m: he attained expiation of the karma that had caused his state as a deer. / Leaving his body there, he was born as a brāhmaṇa remembering his previous lives,

1.48.s:
sadācāravatāṃ śuddhe yāgināṃ pravare kule /
sarvavijñāna saṃpannaḥ sarvaśāstrārthatattvavit //
1.48.d:
सदाचारवतां शुद्धे यागिनां प्रवरे कुले ।
सर्वविज्ञान संपन्नः सर्वशास्त्रार्थतत्त्ववित् ॥
1.48.m: in a pure, noble family of sacrificers endowed with good conduct, / endowed with all knowledge, knowing the essential truth of all scriptures.

1.48.s:
apaśyatsa muniśreṣṭhaḥ svātmānaṃ prakṛteḥ param /
ātmanodhigatajñānāddvevādīni mahāmune //
1.48.d:
अपश्यत्स मुनिश्रेष्ठः स्वात्मानं प्रकृतेः परम् ।
आत्मनोधिगतज्ञानाद्द्वेवादीनि महामुने ॥
1.48.m: That best of sages saw his own Self as beyond Prakṛti. / Through the knowledge realized by the Self, O great sage,

1.48.s:
sarvabhūtānyabhe dena dadarśa sa mahāmatiḥ /
na papāṭha guruproktaṃ kṛtopanayanaḥ śrutam //
1.48.d:
सर्वभूतान्यभे देन ददर्श स महामतिः ।
न पपाठ गुरुप्रोक्तं कृतोपनयनः श्रुतम् ॥
1.48.m: that noble-minded one beheld all beings, beginning with the gods, without difference. / Having had the upanayana performed, he did not recite what was taught by the guru from scripture;

1.48.s:
na dadarśa ca karmāṇi śāstrāṇi jagṛhe na ca /
ukto 'pi bahuśaḥ kiñcijjaṇḍa vākyamabhāṣata //
1.48.d:
न ददर्श च कर्माणि शास्त्राणि जगृहे न च ।
उक्तो ऽपि बहुशः किञ्चिज्जण्ड वाक्यमभाषत ॥
1.48.m: he did not perform rituals, nor did he study the scriptures; / and even though addressed many times, he spoke only a few dull words.

1.48.s:
tadapyasaṃskāraguṇaṃ grāmabhāṣoktisaṃyutam /
apaddhastavapuḥ so 'pi malināṃbaradhṛṅ mune //
1.48.d:
तदप्यसंस्कारगुणं ग्रामभाषोक्तिसंयुतम् ।
अपद्धस्तवपुः सो ऽपि मलिनांबरधृङ् मुने ॥
1.48.m: Even so, lacking refinements, speaking the vulgar dialect, / with distorted body, he wore filthy garments, O sage;

1.48.s:
klinnadantāntaraḥ sarvaiḥ paribhūtaḥ sa nāgaraiḥ /
saṃmānena parāṃ hāniṃ yogarddheḥ kurute yataḥ //
1.48.d:
क्लिन्नदन्तान्तरः सर्वैः परिभूतः स नागरैः ।
संमानेन परां हानिं योगर्द्धेः कुरुते यतः ॥
1.48.m: with dirt between his teeth, he was despised by all the townsfolk; / for honor causes the greatest ruin to the prosperity of yoga.

1.48.s:
janenāvamato yogī yogasiddhiṃ ca vindati /
tasmāñcareta vai yogī satāṃ dharmamadūṣayan //
1.48.d:
जनेनावमतो योगी योगसिद्धिं च विन्दति ।
तस्माञ्चरेत वै योगी सतां धर्ममदूषयन् ॥
1.48.m: Disdained by the people, the yogin attains perfection in yoga; / therefore the yogin should wander without corrupting the dharma of the virtuous,

1.48.s:
janā yathāvamanyeyurgaccheyurnaiva saṃgatim /
hiraṇyagarbhavacanaṃ vicintyetthaṃ mahāmatiḥ //
1.48.d:
जना यथावमन्येयुर्गच्छेयुर्नैव संगतिम् ।
हिरण्यगर्भवचनं विचिन्त्येत्थं महामतिः ॥
1.48.m: so that people might despise him and never associate with him. / Reflecting thus on the words of Hiraṇyagarbha, the great-minded one

1.48.s:
ātmānaṃ darśayāmāsa jaḍonmattākṛtiṃ jane /
bhuṅkte kulmāṣavaṭakān śākaṃ tranyaphalaṃ kaṇān //
1.48.d:
आत्मानं दर्शयामास जडोन्मत्ताकृतिं जने ।
भुङ्क्ते कुल्माषवटकान् शाकं त्रन्यफलं कणान् ॥
1.48.m: showed himself to the people in the form of a dull-witted madman. / He ate boiled pulse cakes, vegetables, wild fruits, and grains;

1.48.s:
yadyadāpnoti sa bahūnatti vai kālasaṃbhavam /
pitaryuparate so 'tha bhrātṛbhrātṛvyabāndhavaiḥ //
1.48.d:
यद्यदाप्नोति स बहूनत्ति वै कालसंभवम् ।
पितर्युपरते सो ऽथ भ्रातृभ्रातृव्यबान्धवैः ॥
1.48.m: whatever abundant [food] came in season, he indeed consumed. / Then, when his father passed away, he was made by his brothers, nephews, and kinsmen

1.48.s:
kāritaḥ kṣetrakarmādi kadannāhārapoṣitaḥ /
sarūkṣapīnāvayavo jaḍakārī ca karmaṇi //
1.48.d:
कारितः क्षेत्रकर्मादि कदन्नाहारपोषितः ।
सरूक्षपीनावयवो जडकारी च कर्मणि ॥
1.48.m: to do farm-work and the like, nourished on coarse food. / With rough, stout limbs, he acted like an idiot in [every] task.

1.48.s:
sarvalokopakaraṇaṃ babhūvāhāravetanaḥ /
taṃ tādṛśamasaṃskāraṃ viprākṛtiviceṣṭitam //
1.48.d:
सर्वलोकोपकरणं बभूवाहारवेतनः ।
तं तादृशमसंस्कारं विप्राकृतिविचेष्टितम् ॥
1.48.m: He became the servant of all people, receiving food as his wage. / Seeing him thus devoid of refinements, acting contrary to the nature of a brāhmaṇa,

1.48.s:
kṣattā sauvīrarājyasya viṣṭiyogyamamanyata /
sa rājā śibikārūḍho gantuṃ kṛtamatirdvija //
1.48.d:
क्षत्ता सौवीरराज्यस्य विष्टियोग्यममन्यत ।
स राजा शिबिकारूढो गन्तुं कृतमतिर्द्विज ॥
1.48.m: the chamberlain of the Sauvīra king considered him fit for forced labor. / That king, mounted on a palanquin, resolved to go, O twice-born,

1.48.s:
babhūvekṣumatītīre kapilarṣervarāśramam /
śreyaḥ kimatra saṃsāre duḥkhaprāye nṛṇāmiti //
1.48.d:
बभूवेक्षुमतीतीरे कपिलर्षेर्वराश्रमम् ।
श्रेयः किमत्र संसारे दुःखप्राये नृणामिति ॥
1.48.m: to the excellent hermitage of the sage Kapila on the bank of the Ikṣumatī, / thinking: 'What is the highest good for men in this worldly existence, which is mostly suffering?'

1.48.s:
praṣṭuṃ taṃ mokṣadharmajñaṃ kapilākhyaṃ mahāmunim /
uvāha śibikāmasya kṣatturvacanacoditaḥ //
1.48.d:
प्रष्टुं तं मोक्षधर्मज्ञं कपिलाख्यं महामुनिम् ।
उवाह शिबिकामस्य क्षत्तुर्वचनचोदितः ॥
1.48.m: In order to question that great sage named Kapila, who knew the path to liberation, / he was carried in a palanquin; and urged by the chamberlain's command,

1.48.s:
nṛṇāṃ viṣṭigṛhītānāmanyeṣāṃ so 'pi madhyagaḥ /
gṛhīto viṣṭinā vipra sarvajñānaikabhājanam //
1.48.d:
नृणां विष्टिगृहीतानामन्येषां सो ऽपि मध्यगः ।
गृहीतो विष्टिना विप्र सर्वज्ञानैकभाजनम् ॥
1.48.m: he too went in the midst of other men seized for forced labor. / Seized for forced labor, O twice-born, though the sole receptacle of all knowledge,

1.48.s:
jātismaro 'sau pāpasya kṣayakāma uvāha tām /
yayau jaḍagatistatra yugamātrāvalokanam //
1.48.d:
जातिस्मरो ऽसौ पापस्य क्षयकाम उवाह ताम् ।
ययौ जडगतिस्तत्र युगमात्रावलोकनम् ॥
1.48.m: remembering his past births and desiring the destruction of sin, he carried it. / He walked with the slow gait of an idiot, looking ahead only the distance of a yoke.

1.48.s:
kurvanmatimatāṃ śreṣṭhaste tvanye tvaritaṃ yayuḥ /
vilokya nṛpatiḥ so 'tha viṣamaṃ śibikāgatam //
1.48.d:
कुर्वन्मतिमतां श्रेष्ठस्ते त्वन्ये त्वरितं ययुः ।
विलोक्य नृपतिः सो ऽथ विषमं शिबिकागतम् ॥
1.48.m: While he, best among the wise, moved thus, the others walked swiftly. / Then the king, noticing that the palanquin was moving unevenly,

1.48.s:
kimetadityāha samaṃ gamyatāṃ śibikāvahāḥ /
punastathaiva śibikāṃ vilokya viṣamāṃ hasan //
1.48.d:
किमेतदित्याह समं गम्यतां शिबिकावहाः ।
पुनस्तथैव शिबिकां विलोक्य विषमां हसन् ॥
1.48.m: said: 'What is this? Walk evenly, palanquin-bearers!' / Again seeing the palanquin moving unevenly, smiling,

1.48.s:
nṛpaḥ kime 'tadityāha bhavadbhirgamyate 'nyathā /
bhūpatervadatastasya śrutvetthaṃ bahuśo vacaḥ /
śibikāvāhakāḥ procurayaṃ yātītyasatvaram //
1.48.d:
नृपः किमे ऽतदित्याह भवद्भिर्गम्यते ऽन्यथा ।
भूपतेर्वदतस्तस्य श्रुत्वेत्थं बहुशो वचः ।
शिबिकावाहकाः प्रोचुरयं यातीत्यसत्वरम् ॥
1.48.m: the king said: 'What is this? You are walking improperly!' / Hearing this utterance spoken repeatedly by the lord of the earth, / the palanquin-bearers said: 'This one is walking slowly.'

1.48.s:
rājovāca
kiṃ śrānto 'syalpamadhvānaṃ tvayoḍhā śibikā mama /
kimāyāsasaho na tvaṃ pīvā nāsi nirīkṣyase //
1.48.d:
राजोवाच
किं श्रान्तो ऽस्यल्पमध्वानं त्वयोढा शिबिका मम ।
किमायाससहो न त्वं पीवा नासि निरीक्ष्यसे ॥
1.48.m: The king said: / 'Are you fatigued? My palanquin has been carried by you for only a short distance. / Can you not bear exertion? Are you not robust? You are seen [to be so].'

1.48.s:
brāhmaṇa uvāca
nāhaṃ pīvā na caivoḍhā śibikā bhavato mayā /
na śrānto 'smi na cāyāso voḍhānyo 'sti mahīpate //
1.48.d:
ब्राह्मण उवाच
नाहं पीवा न चैवोढा शिबिका भवतो मया ।
न श्रान्तो ऽस्मि न चायासो वोढान्यो ऽस्ति महीपते ॥
1.48.m: The brāhmaṇa said: / 'I am not robust, nor has your palanquin been carried by me; / I am not fatigued, nor is there exertion. There is another bearer, O ruler of the earth.'

1.48.s:
rājovāca
pratyakṣaṃ dṛśyate pīvātvadyāpi śibikā tvayi /
śramaśca bhāro dvahane bhavatyeva hi dehinām //
1.48.d:
राजोवाच
प्रत्यक्षं दृश्यते पीवात्वद्यापि शिबिका त्वयि ।
श्रमश्च भारो द्वहने भवत्येव हि देहिनाम् ॥
1.48.m: The king said: / 'Directly visible is your stoutness, and the palanquin is upon you even now; / and fatigue certainly arises for embodied beings from carrying a burden.'

1.48.s:
brāhmaṇa uvāca
pratyakṣaṃ bhavatā bhūpa yaddṛṣṭaṃ mama tadvada /
balavānabalaśceti vācyaṃ paścādviśeṣaṇam //
1.48.d:
ब्राह्मण उवाच
प्रत्यक्षं भवता भूप यद्दृष्टं मम तद्वद ।
बलवानबलश्चेति वाच्यं पश्चाद्विशेषणम् ॥
1.48.m: The brāhmaṇa said: / 'Tell me what was directly seen by you, O king, regarding me. / The qualification "strong" or "weak" is to be spoken only afterwards.

1.48.s:
tvayoḍhā śibikā ceti tvayyadyāpi ca saṃsthitā /
mithyā tadapyatra bhavān śṛṇotu vacanaṃ mama //
1.48.d:
त्वयोढा शिबिका चेति त्वय्यद्यापि च संस्थिता ।
मिथ्या तदप्यत्र भवान् शृणोतु वचनं मम ॥
1.48.m: "The palanquin was carried by you, and even now it rests upon you"— / that too is false; listen to my word in this matter.

1.48.s:
bhūmau pādayugaṃ cātha jaṅghe pādadvaye sthite /
ūru jaṅghādvayāvasthau tadādhāraṃ tathodaram //
1.48.d:
भूमौ पादयुगं चाथ जङ्घे पादद्वये स्थिते ।
ऊरु जङ्घाद्वयावस्थौ तदाधारं तथोदरम् ॥
1.48.m: The two feet rest on the earth, and the shanks are situated upon the two feet; / the thighs rest on the two shanks, and the belly is supported by them.

1.48.s:
vakṣasthalaṃ tathā bāhū skandhau codarasaṃsthitau /
skandhāśritayeṃ śibikā mamādhāro 'tra kiṅkṛtaḥ //
1.48.d:
वक्षस्थलं तथा बाहू स्कन्धौ चोदरसंस्थितौ ।
स्कन्धाश्रितयें शिबिका ममाधारो ऽत्र किङ्कृतः ॥
1.48.m: Likewise the chest, arms, and shoulders are situated upon the belly; / this palanquin is resting upon the shoulders. How is it made into my burden?

1.48.s:
śibikāyāṃ sthitaṃ cedaṃ dehaṃ tvadupalakṣitam /
tatra tvamahamapyatretyucyate cedamanyathā //
1.48.d:
शिबिकायां स्थितं चेदं देहं त्वदुपलक्षितम् ।
तत्र त्वमहमप्यत्रेत्युच्यते चेदमन्यथा ॥
1.48.m: And this body, designated as "you", rests upon the palanquin. / That "you are there" and "I am here" is said improperly.

1.48.s:
ahaṃ tvaṃ ca tathānye ca bhūtairuhyāśca pārthiva /
guṇapravāhapatito bhūtavargo 'pi yātyayam //
1.48.d:
अहं त्वं च तथान्ये च भूतैरुह्याश्च पार्थिव ।
गुणप्रवाहपतितो भूतवर्गो ऽपि यात्ययम् ॥
1.48.m: I, you, and others are carried by the material elements, O king; / and this collection of elements, fallen into the stream of the guṇas, moves along.

1.48.s:
karmavaśyā guṇaścaite sattvādyāḥ pṛthivīpate /
avidyāsaṃcitaṃ karmataścāśeṣeṣu jantuṣu //
1.48.d:
कर्मवश्या गुणश्चैते सत्त्वाद्याः पृथिवीपते ।
अविद्यासंचितं कर्मतश्चाशेषेषु जन्तुषु ॥
1.48.m: And these guṇas, sattva and the rest, are subject to karma, O protector of the earth; / and karma, accumulated by ignorance, exists in all living beings.

1.48.s:
ātmā śuddho 'kṣaraḥ śānto nirguṇaḥ prakṛte paraḥ /
pravṛddhyapacayau na sta ekasyākhilajantuṣu //
1.48.d:
आत्मा शुद्धो ऽक्षरः शान्तो निर्गुणः प्रकृते परः ।
प्रवृद्ध्यपचयौ न स्त एकस्याखिलजन्तुषु ॥
1.48.m: The self is pure, imperishable, tranquil, devoid of qualities, beyond primordial nature; / there is no growth or decay for the One residing in all living beings.

1.48.s:
yadā nopacayastasya nacaivāpacayo nṛpa /
tadāpi bāliśo 'si tvaṃ kayā yuktyā tvayeritam //
1.48.d:
यदा नोपचयस्तस्य नचैवापचयो नृप ।
तदापि बालिशो ऽसि त्वं कया युक्त्या त्वयेरितम् ॥
1.48.m: When there is no growth for it, and no decay either, O king, / even then [you ask]: "Are you robust?" By what reasoning was that spoken by you?

1.48.s:
/
bhūpādajaṅghākaṭyūrujaṭharādiṣu saṃsthitā /
śibikeyaṃ yadā skandhe tadā bhāraḥ samastvayā //
1.48.d:
।
भूपादजङ्घाकट्यूरुजठरादिषु संस्थिता ।
शिबिकेयं यदा स्कन्धे तदा भारः समस्त्वया ॥
1.48.m: When this palanquin, resting upon the feet, shanks, hips, thighs, belly, and so forth [of the body] / which is upon the earth, is upon the shoulder, then the burden is the same for you

1.48.s:
tathānyajantubhirbhūpa śibikoḍhāna kevalam /
śailadrumagṛhottho 'pi pṛthivīsaṃbhavo 'pi ca //
1.48.d:
तथान्यजन्तुभिर्भूप शिबिकोढान केवलम् ।
शैलद्रुमगृहोत्थो ऽपि पृथिवीसंभवो ऽपि च ॥
1.48.m: as well as for other living beings, O king. Not only the palanquin is carried, / but also whatever arises from mountains, trees, and houses, or whatever originates from the earth.

1.48.s:
yathā puṃsaḥ pṛthagbhāvaḥ prākṛtaiḥ karaṇairnṛpa /
soḍhavyaḥ sumahānbhāraḥ katamo nṛpa te mayā //
1.48.d:
यथा पुंसः पृथग्भावः प्राकृतैः करणैर्नृप ।
सोढव्यः सुमहान्भारः कतमो नृप ते मया ॥
1.48.m: Since the self is distinct from the material instruments, O king, / what exceedingly great burden of yours is to be borne by me, O king?

1.48.s:
yaddravyo śibikā ceyaṃ taddravyo bhūtasaṃgrahaḥ /
bhavato me 'khilasyāsya samatvenopabṛṃhitaḥ //
1.48.d:
यद्द्रव्यो शिबिका चेयं तद्द्रव्यो भूतसंग्रहः ।
भवतो मे ऽखिलस्यास्य समत्वेनोपबृंहितः ॥
1.48.m: The substance of which this palanquin is made is the same substance as the collection of elements / of you and of me and of all this [world], magnified through sameness.'

1.48.s:
sanandana uvāca
evamuktvābhavaṃnmaunī sa vahañśibikāṃ dvijaḥ /
so 'pi rājāvatīryorvyāṃ tatpādau jagṛhe tvaran //
1.48.d:
सनन्दन उवाच
एवमुक्त्वाभवंन्मौनी स वहञ्शिबिकां द्विजः ।
सो ऽपि राजावतीर्योर्व्यां तत्पादौ जगृहे त्वरन् ॥
1.48.m: Sanandana said: / Having spoken thus, the twice-born remained silent as he carried the palanquin. / That king too, having quickly descended to the ground, clasped his feet.

1.48.s:
rājovāca
bho bho visṛjya śibikāṃ prasādaṃ kuru me dvija /
kathyatāṃ ko bhavānatra jālmarupadharaḥ sthitaḥ //
1.48.d:
राजोवाच
भो भो विसृज्य शिबिकां प्रसादं कुरु मे द्विज ।
कथ्यतां को भवानत्र जाल्मरुपधरः स्थितः ॥
1.48.m: The king said: / 'O sir, setting down the palanquin, grant me your favor, O twice-born! / Tell me, who are you who stand here in the guise of a fool?

1.48.s:
yo bhavānyadapatyaṃ vā yadāgamanakāraṇam /
tatsarvaṃ kathyatāṃ vidvanmahyaṃ śuśrūṣave tvayā //
1.48.d:
यो भवान्यदपत्यं वा यदागमनकारणम् ।
तत्सर्वं कथ्यतां विद्वन्मह्यं शुश्रूषवे त्वया ॥
1.48.m: Who you are, whose son, or what the reason for your coming is— / let all that be told by you, O wise one, to me who wish to listen!'

1.48.s:
brāhmaṇa uvāca
śrūyatāṃ ko 'hamityetadvaktuṃ bhūpa na śakyate /
upayoganimittaṃ ca sarvatrāgamanakriyā //
1.48.d:
ब्राह्मण उवाच
श्रूयतां को ऽहमित्येतद्वक्तुं भूप न शक्यते ।
उपयोगनिमित्तं च सर्वत्रागमनक्रिया ॥
1.48.m: The brāhmaṇa said: / 'Listen: to state "who I am" is not possible, O king; / and the action of coming everywhere is for the sake of functional purpose.'

1.48.s:
sukhaduḥkhopabhogau tu tau dehādyupapādakau /
dharmādharmodbhavau bhoktuṃ janturdehādimṛcchati //
1.48.d:
सुखदुःखोपभोगौ तु तौ देहाद्युपपादकौ ।
धर्माधर्मोद्भवौ भोक्तुं जन्तुर्देहादिमृच्छति ॥
1.48.m: The experience of pleasure and pain produces the body and the rest; / born of merit and demerit, a creature obtains a body and other [instruments] in order to experience them.

1.48.s:
sarvasyaiva hi bhūpāla jantoḥ sarvatra kāraṇam /
dharmādharmauṃ yatastasmātkāraṇaṃ pṛcchyate kutaḥ //
1.48.d:
सर्वस्यैव हि भूपाल जन्तोः सर्वत्र कारणम् ।
धर्माधर्मौं यतस्तस्मात्कारणं पृच्छ्यते कुतः ॥
1.48.m: For in every creature, O king, merit and demerit / are indeed the cause everywhere; therefore, why is a cause asked about?

1.48.s:
rājovāca
dharmādharmauṃ na saṃdehaḥ sarvakāryeṣu kāraṇam /
upabhoganimittaṃ ca dehāddehāntarāgamaḥ //
1.48.d:
राजोवाच
धर्माधर्मौं न संदेहः सर्वकार्येषु कारणम् ।
उपभोगनिमित्तं च देहाद्देहान्तरागमः ॥
1.48.m:
The king said:
Merit and demerit, without doubt, are the cause in all effects, / and the passage from one body to another body is for the sake of experience.

1.48.s:
yattvetadbhavatā proktaṃ ko 'hamityetadātmanaḥ /
vaktuṃ na śakyate śrotuṃ tanmameccā pravartate //
1.48.d:
यत्त्वेतद्भवता प्रोक्तं को ऽहमित्येतदात्मनः ।
वक्तुं न शक्यते श्रोतुं तन्ममेच्चा प्रवर्तते ॥
1.48.m: However, as to what you said, that one cannot say of the self / “Who am I?”, my desire arises to hear about that.

1.48.s:
yo 'sti yo 'hamiti brahmankathaṃ vaktuṃ na śakyate /
ātmanyeva na doṣāya śabdo 'hamiti yo dvijā //
1.48.d:
यो ऽस्ति यो ऽहमिति ब्रह्मन्कथं वक्तुं न शक्यते ।
आत्मन्येव न दोषाय शब्दो ऽहमिति यो द्विजा ॥
1.48.m: How can it not be possible to say who one is, [stating] “I am [so-and-so]”, O Brahmin? / The word “I” with reference to the self itself cannot be faulty, O twice-born!

1.48.s:
brāhmaṇa uvāca
śabdo 'hamiti doṣāya nātmanyevaṃ tathaiva tat /
anātmanyātmavijñānaṃ śabdo vā śrutilakṣaṇaḥ //
1.48.d:
ब्राह्मण उवाच
शब्दो ऽहमिति दोषाय नात्मन्येवं तथैव तत् ।
अनात्मन्यात्मविज्ञानं शब्दो वा श्रुतिलक्षणः ॥
1.48.m:
The Brahmin said:
The word “I” is indeed not faulty with reference to the self, that is so; / [it is faulty when there is] the notion of self in what is not the self, or [when] a word has the character of [mere] sounds.

1.48.s:
jihvā bravītyahamiti dantauṣṭatāluka nṛpa /
etenāhaṃ yataḥ sarve vāṅniṣpādanahetavaḥ //
1.48.d:
जिह्वा ब्रवीत्यहमिति दन्तौष्टतालुक नृप ।
एतेनाहं यतः सर्वे वाङ्निष्पादनहेतवः ॥
1.48.m: The tongue says “I”, [as do] the teeth, the lips, and the palate, O king; / [yet can one say] “I am these”, since all of them are merely causes for producing speech?

1.48.s:
kiṃ hetubhirvadūtyeṣā vāgevāhamiti svayam /
tathāpi vāgahamedvaktumitthaṃ na yujyate //
1.48.d:
किं हेतुभिर्वदूत्येषा वागेवाहमिति स्वयम् ।
तथापि वागहमेद्वक्तुमित्थं न युज्यते ॥
1.48.m: Does speech itself say “I am” through these causes? / Even so, it is not fitting to say in this manner: “I am speech.”

1.48.s:
piṇḍaḥ pṛthagyataḥ puṃsaḥ śiraḥpāṇyādilakṣaṇaḥ /
tato 'hamiti kutraināṃ saṃjñāṃ rājankaromyaham //
1.48.d:
पिण्डः पृथग्यतः पुंसः शिरःपाण्यादिलक्षणः ।
ततो ऽहमिति कुत्रैनां संज्ञां राजन्करोम्यहम् ॥
1.48.m: Since the physical body, characterized by the head, hands, and other [limbs], is separate from the person, / where, then, O king, do I apply this designation “I”?

1.48.s:
yadyanyo 'sti paraḥ ko 'pi mattaḥ pārthivasattam /
na deho 'hamayaṃ cānye vaktumevamapīṣyate //
1.48.d:
यद्यन्यो ऽस्ति परः को ऽपि मत्तः पार्थिवसत्तम् ।
न देहो ऽहमयं चान्ये वक्तुमेवमपीष्यते ॥
1.48.m: If there is any other supreme [entity] different from me, O best of kings, / then one may wish to say: “I am not this body, and they are others.”

1.48.s:
yadā samastadeheṣu pumāneko vyavasthitaḥ /
tadadā hi ko bhavānko 'hamityetadviphalaṃ vacaḥ //
1.48.d:
यदा समस्तदेहेषु पुमानेको व्यवस्थितः ।
तददा हि को भवान्को ऽहमित्येतद्विफलं वचः ॥
1.48.m: en: When one single person resides in all bodies, / then indeed words like "Who are you?" or "Who am I?" are meaningless.

1.48.s:
tvaṃ rājā śibikā ceyaṃ vayaṃ vāhāḥ puraḥ sarāḥ /
ayaṃ ca bhavato loko na sadetannṛpocyate //
1.48.d:
त्वं राजा शिबिका चेयं वयं वाहाः पुरः सराः ।
अयं च भवतो लोको न सदेतन्नृपोच्यते ॥
1.48.m: en: "You are the king, this is the palanquin, we are the bearers walking ahead, / and this is your folk"—king, this is not said of what is real.

1.48.s:
vṛkṣāddāru tataśceyaṃ śibikā tvadadhiṣṭitā /
kva vṛkṣasaṃjñā vai tasyā dārusaṃjñāthavā nṛpa //
1.48.d:
वृक्षाद्दारु ततश्चेयं शिबिका त्वदधिष्टिता ।
क्व वृक्षसंज्ञा वै तस्या दारुसंज्ञाथवा नृप ॥
1.48.m: en: From a tree comes wood, and from that comes this palanquin upon which you sit; / where indeed is the designation "tree" for it, or the designation "wood", O king?

1.48.s:
vṛkṣārūḍho mahārājo nāyaṃ vadati te janaḥ /
na ca dāruṇi sarvastvāṃ bravīti śibikāgatam //
1.48.d:
वृक्षारूढो महाराजो नायं वदति ते जनः ।
न च दारुणि सर्वस्त्वां ब्रवीति शिबिकागतम् ॥
1.48.m: en: This folk of yours does not say, "The great king is mounted on a tree"; / nor does anyone say of you, seated in the palanquin, "He is on wood."

1.48.s:
śibikādārusaṃghāto svanāmasthitisaṃsthitaḥ /
anviṣyatāṃ nṛpaśreṣṭhānandadāśibikā tvayā //
1.48.d:
शिबिकादारुसंघातो स्वनामस्थितिसंस्थितः ।
अन्विष्यतां नृपश्रेष्ठानन्ददाशिबिका त्वया ॥
1.48.m: en: The palanquin is an aggregate of pieces of wood, abiding under the status of its own name; / let the palanquin be sought by you, O best of kings, [which is] a giver of bliss.

1.48.s:
evaṃ chatraṃ śalākābhyaḥ pṛthagbhāvo vimṛśyatām /
kva jātaṃ chatramityeṣa nyāyastvayi tathā mayi //
1.48.d:
एवं छत्रं शलाकाभ्यः पृथग्भावो विमृश्यताम् ।
क्व जातं छत्रमित्येष न्यायस्त्वयि तथा मयि ॥
1.48.m: en: In this way, let the parasol be considered distinct from its ribs: / where has the parasol arisen? This reasoning applies to you and likewise to me.

1.48.s:
pumānstrī gaurajā bājī kuñjaro vihagastaruḥ /
deheṣu lokasaṃjñeyaṃ vijñeyā karmahetuṣu //
1.48.d:
पुमान्स्त्री गौरजा बाजी कुञ्जरो विहगस्तरुः ।
देहेषु लोकसंज्ञेयं विज्ञेया कर्महेतुषु ॥
1.48.m: en: Man, woman, cow, goat, horse, elephant, bird, tree— / this worldly designation is to be understood regarding bodies caused by past karma.

1.48.s:
pumānna devo na naro na paśurna ca pādapaḥ /
śarīrākṛtibhedāstu bhūpaite karmayonayaḥ //
1.48.d:
पुमान्न देवो न नरो न पशुर्न च पादपः ।
शरीराकृतिभेदास्तु भूपैते कर्मयोनयः ॥
1.48.m: en: The person is neither a god nor a man, nor a beast, nor a tree; / these bodily forms, O king, are born of karma.

1.48.s:
vastu rājeti yalleke yañca rājabhaṭātmakam /
tathānyaśca nṛpetthaṃ tanna satyaṃ kalpanāmayam //
1.48.d:
वस्तु राजेति यल्लेके यञ्च राजभटात्मकम् ।
तथान्यश्च नृपेत्थं तन्न सत्यं कल्पनामयम् ॥
1.48.m: en: That entity which is in the world as "king", and that which consists of royal soldiers, / and likewise another, O king: in this manner, that is not real; it is made of imagination.

1.48.s:
yastu kālāntareṇāpi nāśasaṃjñāmupaiti vai /
pariṇāmādisaṃbhūtaṃ tadvastu nṛpa tañca kim //
1.48.d:
यस्तु कालान्तरेणापि नाशसंज्ञामुपैति वै ।
परिणामादिसंभूतं तद्वस्तु नृप तञ्च किम् ॥
1.48.m: en: But that which, even in the course of time, attains the designation of destruction, / arisen from transformation and the like—what entity is that, O king?

1.48.s:
tvaṃ rājā sarvasokasya pituḥ putro ripo ripuḥ /
patnyāḥ patiḥ pitā sūnoḥ kastvaṃ bhūpa vadāmyaham //
1.48.d:
त्वं राजा सर्वसोकस्य पितुः पुत्रो रिपो रिपुः ।
पत्न्याः पतिः पिता सूनोः कस्त्वं भूप वदाम्यहम् ॥
1.48.m: en: You are the king of all the world, the son of a father, the enemy of an enemy, / the husband of a wife, the father of a son: which of these are you, O king? Tell [me].

1.48.s:
tvaṃ kimetacciraḥ kiṃ tu śirastava tatho daram /
kimu pādādikaṃ tvetannaiva kiṃ te mahīpate //
1.48.d:
त्वं किमेतच्चिरः किं तु शिरस्तव तथो दरम् ।
किमु पादादिकं त्वेतन्नैव किं ते महीपते ॥
1.48.m: en: Are you this head? Or is the head yours, and likewise the belly? / Or are the feet and so forth you, or are they not yours, O lord of the earth?

1.48.s:
samastāvayavebhyastvaṃ pṛthagbhūto vyavasthitaḥ /
ko 'hamityatra nipuṇaṃ bhūtvā cintaya pārthiva //
1.48.d:
समस्तावयवेभ्यस्त्वं पृथग्भूतो व्यवस्थितः ।
को ऽहमित्यत्र निपुणं भूत्वा चिन्तय पार्थिव ॥
1.48.m: en: You exist standing apart from all the limbs; / having become discerning, reflect on this, O ruler: "Who am I?"

1.48.s:
evaṃ vyavasthite tattve mayāhamiti bhāvitum /
pṛthakūcaraṇaniṣpādyaṃ śakyaṃ tu nṛpate katham //
iti śṛbṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne dvi.pā.ṣṭacatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.48.d:
एवं व्यवस्थिते तत्त्वे मयाहमिति भावितुम् ।
पृथकूचरणनिष्पाद्यं शक्यं तु नृपते कथम् ॥
इति शृबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने द्वि।पा।ष्टचत्वारिंशो ऽध्यायः
1.48.m:
en: When the truth is established thus, how can it be possible, O king, / for me to imagine "I", which is brought about by separate limbs?

en: Thus ends the forty-eighth chapter in the Second Part of the Great Narrative in the Pūrvabhāga of the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.49.s:
sanandana uvāca
niśamya tasyeti vacaḥ paramārthasamanvitam /
praśrayāvanato bhūtvā tamāha nṛpatirdvijam //
1.49.d:
सनन्दन उवाच
निशम्य तस्येति वचः परमार्थसमन्वितम् ।
प्रश्रयावनतो भूत्वा तमाह नृपतिर्द्विजम् ॥
1.49.m: en: Sanandana said: / Having heard his words endowed with ultimate truth, / the king, bowing down with humility, said to that twice-born:

1.49.s:
rājovāca
bhagavanyattvayā prokta paramārthamayaṃ vacaḥ /
śrute tasminbhramantīva manaso mama vṛttayaḥ //
1.49.d:
राजोवाच
भगवन्यत्त्वया प्रोक्त परमार्थमयं वचः ।
श्रुते तस्मिन्भ्रमन्तीव मनसो मम वृत्तयः ॥
1.49.m: en: The king said: / Holy one, as for this word full of ultimate truth that you have spoken, / when it was heard, the movements of my mind seem to wander.

1.49.s:
etadvivekavijñānaṃ yadi śeṣeṣu jantuṣu /
bhavatā darśitaṃ vipra tatparaṃ prakṛtermahat //
1.49.d:
एतद्विवेकविज्ञानं यदि शेषेषु जन्तुषु ।
भवता दर्शितं विप्र तत्परं प्रकृतेर्महत् ॥
1.49.m: en: If this discriminative knowledge regarding all remaining creatures / has been shown by you, O twice-born, it is beyond Prakṛti, supreme.

1.49.s:
nāhaṃ vahāmi śibikāṃ śibikā mayi na sthitā /
śarīramanyadasmatto yeneyaṃ śibikā dhṛtā //
1.49.d:
नाहं वहामि शिबिकां शिबिका मयि न स्थिता ।
शरीरमन्यदस्मत्तो येनेयं शिबिका धृता ॥
1.49.m: en: "I do not carry the palanquin; the palanquin does not rest on me; / the body by which this palanquin is borne is different from us;

1.49.s:
guṇa pravṛttirbhūtānāṃ pravṛttiḥ karmacoditā /
pravartante guṇāścaite kiṃ mameti tvayoditam //
1.49.d:
गुण प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां प्रवृत्तिः कर्मचोदिता ।
प्रवर्तन्ते गुणाश्चैते किं ममेति त्वयोदितम् ॥
1.49.m: en: the activity of beings is the activity of the guṇas impelled by karma, / and these guṇas are active—what is it to me?"—so you have said.

1.49.s:
etasminparamārthajña mama śrotrapathaṃ gate /
mano vihvalatāmeti paramārthārthatāṃ gatam //
1.49.d:
एतस्मिन्परमार्थज्ञ मम श्रोत्रपथं गते ।
मनो विह्वलतामेति परमार्थार्थतां गतम् ॥
1.49.m: en: When this has entered the path of my hearing, O knower of the ultimate truth, / my mind, seeking the purpose of the ultimate truth, becomes bewildered.

1.49.s:
pūrvameva mahābhāga kapilarṣimahaṃ dvija /
praṣṭumabhyudyato gatvā śreyaḥ kintvatra saṃśaye //
1.49.d:
पूर्वमेव महाभाग कपिलर्षिमहं द्विज ।
प्रष्टुमभ्युद्यतो गत्वा श्रेयः किन्त्वत्र संशये ॥
1.49.m: en: Previously indeed, O fortunate one, I set out, having gone to the sage Kapila, / to ask, O twice-born, what is the ultimate good; but here I am in doubt.

1.49.s:
tadantare ca bhavatā yadidaṃ vākyamīritam /
tenaiva paramārthārthaṃ tvayi cetaḥ pradhāvati //
1.49.d:
तदन्तरे च भवता यदिदं वाक्यमीरितम् ।
तेनैव परमार्थार्थं त्वयि चेतः प्रधावति ॥
1.49.m: en: And meanwhile, this speech has been uttered by you; / by that very [speech], my mind runs towards you for the sake of the ultimate truth.

1.49.s:
kapilarṣirbhagavataḥ sarvabhūtasya vai kila /
viṣṇoraṃśo jaganmohanāśāya samupāgataḥ //
1.49.d:
कपिलर्षिर्भगवतः सर्वभूतस्य वै किल ।
विष्णोरंशो जगन्मोहनाशाय समुपागतः ॥
1.49.m: en: The sage Kapila, surely, is a portion of the blessed Viṣṇu, who is all beings, / come to destroy the delusion of the world.

1.49.s:
sa eva bhagavānnūnamasmākaṃ hitakāmyayā /
pratyakṣatāmanugatastathaitadbhavatocyate //
1.49.d:
स एव भगवान्नूनमस्माकं हितकाम्यया ।
प्रत्यक्षतामनुगतस्तथैतद्भवतोच्यते ॥
1.49.m: en: That very Blessed One, indeed, wishing our welfare, / has come into view, and thus it is spoken by you.

1.49.s:
tanmahyaṃ mohanāśāya yacchreyaḥ paramaṃ dvija /
tadvadākhila vijñānajalavīcyujadhirbhavān //
1.49.d:
तन्मह्यं मोहनाशाय यच्छ्रेयः परमं द्विज ।
तद्वदाखिल विज्ञानजलवीच्युजधिर्भवान् ॥
1.49.m: en: Therefore, for the destruction of my delusion, O twice-born, tell me what is the highest good; / you are an ocean of the waters and waves of all knowledge.

1.49.s:
brāhmaṇa uvāca
bhūyaḥ pṛcchasi kiṃ śreyaḥ paramārthena pṛcchasi /
śreyāṃsi paramārthāni hyaśeṣāṇyena bhūpate //
1.49.d:
ब्राह्मण उवाच
भूयः पृच्छसि किं श्रेयः परमार्थेन पृच्छसि ।
श्रेयांसि परमार्थानि ह्यशेषाण्येन भूपते ॥
1.49.m: en: The brāhmaṇa said: / Again you ask: "What is the highest good?" Do you ask from the viewpoint of ultimate truth? / For all goods are ultimate truths, O king.

1.49.s:
devatārādhanaṃ kṛtvā dhanasaṃpadamicchati /
putrānicchati rājyaṃ ca śreyastasyaiva tannṛpa //
1.49.d:
देवताराधनं कृत्वा धनसंपदमिच्छति ।
पुत्रानिच्छति राज्यं च श्रेयस्तस्यैव तन्नृप ॥
1.49.m: en: Having performed the worship of deities, one desires wealth and abundance, / one desires sons and kingship; that indeed is the good for him, O king.

1.49.s:
vivakinastu saṃyogaḥ śreyo 'sau paramātmanā /
karmayajñādikaṃ śreyaḥ svarlokapaladāyi yat //
1.49.d:
विवकिनस्तु संयोगः श्रेयो ऽसौ परमात्मना ।
कर्मयज्ञादिकं श्रेयः स्वर्लोकपलदायि यत् ॥
1.49.m: en: But for the discerning, union with the Supreme Self is the good; / the rites of sacrifice and the like, which bestow the fruit of heaven, are [also] a good.

1.49.s:
śreyaḥ pradhānaṃ ca phale tadevānabhisaṃhite /
ātmā dhyeyaḥ sadā bhūpa yogayuktaistathā paraiḥ //
1.49.d:
श्रेयः प्रधानं च फले तदेवानभिसंहिते ।
आत्मा ध्येयः सदा भूप योगयुक्तैस्तथा परैः ॥
1.49.m: en: And that very [action] is the foremost good when its fruit is not aimed at; / the Self is always to be meditated upon by those joined in yoga, O king, as well as by others.

1.49.s:
śreya stasyaiva saṃyogaḥ śreyo yaḥ paramātmanaḥ /
śreyāṃsyevamanekāni śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ //
1.49.d:
श्रेय स्तस्यैव संयोगः श्रेयो यः परमात्मनः ।
श्रेयांस्येवमनेकानि शतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः ॥
1.49.m: en: His good is union with that very Supreme Self; / thus there are many goods, by hundreds and by thousands.

1.49.s:
saṃtyatra paramārthāstu na tvete śrūyatāṃ ca me /
dharmo 'yaṃ tyajate kiṃ tu paramārtho dhanaṃ yadi //
1.49.d:
संत्यत्र परमार्थास्तु न त्वेते श्रूयतां च मे ।
धर्मो ऽयं त्यजते किं तु परमार्थो धनं यदि ॥
1.49.m: en: But these are not the ultimate truth here; listen to me: / if wealth is the ultimate truth, why is this dharma abandoned?

1.49.s:
vyayaścakriyata kasmātkāmaprāptyupalakṣaṇaḥ /
mutraścetparamārthākhyaḥ so 'pyanyasya nareśvara //
1.49.d:
व्ययश्चक्रियत कस्मात्कामप्राप्त्युपलक्षणः ।
मुत्रश्चेत्परमार्थाख्यः सो ऽप्यन्यस्य नरेश्वर ॥
1.49.m: en: And why is expenditure incurred, characterized by the attainment of desire? / If a son is called the ultimate truth, he too [belongs] to another, O ruler of men.

1.49.s:
paramārthabhūtaḥ so 'nyasya paramārtho hi naḥ pitā /
evaṃ na paramārtho 'sti jagatyatra carācare //
1.49.d:
परमार्थभूतः सो ऽन्यस्य परमार्थो हि नः पिता ।
एवं न परमार्थो ऽस्ति जगत्यत्र चराचरे ॥
1.49.m: en: He is an ultimate truth to another; indeed, our father is an ultimate truth [to us]; / thus there is no ultimate truth in this moving and unmoving world.

1.49.s:
paramārtho hi kāryāṇi karaṇānāmaśeṣataḥ /
rājyādiprāptiratroktā paramārthatayā yadi //
1.49.d:
परमार्थो हि कार्याणि करणानामशेषतः ।
राज्यादिप्राप्तिरत्रोक्ता परमार्थतया यदि ॥
1.49.m: en: For the ultimate truth [would be] the actions of the sense organs without remainder; / if the attainment of kingship and the like here is spoken of as the ultimate truth,

1.49.s:
paramārthā bhavantyatra na bhavanti ca vai tataḥ /
ṛgyajuḥsāmaniṣpādyaṃ yajñakarma mataṃ tava //
1.49.d:
परमार्था भवन्त्यत्र न भवन्ति च वै ततः ।
ऋग्यजुःसामनिष्पाद्यं यज्ञकर्म मतं तव ॥
1.49.m: en: then ultimate truths exist and do not exist here on that account. / Sacrificial rite accomplished by the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāma [Vedas] is held by you

1.49.s:
paramārthabhūtaṃ tatrāpi śrūyatāṃ gadato mama /
yattu niṣpādyate kāryaṃ mṛdā kāraṇabhūtayā //
1.49.d:
परमार्थभूतं तत्रापि श्रूयतां गदतो मम ।
यत्तु निष्पाद्यते कार्यं मृदा कारणभूतया ॥
1.49.m: en: to be the ultimate truth; hear from me speaking on that too: / that effect which is produced by clay as the material cause,

1.49.s:
tatkāraṇānugamanājjāyate nṛpa mṛnmayam /
evaṃ vināśibhirdravyaiḥ samidājyakuśādibhiḥ //
1.49.d:
तत्कारणानुगमनाज्जायते नृप मृन्मयम् ।
एवं विनाशिभिर्द्रव्यैः समिदाज्यकुशादिभिः ॥
1.49.m: en: that, by following its cause, O king, becomes made of clay; / so too, by perishable substances such as fuel, ghee, and kuśa grass,

1.49.s:
niṣpādyate kriyā yā tu sā bhavitrī vināśinī /
anāśī paramārthastu prājñairabhyupagamyate //
1.49.d:
निष्पाद्यते क्रिया या तु सा भवित्री विनाशिनी ।
अनाशी परमार्थस्तु प्राज्ञैरभ्युपगम्यते ॥
1.49.m: en: that rite which is performed is bound to be perishable; / but the imperishable is accepted as the ultimate truth by the wise.

1.49.s:
yattuṃ nāśi na saṃdeho nāśidravyopapāditam /
tadevāpaladaṃ karma paramārtho mato mama //
1.49.d:
यत्तुं नाशि न संदेहो नाशिद्रव्योपपादितम् ।
तदेवापलदं कर्म परमार्थो मतो मम ॥
1.49.m: en: What is produced by perishable substances is perishable—there is no doubt; / that very action which is without [desire for] fruit is held by me to be the ultimate truth.

1.49.s:
muktisādhanabhūtatvātparamārtho na sādhanam /
dhyānamevātmano bhūpaparamārthārthaśabditam //
1.49.d:
मुक्तिसाधनभूतत्वात्परमार्थो न साधनम् ।
ध्यानमेवात्मनो भूपपरमार्थार्थशब्दितम् ॥
1.49.m: en: Because it is a means to liberation, the ultimate truth is not a [mere] means; / meditation on the Self alone, O king, is designated as the ultimate truth.

1.49.s:
bhedakāri parebhyastu paramārtho na bhedavān /
paramārthātmanoryogaḥ paramārtha itīṣyate //
1.49.d:
भेदकारि परेभ्यस्तु परमार्थो न भेदवान् ।
परमार्थात्मनोर्योगः परमार्थ इतीष्यते ॥
1.49.m: en: But what creates division [belongs] to other things; the ultimate truth is without division; / the union of the ultimate truth and the Self is acknowledged as the ultimate truth.

1.49.s:
mithyaitadanyaddravyaṃ hi naitaddravyamayaṃ yataḥ /
tasmācchreyāṃsyaśeṣāṇi nṛpaitāni na saṃśayaḥ //
1.49.d:
मिथ्यैतदन्यद्द्रव्यं हि नैतद्द्रव्यमयं यतः ।
तस्माच्छ्रेयांस्यशेषाणि नृपैतानि न संशयः ॥
1.49.m: en: For this other substance is false, because it does not consist of [that real] substance; / therefore all these are goods, O king, there is no doubt.

1.49.s:
paramārthastu bhūpāla saṃkṣepācchrūyatāṃ mama /
eko vyāpī samaḥ śuddho nirguṇa prakṛteḥ paraḥ //
1.49.d:
परमार्थस्तु भूपाल संक्षेपाच्छ्रूयतां मम ।
एको व्यापी समः शुद्धो निर्गुण प्रकृतेः परः ॥
1.49.m: en: But hear the ultimate truth briefly from me, O king: / one, all-pervading, equal, pure, free from the guṇas, beyond Prakṛti,

1.49.s:
janmavṛddhyādirahita ātmā sarvagato nṛpa /
parijñānamayo sadbhirnāmajātyādibhivibhuḥ //
1.49.d:
जन्मवृद्ध्यादिरहित आत्मा सर्वगतो नृप ।
परिज्ञानमयो सद्भिर्नामजात्यादिभिविभुः ॥
1.49.m: en: devoid of birth, growth, and the like, the Self is all-pervading, O king, / consisting of full consciousness, [perceived] by the wise, all-pervasive through names, species, and the like.

1.49.s:
na yogavānna yukto 'bhūnnaiva pārthivaḥ yokṣyati /
tasyātmaparadeheṣu sato 'pyekamayaṃ hi tat //
1.49.d:
न योगवान्न युक्तो ऽभून्नैव पार्थिवः योक्ष्यति ।
तस्यात्मपरदेहेषु सतो ऽप्येकमयं हि तत् ॥
1.49.m: en: It has no contact, nor was it united, nor will it be united, O king; / though existing in one's own and others' bodies, it is indeed of one nature.

1.49.s:
vijñānaṃ paramārtho 'sau vetti no 'tathyadarśanaḥ /
veṇuraṅghravibhedena bhedaḥ ṣaṅjādisaṃjñitaḥ //
1.49.d:
विज्ञानं परमार्थो ऽसौ वेत्ति नो ऽतथ्यदर्शनः ।
वेणुरङ्घ्रविभेदेन भेदः षङ्जादिसंज्ञितः ॥
1.49.m: en: That consciousness is the ultimate truth; one who perceives untruth does not know it. / By the difference of holes in a flute, there is a difference known as the notes ṣaḍja and the rest;

1.49.s:
abhedo vyāpino vāyostathā tasya mahātmanaḥ /
ekatvaṃ rūpabhedaśca vāhyakarmapravṛttijaḥ //
1.49.d:
अभेदो व्यापिनो वायोस्तथा तस्य महात्मनः ।
एकत्वं रूपभेदश्च वाह्यकर्मप्रवृत्तिजः ॥
1.49.m: en: there is no difference in the all-pervading air; likewise is it for that Great Self: / unity [is its nature], and diversity of form arises from the operation of external karma.

1.49.s:
devādibhedamadhyāste nāstyevācaraṇo hi saḥ /
śṛṇvatra bhūpa prāgvṛttaṃ yadgītamṛbhuṇā bhavet //
1.49.d:
देवादिभेदमध्यास्ते नास्त्येवाचरणो हि सः ।
शृण्वत्र भूप प्राग्वृत्तं यद्गीतमृभुणा भवेत् ॥
1.49.m: He who resides within differences such as gods and the rest is indeed without bodily action. / Hear regarding this, O king, an ancient event that was sung by Ṛbhu,

1.49.s:
avabodhaṃ janayato nidādhasya dvijanmanaḥ /
ṛbhurnāmābavatputro brahmaṇaḥ parameṣṭinaḥ //
1.49.d:
अवबोधं जनयतो निदाधस्य द्विजन्मनः ।
ऋभुर्नामाबवत्पुत्रो ब्रह्मणः परमेष्टिनः ॥
1.49.m: imparting awakening to the twice-born Nidāgha. / There was a son of the supreme lord Brahmā named Ṛbhu,

1.49.s:
vijñāta tattvasadbhāvo nisargādeva bhūpate /
tasya śiṣyo nidāgho 'bhūtpulastyatanayaḥ purā //
1.49.d:
विज्ञात तत्त्वसद्भावो निसर्गादेव भूपते ।
तस्य शिष्यो निदाघो ऽभूत्पुलस्त्यतनयः पुरा ॥
1.49.m: who had understood the reality of truth by his very nature, O ruler of the earth. / Formerly, his disciple was Nidāgha, the son of Pulastya.

1.49.s:
prādādaśeṣavijñānaṃ sa tasmai parayā mudā /
avāptajñāna tattvasya na tasyādvaitavāsanā //
1.49.d:
प्रादादशेषविज्ञानं स तस्मै परया मुदा ।
अवाप्तज्ञान तत्त्वस्य न तस्याद्वैतवासना ॥
1.49.m: With great joy, he gave him complete knowledge; / yet though he had attained knowledge of truth, he lacked the latent impression of non-duality.

1.49.s:
sa ṛbhustarkayāmāsa nidāghasya nareśvara /
devikāyāstaṭe vīra nāgaraṃ nāma vai puram //
1.49.d:
स ऋभुस्तर्कयामास निदाघस्य नरेश्वर ।
देविकायास्तटे वीर नागरं नाम वै पुरम् ॥
1.49.m: That Ṛbhu reflected upon Nidāgha, O ruler of men. / On the bank of the Devikā, O hero, there was a city named Nāgara,

1.49.s:
samṛddhamatiramyaṃ ca pulastyena niveśitam /
ramyopavanaparyantaṃ sa tasminpārthavottama //
1.49.d:
समृद्धमतिरम्यं च पुलस्त्येन निवेशितम् ।
रम्योपवनपर्यन्तं स तस्मिन्पार्थवोत्तम ॥
1.49.m: prosperous and very charming, founded by Pulastya, / surrounded by delightful groves; in it, O best of kings,

1.49.s:
nidādhanāmāyogajñastasya śiṣyo 'bhavatpurā /
divye varṣasahasre tu samatīte 'sya tatpuram //
1.49.d:
निदाधनामायोगज्ञस्तस्य शिष्यो ऽभवत्पुरा ।
दिव्ये वर्षसहस्रे तु समतीते ऽस्य तत्पुरम् ॥
1.49.m: his disciple formerly lived, Nidāgha by name, who knew yoga. / When a thousand divine years had elapsed, to his city

1.49.s:
jagāma sa ṛbhuḥ śiṣyaṃ nidāghamavalokitum /
sa tasya vaiśvadevanti dvārālokanagocaraḥ //
1.49.d:
जगाम स ऋभुः शिष्यं निदाघमवलोकितुम् ।
स तस्य वैश्वदेवन्ति द्वारालोकनगोचरः ॥
1.49.m: that Ṛbhu went, to see his disciple Nidāgha. / At the end of his Vaiśvadeva rite, [Ṛbhu] came into the range of his sight at the doorway.

1.49.s:
sthita stena gṛhītārtho nijaveśma praveśitaḥ /
prakṣālitāṅghripāṇiṃ ca kṛtāsanaparigraham //
1.49.d:
स्थित स्तेन गृहीतार्थो निजवेश्म प्रवेशितः ।
प्रक्षालिताङ्घ्रिपाणिं च कृतासनपरिग्रहम् ॥
1.49.m: Standing there, his hospitality was accepted by him and he was led into his house; / and when his feet and hands had been washed and he had taken a seat,

1.49.s:
uvāca sa dvijaśreṣṭho bhujyatāmiti sādaram /
ṛbhuruvāca
bho vipravarya bhoktavyaṃ yadatra bhavato gṛhe //
1.49.d:
उवाच स द्विजश्रेष्ठो भुज्यतामिति सादरम् ।
ऋभुरुवाच
भो विप्रवर्य भोक्तव्यं यदत्र भवतो गृहे ॥
1.49.m:
that best of the twice-born said respectfully: “Please eat.” / Ṛbhu said:
“O best of Brahmins, whatever food is here in your house,

1.49.s:
tatkathyatāṃ kadanneṣu na prītiḥ satataṃ mama /
nidāgha uvāca
saktuyāvakavrīhīnāmapūpānāṃ ca me gṛhe //
1.49.d:
तत्कथ्यतां कदन्नेषु न प्रीतिः सततं मम ।
निदाघ उवाच
सक्तुयावकव्रीहीनामपूपानां च मे गृहे ॥
1.49.m:
let that be told; I never have pleasure in bad food.” / Nidāgha said:
“In my house there are roasted grain flours, barley dishes, rice, and cakes;

1.49.s:
yadrocate dvijaśreṣṭha tāvadbhuṅkṣva yathecchayā /
ṛbhuruvāca
kadannāni dijaitāni miṣṭamannaṃ prayaccha me //
1.49.d:
यद्रोचते द्विजश्रेष्ठ तावद्भुङ्क्ष्व यथेच्छया ।
ऋभुरुवाच
कदन्नानि दिजैतानि मिष्टमन्नं प्रयच्छ मे ॥
1.49.m:
whatever pleases you, O best of the twice-born, eat that much as you wish.” / Ṛbhu said:
“These are bad foods, O twice-born; give me sweet food,

1.49.s:
saṃyāvapāyasādīni cekṣukā rasavanti ca /
nidāgha uvāca
gṛhe śālini madgehe yatkiñcidati śobhanam //
1.49.d:
संयावपायसादीनि चेक्षुका रसवन्ति च ।
निदाघ उवाच
गृहे शालिनि मद्गेहे यत्किञ्चिदति शोभनम् ॥
1.49.m:
such as saṃyāva sweets, milk rice, and sweet dishes prepared with sugarcane juice.” / Nidāgha said:
“O lady of the house, whatever is exceedingly fine in my home,

1.49.s:
bhojyeṣu sādhanaṃ miṣṭaṃ tenāsyānnaṃ prasādhaya /
ityuktā tena sā patnī miṣṭamannaṃ dvijasya tat //
1.49.d:
भोज्येषु साधनं मिष्टं तेनास्यान्नं प्रसाधय ।
इत्युक्ता तेन सा पत्नी मिष्टमन्नं द्विजस्य तत् ॥
1.49.m: the sweet ingredients among foods, prepare his meal with that.” / Addressed in this way by him, his wife prepared that sweet food

1.49.s:
prasādhitavatī tadvai bharturvacanagauravāt /
na bhuktavantamicchāto miṣṭamannaṃ mahāmunim //
1.49.d:
प्रसाधितवती तद्वै भर्तुर्वचनगौरवात् ।
न भुक्तवन्तमिच्छातो मिष्टमन्नं महामुनिम् ॥
1.49.m: for the twice-born, out of respect for her husband's word. / When the great sage had eaten the sweet food to his satisfaction,

1.49.s:
nidāghaḥ prāhabhūpāla praśrayāvanataḥ sthitaḥ /
nidāgha uvāca
api te paramā tṛptirutpannā puṣṭireva //
1.49.d:
निदाघः प्राहभूपाल प्रश्रयावनतः स्थितः ।
निदाघ उवाच
