अपि ते परमा तृप्तिरुत्पन्ना पुष्टिरेव ॥
1.49.m:
Nidāgha, standing bowed with deference, said, O king: / Nidāgha said:
“Has supreme satisfaction arisen in you, and nourishment as well?

1.49.s:
api te mānasaṃ svasthamāhāreṇa kṛtaṃ dvija /
kva nivāsī bhavānvipra kva vā gantuṃ samudyataḥ //
1.49.d:
अपि ते मानसं स्वस्थमाहारेण कृतं द्विज ।
क्व निवासी भवान्विप्र क्व वा गन्तुं समुद्यतः ॥
1.49.m: Has your mind been made comfortable by the meal, O twice-born? / Where is your dwelling, O Brahmin, and where are you preparing to go?

1.49.s:
āgamyate ca bhavatā yatastaśca nivedyatām /
ṛmuruvāca
kṣudhitasya ca bhukte 'nne tṛptirbrahmanvijāyate //
1.49.d:
आगम्यते च भवता यतस्तश्च निवेद्यताम् ।
ऋमुरुवाच
क्षुधितस्य च भुक्ते ऽन्ने तृप्तिर्ब्रह्मन्विजायते ॥
1.49.m:
And from where have you arrived? Please tell that.” / Ṛbhu said:
“When food is eaten by a hungry man, O Brahmin, satisfaction arises.

1.49.s:
na me kṣudhā bhavettṝptiḥ kasmānmāṃ dvija pṛcchati /
vahninā pārthivenādau dagdhe vai kṣurāpīśvaḥ //
1.49.d:
न मे क्षुधा भवेत्तॄप्तिः कस्मान्मां द्विज पृच्छति ।
वह्निना पार्थिवेनादौ दग्धे वै क्षुरापीश्वः ॥
1.49.m: I have no hunger; why does the twice-born ask me about satisfaction? / When the bodily essence is consumed by the gastric fire, hunger arises;

1.49.s:
bhavatyaṃbhasi ca kṣīṇe nṛṇāṃ tṛṣṇāsamudbhavaḥ /
kṣuttṛṣṇe dehadharmākhye na mamaite yato dvija //
1.49.d:
भवत्यंभसि च क्षीणे नृणां तृष्णासमुद्भवः ।
क्षुत्तृष्णे देहधर्माख्ये न ममैते यतो द्विज ॥
1.49.m: and when water is diminished, thirst arises in men. / Hunger and thirst are properties of the body; because these are not mine, O twice-born,

1.49.s:
tataḥ kṣutsaṃbhavābhāvāttṛptirastyeva me sadā /
manasaḥ svasthatā tuṣṭiścittadharmāvimau dvija //
1.49.d:
ततः क्षुत्संभवाभावात्तृप्तिरस्त्येव मे सदा ।
मनसः स्वस्थता तुष्टिश्चित्तधर्माविमौ द्विज ॥
1.49.m: therefore, in the absence of the occurrence of hunger, there is ever satisfaction for me. / Composure of mind and contentment are properties of thought, O twice-born.

1.49.s:
cetaso yasya yatpṛṣṭaṃ pumānebhirna yujyate /
kva nivāsastavetyuktaṃ kva gantāsi ca yattvayā //
1.49.d:
चेतसो यस्य यत्पृष्टं पुमानेभिर्न युज्यते ।
क्व निवासस्तवेत्युक्तं क्व गन्तासि च यत्त्वया ॥
1.49.m: What was asked belongs to the mind; the person is not connected with these. / As to what was said by you: ‘Where is your dwelling, and where will you go,’

1.49.s:
kutaścāgamyate tvetātrritaye 'pi nibodha me /
pumānsavargato vyāpītyākāśavadayaṃ yataḥ //
1.49.d:
कुतश्चागम्यते त्वेतात्र्रितये ऽपि निबोध मे ।
पुमान्सवर्गतो व्यापीत्याकाशवदयं यतः ॥
1.49.m: ‘and whence do you come?’—listen to me regarding all three of these: / since the person is all-pervading and omnipresent like space,

1.49.s:
kutaḥ kutra kva gantāsītyetadapyarthavatkatham /
so 'haṃ gantā na cāgantā naikadeśaniketanaḥ //
1.49.d:
कुतः कुत्र क्व गन्तासीत्येतदप्यर्थवत्कथम् ।
सो ऽहं गन्ता न चागन्ता नैकदेशनिकेतनः ॥
1.49.m: how is this meaningful: ‘Whence, whither, and where will you go?’ / As such, I am neither a goer nor a comer, nor do I have a home in any single place.

1.49.s:
tvaṃ cānye ca na ca tvaṃ tvaṃ nānye naivāhamapyaham /
miṣṭanne miṣṭamityeṣā jihvā sā me kṛtā tava //
1.49.d:
त्वं चान्ये च न च त्वं त्वं नान्ये नैवाहमप्यहम् ।
मिष्टन्ने मिष्टमित्येषा जिह्वा सा मे कृता तव ॥
1.49.m: You and others [are one]; you are not you, others are not others, nor am I indeed I. / As for sweet food, this tongue of mine was made by you [to ask]: ‘What is sweet?’

1.49.s:
kiṃ vakṣyatīti tatrāpi śrūyatāṃ dvijasattamā /
miṣṭameva yadāmiṣṭaṃ tadevodvegakāraṇam //
1.49.d:
किं वक्ष्यतीति तत्रापि श्रूयतां द्विजसत्तमा ।
मिष्टमेव यदामिष्टं तदेवोद्वेगकारणम् ॥
1.49.m: Regarding what it would say, hear that too, O best of the twice-born: / when sweet food itself becomes non-sweet, it becomes a cause of distress.

1.49.s:
amiṣṭaṃ jāyate miṣṭaṃ miṣṭādudvijate janaḥ /
ādimadhyāvasāneṣu kimannaṃ rucikāraṇam //
1.49.d:
अमिष्टं जायते मिष्टं मिष्टादुद्विजते जनः ।
आदिमध्यावसानेषु किमन्नं रुचिकारणम् ॥
1.49.m: The non-sweet becomes sweet, and a person grows disgusted with the sweet; / at the beginning, middle, and end, what food is [inherently] the cause of delight?

1.49.s:
mṛṇmayaṃ hi mṛdā yadvadgṛhaṃ liptaṃ sthirībhavet /
pārthivo 'yaṃ tathā dehaḥ pārthivaiḥ paramāṇubhiḥ //
1.49.d:
मृण्मयं हि मृदा यद्वद्गृहं लिप्तं स्थिरीभवेत् ।
पार्थिवो ऽयं तथा देहः पार्थिवैः परमाणुभिः ॥
1.49.m: Just as an earthen house plastered with earth becomes firm, / so this earthy body is maintained by earthy particles.

1.49.s:
yavagodhūmamudgādir ghṛtaṃ tailaṃ payo dadhi /
guḍaḥ phalānīti tathā pārthivāḥ paramāṇavaḥ //
1.49.d:
यवगोधूममुद्गादिर् घृतं तैलं पयो दधि ।
गुडः फलानीति तथा पार्थिवाः परमाणवः ॥
1.49.m: Barley, wheat, mung beans, and the like, ghee, oil, milk, curd, / molasses, and fruits are likewise earthy particles.

1.49.s:
tadetadbhavatā jñātvā miṣṭāmiṣṭavicāri yat /
tanmanaḥ śamanālabi kāryaṃ prāpyaṃ hi muktaye //
1.49.d:
तदेतद्भवता ज्ञात्वा मिष्टामिष्टविचारि यत् ।
तन्मनः शमनालबि कार्यं प्राप्यं हि मुक्तये ॥
1.49.m: Knowing all this, one should bring peace to that mind / which deliberates upon the sweet and the non-sweet, for liberation is to be attained.”

1.49.s:
ityākarṇya vacastasya paramārthāśritaṃ nṛpa /
praṇipatya mahābhāgo nidāgho vākyamabravīt //
1.49.d:
इत्याकर्ण्य वचस्तस्य परमार्थाश्रितं नृप ।
प्रणिपत्य महाभागो निदाघो वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥
1.49.m: Hearing his speech based upon the supreme truth, O king, / the illustrious Nidāgha prostrated and spoke these words:

1.49.s:
prasīda maddhitārthāya kathyatāṃ yastvamāgataḥ /
naṣṭo mohastavākarṇya vacāṃsyetāni me dvija //
1.49.d:
प्रसीद मद्धितार्थाय कथ्यतां यस्त्वमागतः ।
नष्टो मोहस्तवाकर्ण्य वचांस्येतानि मे द्विज ॥
1.49.m: “Be gracious; for my benefit, tell who you are that have come. / Hearing these words of yours, my delusion has been destroyed, O twice-born.”

1.49.s:
ṛbhuruvāca
ṛbhurasmi tavācāryaḥ prajñādānāya te dvija /
ihāgato 'haṃ dāsyāmi paramārthaṃ subodhitam //
1.49.d:
ऋभुरुवाच
ऋभुरस्मि तवाचार्यः प्रज्ञादानाय ते द्विज ।
इहागतो ऽहं दास्यामि परमार्थं सुबोधितम् ॥
1.49.m:
Ṛbhu said:
“I am Ṛbhu, your teacher, [come] to bestow wisdom upon you, O twice-born. / Having come here, I will impart the well-understood supreme truth.

1.49.s:
eka evamidaṃ viddhi na bhedi sakalaṃ jagat /
vāsudevābhidheyasya svarupaṃ parātmanaḥ //
1.49.d:
एक एवमिदं विद्धि न भेदि सकलं जगत् ।
वासुदेवाभिधेयस्य स्वरुपं परात्मनः ॥
1.49.m: Know this entire universe to be one only, without differentiation: / the essential form of the supreme self, designated as Vāsudeva.”

1.49.s:
brahmaṇa uvāca
tathetyuktvā nidādhena praṇipātapuraḥ saram /
pūjitaḥ parayā bhaktyānicchitaḥ prayayau vibhuḥ //
1.49.d:
ब्रह्मण उवाच
तथेत्युक्त्वा निदाधेन प्रणिपातपुरः सरम् ।
पूजितः परया भक्त्यानिच्छितः प्रययौ विभुः ॥
1.49.m:
The Brahmin said:
Having said “So be it”, Nidāgha prostrated before him / and worshipped him with supreme devotion; and the powerful lord departed without any desire.

1.49.s:
punavaṣasahasrante samāyāto nareśvara /
nidāghajñānadānāya tadeva nagaraṃ guruḥ //
1.49.d:
पुनवषसहस्रन्ते समायातो नरेश्वर ।
निदाघज्ञानदानाय तदेव नगरं गुरुः ॥
1.49.m: At the end of another thousand years, O ruler of men, / the teacher came again to that very city to bestow knowledge upon Nidāgha.

1.49.s:
nagarasya bahiḥ so 'tha nidāghaṃ dṛṣṭavān munim /
mahābalaparīvāre puraṃ viśati pārthive //
1.49.d:
नगरस्य बहिः सो ऽथ निदाघं दृष्टवान् मुनिम् ।
महाबलपरीवारे पुरं विशति पार्थिवे ॥
1.49.m: Then, outside the city, he saw the sage Nidāgha / while the king, surrounded by a large army, was entering the city.

1.49.s:
dūrasthitaṃ mahābhāge janasaṃmardavarjakam /
kṣutkṣāmakaṇṭhamāyāntamaraṇyātsasamitkuśam //
1.49.d:
दूरस्थितं महाभागे जनसंमर्दवर्जकम् ।
क्षुत्क्षामकण्ठमायान्तमरण्यात्ससमित्कुशम् ॥
1.49.m: Standing far away, O fortunate one, avoiding the crowd of people, / his throat parched with hunger, coming from the forest with sacrificial fuel and kuśa grass,

1.49.s:
dṛṣṭvā nidāghaṃ sa ṛbhurupāgatyābhivādya ca /
uvāca kasmādekāntaṃ sthīyata bhavatā dvija //
1.49.d:
दृष्ट्वा निदाघं स ऋभुरुपागत्याभिवाद्य च ।
उवाच कस्मादेकान्तं स्थीयत भवता द्विज ॥
1.49.m: seeing Nidāgha, Ṛbhu approached, saluted him, / and said: “Why are you staying apart in solitude, O twice-born one?”

1.49.d:
॥ निदाघ उवाच
भो विप्र जनसंमर्द्दो महानेष जनेश्वरे ।
प्रविवक्षौ पुरे रम्ये तेनात्र स्थीयते मया ॥
1.49.m: Nidāgha said: / “O brāhmaṇa, great is this crowd of people as the lord of men / is wishing to enter this delightful city; therefore do I stay here.”

1.49.s:
ṛbhuruvāca
narādhipo 'tra katamaḥ katamaścetaro janaḥ /
kathyatāṃ me dvijaśreṣṭha tvamabhijño mato mama //
1.49.d:
ऋभुरुवाच
नराधिपो ऽत्र कतमः कतमश्चेतरो जनः ।
कथ्यतां मे द्विजश्रेष्ठ त्वमभिज्ञो मतो मम ॥
1.49.m: Ṛbhu said: / “Which one here is the king, and which one is the other person? / Tell me, O best of the twice-born; in my view, you are knowledgeable.”

1.49.s:
nidāgha uvāca
yo 'yaṃ gajendramunmattamadriśṛṅgasamucchrayam /
adhiruḍho narendro 'yaṃ parito yastathetaraḥ //
1.49.d:
निदाघ उवाच
यो ऽयं गजेन्द्रमुन्मत्तमद्रिशृङ्गसमुच्छ्रयम् ।
अधिरुढो नरेन्द्रो ऽयं परितो यस्तथेतरः ॥
1.49.m: Nidāgha said: / “He who is mounted upon that lordly elephant, furious and lofty like a mountain peak, / is the king; those who are around him are the others.”

1.49.s:
ṛbhuruvāca
etau hi gajarājānau dṛṣṭau hi yugapanmayā /
bhavatā nirviśeṣeṇa pṛthagvedopalakṣitau //
1.49.d:
ऋभुरुवाच
एतौ हि गजराजानौ दृष्टौ हि युगपन्मया ।
भवता निर्विशेषेण पृथग्वेदोपलक्षितौ ॥
1.49.m: Ṛbhu said: / “Indeed, both of these—the elephant and the king—are seen at once by me; / but by you, without distinction, they are characterized as distinct.

1.49.s:
tatkathyatāṃ mahābhāga viśeṣo bhavatānayoḥ /
jñātumicchāmyahaṃ ko 'tra gajaḥ ko vā narādhipaḥ //
1.49.d:
तत्कथ्यतां महाभाग विशेषो भवतानयोः ।
ज्ञातुमिच्छाम्यहं को ऽत्र गजः को वा नराधिपः ॥
1.49.m: Therefore tell me, O fortunate one, the distinction between the two of them; / I wish to know who here is the elephant, and who is the king.”

1.49.s:
nidādha uvāca
gajoyo 'yamadho brahmannuparyasyaiṣa bhūpatiḥ /
vāhyavāhakasaṃbandhaṃ ko na jānāti vai dvija //
1.49.d:
निदाध उवाच
गजोयो ऽयमधो ब्रह्मन्नुपर्यस्यैष भूपतिः ।
वाह्यवाहकसंबन्धं को न जानाति वै द्विज ॥
1.49.m: Nidāgha said: / “This one below, O brāhmaṇa, is the elephant; above him is the king. / Who indeed does not know the relation between the bearer and the borne, O twice-born one?”

1.49.s:
ṛbhuruvāca
brahmanyathāhaṃ jānīyāṃ tathā māmavabodhaya /
adhaḥ sattvavibhāgaṃ kiṃ kiṃ corddhamabhidhīyate //
1.49.d:
ऋभुरुवाच
ब्रह्मन्यथाहं जानीयां तथा मामवबोधय ।
अधः सत्त्वविभागं किं किं चोर्द्धमभिधीयते ॥
1.49.m: Ṛbhu said: / “O brāhmaṇa, instruct me so that I may understand: / what is designated as the lower entity, and what as the upper?”

1.49.s:
brāhmaṇa uvāca
ityuktvā sahasāruhya nidāghaḥ prāha taṃ ṛbhum /
śrayatāṃ kathayāmyeṣa yanmāṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi //
1.49.d:
ब्राह्मण उवाच
इत्युक्त्वा सहसारुह्य निदाघः प्राह तं ऋभुम् ।
श्रयतां कथयाम्येष यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि ॥
1.49.m: The brāhmaṇa said: / Having spoken thus, suddenly mounting upon him, Nidāgha said to Ṛbhu: / “Listen, I shall explain that about which you question me:

1.49.s:
uparyahaṃ yathā rājā tvamadhaḥkuñjaro yathā /
avabodhāya te brahmandṛṣṭānto darśito mayā //
1.49.d:
उपर्यहं यथा राजा त्वमधःकुञ्जरो यथा ।
अवबोधाय ते ब्रह्मन्दृष्टान्तो दर्शितो मया ॥
1.49.m: I am above, like the king; you are below, like the elephant. / For your understanding, O brāhmaṇa, this example has been shown by me.”

1.49.s:
ṛbhuruvāca
tvaṃ rājeva dvijaśreṣṭha sthito 'haṃ gajavadyadi /
tadevaṃ tvaṃ samācakṣva katamastvamahaṃ tathā //
1.49.d:
ऋभुरुवाच
त्वं राजेव द्विजश्रेष्ठ स्थितो ऽहं गजवद्यदि ।
तदेवं त्वं समाचक्ष्व कतमस्त्वमहं तथा ॥
1.49.m: Ṛbhu said: / “If you are like the king, O best of the twice-born, and I stand like the elephant, / then explain this: which one are you, and which one am I?”

1.49.s:
brāhmaṇa uvāca
ityuktaḥ satvarastasya caraṇāvabhivandya saḥ /
nidādhaḥ prāha bhagavannācāryastvamṛbhurmam //
1.49.d:
ब्राह्मण उवाच
इत्युक्तः सत्वरस्तस्य चरणावभिवन्द्य सः ।
निदाधः प्राह भगवन्नाचार्यस्त्वमृभुर्मम् ॥
1.49.m: The brāhmaṇa said: / Addressed thus, quickly bowing to his feet, / Nidāgha said: “O venerable one, you are my teacher, Ṛbhu!

1.49.s:
nānyasyādvai vasaṃskārasaṃskṛtaṃ mānasaṃ tathā /
yathācāryasya tena tvāṃ manye prāptamahaṃ gurum //
1.49.d:
नान्यस्याद्वै वसंस्कारसंस्कृतं मानसं तथा ।
यथाचार्यस्य तेन त्वां मन्ये प्राप्तमहं गुरुम् ॥
1.49.m: No one else’s mind is thus refined by the impression of non-duality / as that of my teacher; by that I recognize that you, my guru, have arrived.”

1.49.s:
ṛbhuruvāca
tavopadeśadānāya pūrvaśuśrūṣaṇāttava /
gurusnehādṛbhurnāmanidāghaṃ samupāgataḥ //
1.49.d:
ऋभुरुवाच
तवोपदेशदानाय पूर्वशुश्रूषणात्तव ।
गुरुस्नेहादृभुर्नामनिदाघं समुपागतः ॥
1.49.m: Ṛbhu said: / “To bestow instruction upon you, because of your past service / and out of affection for a disciple, I, named Ṛbhu, have come to Nidāgha.

1.49.s:
tadetadupadiṣṭaṃ te saṃkṣepeṇa mahāmate /
paramārthasārabhūtaṃ yattadadvaitamaśeṣataḥ //
1.49.d:
तदेतदुपदिष्टं ते संक्षेपेण महामते ।
परमार्थसारभूतं यत्तदद्वैतमशेषतः ॥
1.49.m: Thus has this been taught to you in brief, O great-minded one: / that which is the essence of the ultimate truth, non-duality, completely.

1.49.s:
brāhmaṇa uvāca
evamuktvā dadau vidyāṃ nidāghaṃ sa ṛbhurguruḥ /
nidāgho 'pyupadeśena tenādvaitaparo 'bhavat //
1.49.d:
ब्राह्मण उवाच
एवमुक्त्वा ददौ विद्यां निदाघं स ऋभुर्गुरुः ।
निदाघो ऽप्युपदेशेन तेनाद्वैतपरो ऽभवत् ॥
1.49.m: The brāhmaṇa said: / Having spoken thus, the guru Ṛbhu imparted knowledge to Nidāgha; / and Nidāgha too, through that instruction, became devoted to non-duality.

1.49.s:
sarvabhūtānyabhedena dadṛśe sa tadātmanaḥ /
tathā brahmatanau muktimavāca paramādvijaḥ //
1.49.d:
सर्वभूतान्यभेदेन ददृशे स तदात्मनः ।
तथा ब्रह्मतनौ मुक्तिमवाच परमाद्विजः ॥
1.49.m: He beheld all beings without distinction from his own Self; / and thus the twice-born one attained supreme liberation in the body of Brahman.

1.49.s:
tathā tvamapi dharmajña tulyātmaripubāndhavaḥ /
bhava sarvagataṃ jñānamātmānamavanīpate //
1.49.d:
तथा त्वमपि धर्मज्ञ तुल्यात्मरिपुबान्धवः ।
भव सर्वगतं ज्ञानमात्मानमवनीपते ॥
1.49.m: So you too, O knower of dharma, seeing yourself, your enemy, and your relative as equal, / become the Self, which is omnipresent knowledge, O lord of the earth!

1.49.s:
sitanīlādibhedena yathaikaṃ dṛśyate nabhaḥ /
bhrāntadṛṣṭibhirātmāpi tathaikaḥ sanpṛthak pṛthak //
1.49.d:
सितनीलादिभेदेन यथैकं दृश्यते नभः ।
भ्रान्तदृष्टिभिरात्मापि तथैकः सन्पृथक् पृथक् ॥
1.49.m: Just as the single sky appears different through designations such as white or blue, / so too the Self, though single, appears manifold to those whose vision is confused.

1.49.s:
ekaḥ samastaṃ yadihāsti kiñcittadacyuto nāsti paraṃ tato 'nyat /
so 'haṃ sa ca tvaṃ sa ca sarvametadātmāṃsvayaṃ bhātyapabhedamohaḥ //
1.49.d:
एकः समस्तं यदिहास्ति किञ्चित्तदच्युतो नास्ति परं ततो ऽन्यत् ।
सो ऽहं स च त्वं स च सर्वमेतदात्मांस्वयं भात्यपभेदमोहः ॥
1.49.m: All that is anything whatever here is one, and that is Acyuta; there is nothing else beyond Him. / ‘He is I,’ and ‘He is you,’ and ‘He is all this’: the Self shines of Itself when the delusion of difference is removed.”

1.49.s:
sanandana uvāca
itīritastena sa rājavaryastatyāja bhedaṃ paramārthadṛṣṭiḥ /
sa cāpi jātismaraṇāvabodastatraiva janmanyapavargamāpa //
1.49.d:
सनन्दन उवाच
इतीरितस्तेन स राजवर्यस्तत्याज भेदं परमार्थदृष्टिः ।
स चापि जातिस्मरणावबोदस्तत्रैव जन्मन्यपवर्गमाप ॥
1.49.m: Sanandana said: / Addressed thus by him, that best of kings, endowed with insight into the ultimate truth, abandoned difference; / and he too, awakening to the memory of previous births, attained final emancipation in that very life.

1.49.s:
paramārthādhyātmametattubhyamuktaṃ munīśvara /
brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśāṃ śrortṛāṇāṃ cāpi muktidam //
1.49.d:
परमार्थाध्यात्ममेतत्तुभ्यमुक्तं मुनीश्वर ।
ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां श्रोर्तृआणां चापि मुक्तिदम् ॥
1.49.m: This spiritual discourse on the ultimate truth has been spoken to you, O lord of sages; / it grants liberation to brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and listeners as well.

1.49.s:
yathā pṛṣṭaṃ tvayā brahmaṃstathā te gaditaṃ mayā /
brahmajñānamidaṃ śuddhaṃ kimanyatkathayāmi vai //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne dvi.pā.ekonapañcāśattamodhyāyaḥ
1.49.d:
यथा पृष्टं त्वया ब्रह्मंस्तथा ते गदितं मया ।
ब्रह्मज्ञानमिदं शुद्धं किमन्यत्कथयामि वै ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने द्वि।पा।एकोनपञ्चाशत्तमोध्यायः
1.49.m:
As was asked by you, O brāhmaṇa, so has it been declared to you by me: / this pure knowledge of Brahman. What else indeed shall I tell you?”

Thus ends the forty-ninth chapter in the second quarter of the Bṛhadupākhyāna in the first part of the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

1.50.s:
sūta uvāca
śrutvā sanandanasyetthaṃ vacanaṃ nārado muniḥ /
asaṃtuṣṭa iva prāha bhrātaraṃ taṃ sanandanam //
1.50.d:
सूत उवाच
श्रुत्वा सनन्दनस्येत्थं वचनं नारदो मुनिः ।
असंतुष्ट इव प्राह भ्रातरं तं सनन्दनम् ॥
1.50.m: Sūta said: / Having heard these words of Sanandana, the sage Nārada, / as if unsatisfied, said to his brother Sanandana:

1.50.s:
nārada uvāca
bhagavansarvamākhyātaṃ yatpṛṣṭaṃ bhavato mayā /
tathāpi nātmā prīyeta śṛṇvanharikathāṃ muhuḥ //
1.50.d:
नारद उवाच
भगवन्सर्वमाख्यातं यत्पृष्टं भवतो मया ।
तथापि नात्मा प्रीयेत शृण्वन्हरिकथां मुहुः ॥
1.50.m: Nārada said: / “O venerable one, everything about which I asked you has been told; / nonetheless, my soul is not satiated by repeatedly hearing discourse on Hari.

1.50.s:
śrūyate vyāsaputrastu śukaḥ paramadharmavit /
siddhiṃ sumahatīṃ prāpto nirviṇṇo 'vāntaraṃ bahiḥ //
1.50.d:
श्रूयते व्यासपुत्रस्तु शुकः परमधर्मवित् ।
सिद्धिं सुमहतीं प्राप्तो निर्विण्णो ऽवान्तरं बहिः ॥
1.50.m: It is heard that Vyāsa’s son, Śuka, knowing the highest dharma, / attained exceedingly great perfection, being detached within and without.

1.50.s:
brahmanpuṃsastu vijñānaṃ mahatāṃ sevanaṃ vinā /
na jāyate kathaṃ prāpto jñānaṃ vyāsātmajaḥ śiśuḥ //
1.50.d:
ब्रह्मन्पुंसस्तु विज्ञानं महतां सेवनं विना ।
न जायते कथं प्राप्तो ज्ञानं व्यासात्मजः शिशुः ॥
1.50.m: O brāhmaṇa, discernment does not arise in a person without serving the great; / how did Vyāsa’s son, as a child, attain knowledge?

1.50.s:
tasya janmarahasyaṃ me kamacāpyasya śṛṇvate /
samākhyāhi mahābhāga mo7śāstrārthavidbhavān //
1.50.d:
तस्य जन्मरहस्यं मे कमचाप्यस्य शृण्वते ।
समाख्याहि महाभाग मो7शास्त्रार्थविद्भवान् ॥
1.50.m: Tell me, who am listening, the secret of his birth and of his deeds, / O fortunate one, for you know the meaning of the scriptures on liberation.”

1.50.s:
sanandana uvāca
śṛṇu viprapravakṣyāmi śukotpattiṃ samāsataḥ /
yāṃ śrutvā brahmatattvajño jāyate mānavo mune //
1.50.d:
सनन्दन उवाच
शृणु विप्रप्रवक्ष्यामि शुकोत्पत्तिं समासतः ।
यां श्रुत्वा ब्रह्मतत्त्वज्ञो जायते मानवो मुने ॥
1.50.m: Sanandana said: / “Listen, O brāhmaṇa; I shall relate the origin of Śuka in brief, / hearing which a man becomes a knower of the truth of Brahman, O sage.

1.50.s:
na hāyanairna palitairna vittena na bandhubhiḥ /
ṛṣayaścakrire dharmaṃ yo 'nūcānaḥ sa no mahān //
1.50.d:
न हायनैर्न पलितैर्न वित्तेन न बन्धुभिः ।
ऋषयश्चक्रिरे धर्मं यो ऽनूचानः स नो महान् ॥
1.50.m: Not by years, nor by grey hair, nor by wealth, nor by kinsmen / did the ṛṣis establish dharma: ‘He who has studied the Veda is great among us.’

1.50.s:
nārada uvāca
anūcānaḥ kathaṃbrahmanpumānbhavati mānada /
tanme karma samācakṣva śrotuṃ kautūhalaṃ mama //
1.50.d:
नारद उवाच
अनूचानः कथंब्रह्मन्पुमान्भवति मानद ।
तन्मे कर्म समाचक्ष्व श्रोतुं कौतूहलं मम ॥
1.50.m: Nārada said: / “How does a man become an anūcāna, O brāhmaṇa, O giver of honor? / Explain that practice to me; I have curiosity to hear.”

1.50.s:
sanandana uvāca
śṛṇu nārada vakṣyāmi hyanūcānasya lakṣaṇam /
yajjñātvā sāṅgavedānāmabhijño jāyate naraḥ //
1.50.d:
सनन्दन उवाच
शृणु नारद वक्ष्यामि ह्यनूचानस्य लक्षणम् ।
यज्ज्ञात्वा साङ्गवेदानामभिज्ञो जायते नरः ॥
1.50.m: Sanandana said: / “Listen, O Nārada, I shall declare the characteristics of an anūcāna, / knowing which a man becomes proficient in the Vedas along with their auxiliary limbs.

1.50.s:
śikṣā kalpo vyākaraṇaṃ niruktaṃ jyotiṣaṃ tathā /
chandaḥśāstraṃ ṣaḍetāni vādāṅgāni vidurbudhāḥ //
1.50.d:
शिक्षा कल्पो व्याकरणं निरुक्तं ज्योतिषं तथा ।
छन्दःशास्त्रं षडेतानि वादाङ्गानि विदुर्बुधाः ॥
1.50.m: Phonetics, ritual treatises, grammar, etymology, astronomy, / and the science of metrics—the wise know these six as the limbs of the Vedas.

1.50.s:
ṛgvedro 'tha yadurvedaḥ sāmavedo hyatharvaṇaḥ /
vedāścatvāra evaite proktā dharmanirūpaṇe //
1.50.d:
ऋग्वेद्रो ऽथ यदुर्वेदः सामवेदो ह्यथर्वणः ।
वेदाश्चत्वार एवैते प्रोक्ता धर्मनिरूपणे ॥
1.50.m: The Ṛgveda, then the Yajurveda, the Sāmaveda, and the Atharvaveda: / these four alone are declared as the Vedas for determining dharma.

1.50.s:
sāṃgānvedānguroryastu samadhīte dvijottamaḥ /
so 'nūcānaḥ prabhavati nānyathā granthakoṭibhiḥ //
1.50.d:
सांगान्वेदान्गुरोर्यस्तु समधीते द्विजोत्तमः ।
सो ऽनूचानः प्रभवति नान्यथा ग्रन्थकोटिभिः ॥
1.50.m: That best of the twice-born who properly studies the Vedas with their auxiliary limbs from a teacher / becomes an anūcāna, not otherwise through crores of texts.”

1.50.s:
nārada uvāca
aṅgānāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ brūhi vedānāṃ cāpi vistarāt /
tvaṃmasmāsu mahāvijñaḥ sāṃgeṣveteṣu mānada //
1.50.d:
नारद उवाच
अङ्गानां लक्षणं ब्रूहि वेदानां चापि विस्तरात् ।
त्वंमस्मासु महाविज्ञः सांगेष्वेतेषु मानद ॥
1.50.m: Nārada said: / “Tell the characteristics of the auxiliary limbs and of the Vedas in detail; / among us you are exceedingly wise concerning these [Vedas] with their auxiliary limbs, O giver of honor.”

1.50.s:
sanandana uvāca
praśnabhāro 'yamatulastvayā mama kṛto dvija /
saṃkṣepātkathayiṣyāmi sārameṣāṃ suniścitam //
1.50.d:
सनन्दन उवाच
प्रश्नभारो ऽयमतुलस्त्वया मम कृतो द्विज ।
संक्षेपात्कथयिष्यामि सारमेषां सुनिश्चितम् ॥
1.50.m: Sanandana said: / “An unequaled burden of questions has been laid upon me by you, O twice-born one; / I shall relate their well-ascertained essence in brief.

1.50.s:
svaraḥ pradhānaḥ śikṣāyāṃ kīrttito munibhirdijaiḥ /
vedānāṃ vedavidbhistu tacchṛṇuṣva vadāmi te //
1.50.d:
स्वरः प्रधानः शिक्षायां कीर्त्तितो मुनिभिर्दिजैः ।
वेदानां वेदविद्भिस्तु तच्छृणुष्व वदामि ते ॥
1.50.m: Pitch is proclaimed by twice-born sages to be the chief [element] in phonetics / for the Vedas, by the knowers of the Veda; listen to that, I shall tell you.

1.50.s:
ārcikaṃ gāthikaṃ caiva sāmikaṃ ca svarāntaram /
kṛtānte svaraśāstrāṇāṃ prayoktavya viśeṣataḥ //
1.50.d:
आर्चिकं गाथिकं चैव सामिकं च स्वरान्तरम् ।
कृतान्ते स्वरशास्त्राणां प्रयोक्तव्य विशेषतः ॥
1.50.m: Belonging to the Ṛc, to the Gāthā, and to the Sāman, and another pitch; / according to the conclusion of the texts on pitch, they are to be employed distinctively.

1.50.s:
ekāntaraḥ svaro hyapsu gāthāsudvyantaraḥ svaraḥ /
sāmasu tryantaraṃ vidyādetāvatsvarato 'ntaram //
1.50.d:
एकान्तरः स्वरो ह्यप्सु गाथासुद्व्यन्तरः स्वरः ।
सामसु त्र्यन्तरं विद्यादेतावत्स्वरतो ऽन्तरम् ॥
1.50.m: Pitch is separated by one interval in the verses, by two intervals in the gāthās, / and one should know it as having three intervals in the sāmans: such is the interval of pitch.

1.50.s:
ṛksāmayajuraṅgāni ye yajñeṣu prayuñjate /
avijñānāddhi śikṣāyāsteṣāṃ bhavati visvaraḥ //
1.50.d:
ऋक्सामयजुरङ्गानि ये यज्ञेषु प्रयुञ्जते ।
अविज्ञानाद्धि शिक्षायास्तेषां भवति विस्वरः ॥
1.50.m: Those who employ the limbs of the Ṛc, Sāman, and Yajus in sacrifices / without knowledge of phonetics—their chant becomes discordant.

1.50.s:
mantro hīnaḥ svarato varṇato vā mithyāprayukto na tamarthamāha /
sa vāgvajro yajamānaṃ hirnāsti yathendraśatruḥ svarato 'parādhāt //
1.50.d:
मन्त्रो हीनः स्वरतो वर्णतो वा मिथ्याप्रयुक्तो न तमर्थमाह ।
स वाग्वज्रो यजमानं हिर्नास्ति यथेन्द्रशत्रुः स्वरतो ऽपराधात् ॥
1.50.m: A mantra deficient in pitch or accent, or falsely employed, does not convey that intended meaning; / that verbal thunderbolt destroys the sacrificer, as did the word ‘indraśatru’ due to an error in pitch.”

1.50.s:
uraḥ kaṇṭhaḥ śiraścaiva sthānāni trīṇi vāṅkye /
savanānyāhuretāni sāma vāpyarddhatoṃ'taram //
1.50.d:
उरः कण्ठः शिरश्चैव स्थानानि त्रीणि वाङ्क्ये ।
सवनान्याहुरेतानि साम वाप्यर्द्धतोंऽतरम् ॥
1.50.m: The chest, the throat, and the head: these are the three places in speech. / They call these the pressings, or [in] the Sāma, intermediate in half.

1.50.s:
uraḥ saptavivāraṃ syāttathā kaṇṭhastathā śiraḥ /
na ca śakto 'si vyaktastu tathā prāvacanā vidhiḥ //
1.50.d:
उरः सप्तविवारं स्यात्तथा कण्ठस्तथा शिरः ।
न च शक्तो ऽसि व्यक्तस्तु तथा प्रावचना विधिः ॥
1.50.m: The chest has seven apertures, as does the throat, and likewise the head; / but you are not capable [to produce it] distinctly, such is the rule of recitation.

1.50.s:
kaṭhakālāpavṛtteṣu taittirāhvarakeṣu ca /
ṛgvede sāmavede ca vaktavyaḥ prathamaḥ svaraḥ //
1.50.d:
कठकालापवृत्तेषु तैत्तिराह्वरकेषु च ।
ऋग्वेदे सामवेदे च वक्तव्यः प्रथमः स्वरः ॥
1.50.m: In the meters of the Kaṭhas and the Kalāpas, and among the Taittirīyas and Āhvarakas, / in the Ṛgveda and the Sāmaveda, the first note should be uttered.

1.50.s:
ṛgvedastu dvitīyena tṛtīyena ca vartate /
uccamadhyamasaṃghātaḥ svaro bhavati pārthivaḥ //
1.50.d:
ऋग्वेदस्तु द्वितीयेन तृतीयेन च वर्तते ।
उच्चमध्यमसंघातः स्वरो भवति पार्थिवः ॥
1.50.m: The Ṛgveda proceeds with the second and third [notes]; / a combination of high and middle becomes the terrestrial note, O king.

1.50.s:
tṛtīya prathamakruṣṭā kurvantyāhvarakān svarān /
dvitīyādyāstu madrāntāstaittirīyāścatuḥsvarān //
1.50.d:
तृतीय प्रथमक्रुष्टा कुर्वन्त्याह्वरकान् स्वरान् ।
द्वितीयाद्यास्तु मद्रान्तास्तैत्तिरीयाश्चतुःस्वरान् ॥
1.50.m: The Āhvarakas make their notes using the third, the first, and the kruṣṭa; / but the Taittirīyas use four notes, beginning with the second and ending with the mandra.

1.50.s:
prathamaśca dvitīyaśca tṛtīyo 'tha caturthakaḥ /
mandraḥ kruṣṭo munīśvara etānkurvanti sāmagāḥ //
1.50.d:
प्रथमश्च द्वितीयश्च तृतीयो ऽथ चतुर्थकः ।
मन्द्रः क्रुष्टो मुनीश्वर एतान्कुर्वन्ति सामगाः ॥
1.50.m: The first, the second, the third, then the fourth, / the mandra, and the kruṣṭa, O lord of sages—these the Sāma-singers produce.

1.50.s:
dvitīyaprathamāvetau nāṇḍibhāllavinau svarau /
tathā śātapathāvetau svarau vājasaneyinām //
1.50.d:
द्वितीयप्रथमावेतौ नाण्डिभाल्लविनौ स्वरौ ।
तथा शातपथावेतौ स्वरौ वाजसनेयिनाम् ॥
1.50.m: These two notes, the second and the first, belong to the Nāṇḍis and Bhāllavins; / likewise these two belong to the Śatapatha [tradition] of the Vājasaneyins.

1.50.s:
ete viśeṣataḥ proktāḥ svarā vai sārvavaidikāḥ /
ityetañcaritaṃ sarvaṃ svarāṇāṃ sārvavaidikam //
1.50.d:
एते विशेषतः प्रोक्ताः स्वरा वै सार्ववैदिकाः ।
इत्येतञ्चरितं सर्वं स्वराणां सार्ववैदिकम् ॥
1.50.m: These have been proclaimed specifically as the universal Vedic notes; / thus has been described this entire course of the universal Vedic notes.

1.50.s:
sāmavede tu vakṣyāmi svarāṇāṃ caritaṃ yathā /
alpagranthaṃ prabhūtārthaṃ sāmavedāṅgamuttamam //
1.50.d:
सामवेदे तु वक्ष्यामि स्वराणां चरितं यथा ।
अल्पग्रन्थं प्रभूतार्थं सामवेदाङ्गमुत्तमम् ॥
1.50.m: Now I shall explain the course of notes according to the Sāmaveda— / concise in text, abundant in meaning, the supreme subsidiary limb of the Sāmaveda—

1.50.s:
tānarāgasvaragrāmamūrcchanānāṃ tu lakṣaṇam /
pavitraṃ pāvanaṃ puṇyaṃ yathā tubhyaṃ prakīrtitam //
1.50.d:
तानरागस्वरग्राममूर्च्छनानां तु लक्षणम् ।
पवित्रं पावनं पुण्यं यथा तुभ्यं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
1.50.m: namely, the characteristics of the tānas, rāgas, svaras, grāmas, and mūrcchanās, / pure, purifying, and meritorious, just as it has been related to you.

1.50.s:
śikṣāmāhurdvijātīnāmṛgyajuḥ sāmalakṣaṇam /
sapta svarāsrayo grāmā mṛrchanāstvekaviṃśatiḥ //
1.50.d:
शिक्षामाहुर्द्विजातीनामृग्यजुः सामलक्षणम् ।
सप्त स्वरास्रयो ग्रामा मृर्छनास्त्वेकविंशतिः ॥
1.50.m: They declare phonetics (śikṣā) to be the characteristic sign of the twice-born for the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāma. / There are seven notes, three grāmas, and twenty-one mūrcchanās,

1.50.s:
tānā ekonapañcāśadityetaḥsvaramaṇḍalam /
ṣaṅjaśca ṛṣabhaścaiva gāndhāro madhyamastathā //
1.50.d:
ताना एकोनपञ्चाशदित्येतःस्वरमण्डलम् ।
षङ्जश्च ऋषभश्चैव गान्धारो मध्यमस्तथा ॥
1.50.m: and forty-nine tānas—such is the circle of musical notes: / ṣaḍja, ṛṣabha, gāndhāra, and madhyama,

1.50.s:
pañcamo dhaivataścaivaṃ niṣādaḥ saptamaḥ svaraḥ /
ṣaṅjamadhyamagāndhārāsrarayo grāmāḥ prakīrtitāḥ //
1.50.d:
पञ्चमो धैवतश्चैवं निषादः सप्तमः स्वरः ।
षङ्जमध्यमगान्धारास्ररयो ग्रामाः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
1.50.m: pañcama, dhaivata, and niṣāda as the seventh note. / Ṣaḍja, madhyama, and gāndhāra are proclaimed as the three grāmas.

1.50.s:
bhūrllokājjāyate ṣaṅjo bhuvarlokāñca madhyamaḥ /
svargābhrāñcaiva gāndhāro grāmasthānāni trīṇi hi //
1.50.d:
भूर्ल्लोकाज्जायते षङ्जो भुवर्लोकाञ्च मध्यमः ।
स्वर्गाभ्राञ्चैव गान्धारो ग्रामस्थानानि त्रीणि हि ॥
1.50.m: Ṣaḍja is born from the earth world (bhūrloka), and madhyama from the mid-region (bhuvarloka), / and gāndhāra from the heavens (svarga); for there are three seats of the grāmas.

1.50.s:
svarāṇāṃ ca viśeṣeṇa grāmarāgā iti smṛtāḥ /
viṃśatirmadhyamagrāme ṣaṅjagrāme caturdaśa //
1.50.d:
स्वराणां च विशेषेण ग्रामरागा इति स्मृताः ।
विंशतिर्मध्यमग्रामे षङ्जग्रामे चतुर्दश ॥
1.50.m: And in particular, they are known as the grāmarāgas of the notes: / twenty in the madhyama-grāma, and fourteen in the ṣaḍja-grāma.

1.50.s:
tānānpaṃ cadaśecchanti gāndhāre sāmagāyinām /
nadī viśālā sumukhī citrā citravatī mukhā //
1.50.d:
तानान्पं चदशेच्छन्ति गान्धारे सामगायिनाम् ।
नदी विशाला सुमुखी चित्रा चित्रवती मुखा ॥
1.50.m: They desire fifteen tānas in the gāndhāra[-grāma] for the singers of the Sāma. / Nadī, Viśālā, Sumukhī, Citrā, Citravatī, Mukhā,

1.50.s:
balā cāpyatha vijñeyā devānāṃ sapta mūrchanāḥ /
āpyāyinī viśvabhṛtā candrā hemā kapardinī //
1.50.d:
बला चाप्यथ विज्ञेया देवानां सप्त मूर्छनाः ।
आप्यायिनी विश्वभृता चन्द्रा हेमा कपर्दिनी ॥
1.50.m: and Balā should be known as the seven mūrcchanās of the gods. / Āpyāyinī, Viśvabhṛtā, Candrā, Hemā, Kapardinī,

1.50.s:
maitrī ca bārhatī caiva pitṝṇāṃ sapta mūrchanāḥ /
ṣaṅje tūttaramandrā syādṛṣabhe cābhirūhatā //
1.50.d:
मैत्री च बार्हती चैव पितॄणां सप्त मूर्छनाः ।
षङ्जे तूत्तरमन्द्रा स्यादृषभे चाभिरूहता ॥
1.50.m: Maitrī, and Bārhatī are the seven mūrcchanās of the ancestors. / In ṣaḍja there is Uttaramandrā, and in ṛṣabha, Abhirūhatā;

1.50.s:
aśvakrāntā tu gāndhāre tṛtīyā mūrcchanā smṛtā /
madhyame khalu sauvīrā hṛṣikā pañcame svare //
1.50.d:
अश्वक्रान्ता तु गान्धारे तृतीया मूर्च्छना स्मृता ।
मध्यमे खलु सौवीरा हृषिका पञ्चमे स्वरे ॥
1.50.m: Aśvakrāntā in gāndhāra is considered the third mūrcchanā; / Sauvīrā indeed in madhyama, and Hṛṣīkā on the note pañcama;

1.50.s:
dhaivate cāpi vijñeyā mūrchanā tūttarā matā /
niṣāde rajanīṃ vidyādṛṣīṇāṃ sapta mūrchanāḥ //
1.50.d:
धैवते चापि विज्ञेया मूर्छना तूत्तरा मता ।
निषादे रजनीं विद्यादृषीणां सप्त मूर्छनाः ॥
1.50.m: on dhaivata, the mūrcchanā known as Uttarā is recognized; / on niṣāda, one should know Rajanī: [these are] the seven mūrcchanās of the sages.

1.50.s:
upajīvanti gandharvā devānāṃ sapta mūrchanāḥ /
pitṝṇāṃ mūrcchānāḥ sapta tathā yakṣā na saṃśayaḥ //
1.50.d:
उपजीवन्ति गन्धर्वा देवानां सप्त मूर्छनाः ।
पितॄणां मूर्च्छानाः सप्त तथा यक्षा न संशयः ॥
1.50.m: The Gandharvas depend upon the seven mūrcchanās of the gods; / likewise the Yakṣas without doubt [depend upon] the seven mūrcchanās of the ancestors.

1.50.s:
ṛṣīṇāṃ mūrchanāḥ sapta yāstvimā laukikāḥ smṛtāḥ /
ṣaṅjaḥ prīṇāti vai devānṛṣīnprīṇāti carṣabhaḥ //
1.50.d:
ऋषीणां मूर्छनाः सप्त यास्त्विमा लौकिकाः स्मृताः ।
षङ्जः प्रीणाति वै देवानृषीन्प्रीणाति चर्षभः ॥
1.50.m: These seven mūrcchanās of the sages are considered mundane (laukika). / Ṣaḍja pleases the gods, and ṛṣabha pleases the sages;

1.50.s:
pitṝn prīṇāti gāndhāro gandharvānmadhyamaḥ svaraḥ /
devānpitṝnṛṣīṃścaiva svaraḥ prīṇāti pañcamaḥ //
1.50.d:
पितॄन् प्रीणाति गान्धारो गन्धर्वान्मध्यमः स्वरः ।
देवान्पितॄनृषींश्चैव स्वरः प्रीणाति पञ्चमः ॥
1.50.m: gāndhāra pleases the ancestors, and the note madhyama pleases the Gandharvas; / the note pañcama pleases the gods, the ancestors, and the sages;

1.50.s:
yakṣānniṣādaḥ prīṇāti bhūtagrāmaṃ ca dhaivataḥ /
gānasya tu daśavidhā guṇavṛttistu tadyathā //
1.50.d:
यक्षान्निषादः प्रीणाति भूतग्रामं च धैवतः ।
गानस्य तु दशविधा गुणवृत्तिस्तु तद्यथा ॥
1.50.m: niṣāda pleases the Yakṣas, and dhaivata pleases the host of living beings. / Now, the tenfold execution of qualities in singing is as follows:

1.50.s: raktaṃ pūrṇamalaṅkṛtaṃ prasannaṃ vyaktaṃ vikruṣṭaṃ ślakṣṇaṃ samaṃ sukumāraṃ madhuramiti guṇāstatra raktaṃ nāma veṇuvīṇāsvarāṇāmekībhāvaṃ raktamityucyate pūrṇaṃ nāma svaraśrutipūraṇācchandaḥ pādākṣaraṃ saṃyogātpūrṇamityucyate alaṅkṛtaṃ nāmorasi śirasi kaṇṭhayuktamityalaṅkṛtaṃ prasannaṃ nāmāpagatāgadgadanirviśaṅkaṃ prasannamityucyate vyaktaṃ nāma padapadārthaprakṛtivikārāgamanopakṛttaddhitasamāsadhātunipātopasargasvaraliṅgaṃ vṛttivārttikavibhaktyarthavacanānāṃ samyagupapādanaṃ vyaktamityucyate vikruṣṭaṃ nāmoñcairuñcāritaṃ vyaktapadākṣaraṃ vikruṣṭamityucyate ślekṣṇaṃ nāma drutamavilaṃbitamuccanīcaplutasamāhārahelatālopanayādibhirupapādanābhiḥ ślakṣṇamityucyate samaṃ nāmāvāpanirvāpapradeśe pratyantarasthānānāṃ samāsaḥ samamityucyate sukumāraṃ nāma mṛdupadavarṇasvarakuhagaraṇayuktaṃ sukumāramityucyate madhuraṃ nāma svabhāvopanītalalitapadākṣaraguṇasamṛddhaṃ madhuramityucyate evametairdaśabhirguṇairyuktaṃ gānaṃ bhavati // 1//
1.50.d: रक्तं पूर्णमलङ्कृतं प्रसन्नं व्यक्तं विक्रुष्टं श्लक्ष्णं समं सुकुमारं मधुरमिति गुणास्तत्र रक्तं नाम वेणुवीणास्वराणामेकीभावं रक्तमित्युच्यते पूर्णं नाम स्वरश्रुतिपूरणाच्छन्दः पादाक्षरं संयोगात्पूर्णमित्युच्यते अलङ्कृतं नामोरसि शिरसि कण्ठयुक्तमित्यलङ्कृतं प्रसन्नं नामापगतागद्गदनिर्विशङ्कं प्रसन्नमित्युच्यते व्यक्तं नाम पदपदार्थप्रकृतिविकारागमनोपकृत्तद्धितसमासधातुनिपातोपसर्गस्वरलिङ्गं वृत्तिवार्त्तिकविभक्त्यर्थवचनानां सम्यगुपपादनं व्यक्तमित्युच्यते विक्रुष्टं नामोञ्चैरुञ्चारितं व्यक्तपदाक्षरं विक्रुष्टमित्युच्यते श्लेक्ष्णं नाम द्रुतमविलंबितमुच्चनीचप्लुतसमाहारहेलतालोपनयादिभिरुपपादनाभिः श्लक्ष्णमित्युच्यते समं नामावापनिर्वापप्रदेशे प्रत्यन्तरस्थानानां समासः सममित्युच्यते सुकुमारं नाम मृदुपदवर्णस्वरकुहगरणयुक्तं सुकुमारमित्युच्यते मधुरं नाम स्वभावोपनीतललितपदाक्षरगुणसमृद्धं मधुरमित्युच्यते एवमेतैर्दशभिर्गुणैर्युक्तं गानं भवति ॥ 1॥
1.50.m: Harmonious (rakta), full (pūrṇa), ornamented (alaṅkṛta), lucid (prasanna), distinct (vyakta), raised (vikruṣṭa), smooth (ślakṣṇa), even (sama), delicate (sukumāra), and sweet (madhura)—these are the qualities. Among them, 'harmonious' means that the unison of the notes of the flute and the lute is called harmonious. 'Full' means that by filling out notes and microtones (śrutis), the syllables of the metrical quarters are brought into alignment; this is called full. 'Ornamented' means performed appropriately in the chest, the head, and the throat; this is called ornamented. 'Lucid' means free from stammering and hesitation; this is called lucid. 'Distinct' means that words, word-meanings, base forms, phonetic modifications, augmentations, prefixes, secondary suffixes, compounds, roots, particles, preverbs, pitch accents, grammatical gender, grammatical functions, vārttika rules, nominal case meanings, and numbers are correctly produced; this is called distinct. 'Raised' means uttered loudly with distinct words and syllables; this is called raised. 'Smooth' means produced gracefully, neither too hurried nor delayed, with proper management of high, low, and prolonged accents, easy cadence, and elision; this is called smooth. 'Even' means that in insertions and omissions the mutual pauses between adjacent positions are harmonized; this is called even. 'Delicate' means furnished with soft words, phonemes, and notes in gentle sequences; this is called delicate. 'Sweet' means rich in the naturally charming qualities of graceful words and syllables; this is called sweet. Thus singing is endowed with these ten qualities.

1.50.s:
bavanti cātra ślokāḥ
śaṅkitaṃ bhīṣaṇaṃ bhītamuddhuṣṭamanunāsikam /
kākasvaraṃ mūrddhagataṃ tathā sthānavivarjitam //
1.50.d:
बवन्ति चात्र श्लोकाः
शङ्कितं भीषणं भीतमुद्धुष्टमनुनासिकम् ।
काकस्वरं मूर्द्धगतं तथा स्थानविवर्जितम् ॥
1.50.m: There are also verses on this topic: / Hesitant, terrifying, frightened, shouted, nasal, / crow-voiced, off-pitch in the head, devoid of proper place of articulation,

1.50.s:
vistaraṃ virasaṃ caiva viśliṣṭaṃ viṣamāhatam /
vyākulaṃ tālahīnaṃ ca gītidoṣāścaturdaśa //
1.50.d:
विस्तरं विरसं चैव विश्लिष्टं विषमाहतम् ।
व्याकुलं तालहीनं च गीतिदोषाश्चतुर्दश ॥
1.50.m: diffuse, tasteless, disjointed, unevenly struck, / confused, and devoid of rhythm (tāla)—these are the fourteen defects of singing.

1.50.s:
ācāryāḥ samamicchanti padacchedaṃ tu paṇḍitāḥ /
sriyo madhuramicchanti vikruṣṭamitare janāḥ //
1.50.d:
आचार्याः सममिच्छन्ति पदच्छेदं तु पण्डिताः ।
स्रियो मधुरमिच्छन्ति विक्रुष्टमितरे जनाः ॥
1.50.m: The teachers desire evenness, while scholars desire proper division of words; / women desire sweetness, and other people desire loud volume.

1.50.s:
padmapatraprabhaḥ ṣaṅja ṛṣabhaḥ śukapiñjaraḥ /
kanakābhastu gāndhāro madhyamaḥ kundasannibhaḥ //
1.50.d:
पद्मपत्रप्रभः षङ्ज ऋषभः शुकपिञ्जरः ।
कनकाभस्तु गान्धारो मध्यमः कुन्दसन्निभः ॥
1.50.m: Ṣaḍja has the radiance of a lotus petal; ṛṣabha is reddish-yellow like a parrot; / gāndhāra has the hue of gold; madhyama resembles a kunda flower;

1.50.s:
pañcamastu bhavetkṛṣṇaḥ pītakaṃ dhaivataṃ viduḥ /
niṣādaḥ sarvavarṇaḥ syādityetāḥ svaravarṇatāḥ //
1.50.d:
पञ्चमस्तु भवेत्कृष्णः पीतकं धैवतं विदुः ।
निषादः सर्ववर्णः स्यादित्येताः स्वरवर्णताः ॥
1.50.m: pañcama should be dark; they know dhaivata to be yellow; / niṣāda is multicolored: such are the colors of the notes.

1.50.s:
pacamo madhyamaḥ ṣaṅja ityete brāhmaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ /
ṛṣabho dhaivataścāpītyetau vai kṣatriyāvubhau //
1.50.d:
पचमो मध्यमः षङ्ज इत्येते ब्राह्मणाः स्मृताः ।
ऋषभो धैवतश्चापीत्येतौ वै क्षत्रियावुभौ ॥
1.50.m: Pañcama, madhyama, and ṣaḍja are remembered as brāhmaṇas; / ṛṣabha and dhaivata are both kṣatriyas;

1.50.s:
gāndhāraśca niṣādaśca vaiśyāvarddhena vai smṛto /
śūdratvaṃ vidhinārddhena patitatvānna saṃśayaḥ //
1.50.d:
गान्धारश्च निषादश्च वैश्यावर्द्धेन वै स्मृतो ।
शूद्रत्वं विधिनार्द्धेन पतितत्वान्न संशयः ॥
1.50.m: gāndhāra and niṣāda are recognized as half vaiśya; / by rule, they are half śūdra, because they are fallen, without doubt.

1.50.s:
ṛṣabho mūrchitavarjito dhaivatasahitaśca pañcamo yatra /
nipatati madhyamarāge sa niṣādaṃ ṣāṅjavaṃ vidyāt //
1.50.d:
ऋषभो मूर्छितवर्जितो धैवतसहितश्च पञ्चमो यत्र ।
निपतति मध्यमरागे स निषादं षाङ्जवं विद्यात् ॥
1.50.m: Where ṛṣabha is free of mūrcchanā and pañcama is combined with dhaivata / and falls in the madhyamarāga, one should know that to be a ṣāḍava [scale] with niṣāda.

1.50.s:
yadi pañcamo viramate gāndhāraścāntarasvaro bhavati /
ṛṣabho niṣādasahitastaṃ pañcamamīdṛśaṃ vidyāt //
1.50.d:
यदि पञ्चमो विरमते गान्धारश्चान्तरस्वरो भवति ।
ऋषभो निषादसहितस्तं पञ्चममीदृशं विद्यात् ॥
1.50.m: If pañcama comes to rest and gāndhāra becomes an intermediate note, / and ṛṣabha is joined with niṣāda, one should know such to be pañcama.

1.50.s:
gāndhārasyādhipatyena niṣādasya gatāgataiḥ /
dhaivatasya ca daurbalyānmadhyamagrāma ucyate //
1.50.d:
गान्धारस्याधिपत्येन निषादस्य गतागतैः ।
धैवतस्य च दौर्बल्यान्मध्यमग्राम उच्यते ॥
1.50.m: Through the dominance of gāndhāra, the movements of niṣāda, / and the weakness of dhaivata, the madhyama-grāma is proclaimed.

1.50.s:
īṣatpṛṣṭo niṣādastu gāndhāraścādhiko bhavet /
dhaivataḥ kaṃpito yatra sa ṣaṅgayāma īritaḥ //
1.50.d:
ईषत्पृष्टो निषादस्तु गान्धारश्चाधिको भवेत् ।
धैवतः कंपितो यत्र स षङ्गयाम ईरितः ॥
1.50.m: Where niṣāda is slightly touched, gāndhāra is heightened, / and dhaivata is shaken, that is said to be the ṣaḍja-grāma.

1.50.s:
antarasvarasaṃyuktaḥ kākaliryatra dṛśyate /
taṃ tu sādhāritaṃ vidyātpañcamasthaṃ tu kaiśikam //
1.50.d:
अन्तरस्वरसंयुक्तः काकलिर्यत्र दृश्यते ।
तं तु साधारितं विद्यात्पञ्चमस्थं तु कैशिकम् ॥
1.50.m: Where the kākalī [note] is seen joined with an intermediate note, / one should know that as sādhārita; but that which resides in pañcama is kaiśika.

1.50.s:
kaiśikaṃ bhāvayitvā tu svaraiḥ sarvaiḥ samantataḥ /
yasmā ttu madhyame nyāsastasmātkaiśikamadhyamaḥ //
1.50.d:
कैशिकं भावयित्वा तु स्वरैः सर्वैः समन्ततः ।
यस्मा त्तु मध्यमे न्यासस्तस्मात्कैशिकमध्यमः ॥
1.50.m: Having produced kaiśika on all sides through all the notes, / because the resting note (nyāsa) is in madhyama, it is therefore called kaiśikamadhyama.

1.50.s:
kākalirdṛśyate yatra prādhānyaṃ pañcamasya tu /
kaśyapaḥ kaiśikaṃ prāha madhyamagrāmasaṃbhavam //
1.50.d:
काकलिर्दृश्यते यत्र प्राधान्यं पञ्चमस्य तु ।
कश्यपः कैशिकं प्राह मध्यमग्रामसंभवम् ॥
1.50.m: Where the kākalī is observed and the pañcama is predominant, / Kaśyapa declared that [mode] to be the kaiśika, arising from the madhyamagrāma.

1.50.s:
geti geyaṃ viduḥ prājñā dheti kārupravādanam /
veti vādyasya saṃjñeyaṃ gandharvasya prarocanam //
1.50.d:
गेति गेयं विदुः प्राज्ञा धेति कारुप्रवादनम् ।
वेति वाद्यस्य संज्ञेयं गन्धर्वस्य प्ररोचनम् ॥
1.50.m: The wise know that 'ga' means singing, 'dha' means the instrument's sounding, / and 'va' is the designation of an instrument; this is the explanation of 'gandharva'.

1.50.s:
yaḥ sāmagānāṃ prathamaḥ sa veṇormadhyamaḥ svaraḥ /
yo dvitīyaḥ sa gāndhārastṛtīyastvṛṣabhaḥ smṛtaḥ //
1.50.d:
यः सामगानां प्रथमः स वेणोर्मध्यमः स्वरः ।
यो द्वितीयः स गान्धारस्तृतीयस्त्वृषभः स्मृतः ॥
1.50.m: The note which is the first among the Sāman-singers is the madhyama note of the flute; / that which is the second is the gāndhāra, and the third is remembered as the ṛṣabha;

1.50.s:
caturthaḥ ṣaṅja ityāhuḥ pañcamo dhaivato bhavet /
ṣaṣṭho niṣādo vijñeyaḥ saptamaḥ pañcamaḥ smṛtaḥ //
1.50.d:
चतुर्थः षङ्ज इत्याहुः पञ्चमो धैवतो भवेत् ।
षष्ठो निषादो विज्ञेयः सप्तमः पञ्चमः स्मृतः ॥
1.50.m: The fourth, they say, is the ṣaḍja; the fifth is the dhaivata; / the sixth is known as the niṣāda; and the seventh is remembered as the pañcama.

1.50.s:
ṣaṅjaṃ mayūro vadati gāvo raṃbhanti carṣabham /
ajāvike tu gāndhāraṃ kraiñco vadati madhyamam //
1.50.d:
षङ्जं मयूरो वदति गावो रंभन्ति चर्षभम् ।
अजाविके तु गान्धारं क्रैञ्चो वदति मध्यमम् ॥
1.50.m: The peacock cries the ṣaḍja, and cows low the ṛṣabha; / goats and sheep bleat the gāndhāra, and the krauñca utters the madhyama;

1.50.s:
puṣpasādhāraṇe kāle kokilā vakti pañcamam /
aśvastu dhaivataṃ vakti niṣaādaṃ vakti kuñjaraḥ //
1.50.d:
पुष्पसाधारणे काले कोकिला वक्ति पञ्चमम् ।
अश्वस्तु धैवतं वक्ति निषआदं वक्ति कुञ्जरः ॥
1.50.m: In the season of flowers, the cuckoo sings the pañcama; / the horse utters the dhaivata, and the elephant trumpets the niṣāda.

1.50.s:
kaṇṭhāduttiṣṭate ṣaṅjaḥ śirasastvṛṣabhaḥ smṛtaḥ /
gāndhārastvanunāsikya uraso madhyamaḥ svaraḥ //
1.50.d:
कण्ठादुत्तिष्टते षङ्जः शिरसस्त्वृषभः स्मृतः ।
गान्धारस्त्वनुनासिक्य उरसो मध्यमः स्वरः ॥
1.50.m: The ṣaḍja arises from the throat, and the ṛṣabha is remembered to come from the head; / the gāndhāra is nasal, and the madhyama note comes from the chest.

1.50.s:
urasaḥ śirasaḥ kaṇṭhādutthitaḥ pañcamaḥ svaraḥ /
lalāṭāddhaivataṃ vidyānniṣādaṃ sarvasandhijam //
1.50.d:
उरसः शिरसः कण्ठादुत्थितः पञ्चमः स्वरः ।
ललाटाद्धैवतं विद्यान्निषादं सर्वसन्धिजम् ॥
1.50.m: the note pañcama arises from the chest, head, and throat; / one should know dhaivata from the forehead, and niṣāda born from all the joints.

1.50.s:
nāsā kaṇṭhamurastālujihvādatāṃśca saṃśritaḥ /
ṣaṅbhiḥ saṃ jāyate yasmāttasmātṣaṅja iti smṛtaḥ //
1.50.d:
नासा कण्ठमुरस्तालुजिह्वादतांश्च संश्रितः ।
षङ्भिः सं जायते यस्मात्तस्मात्षङ्ज इति स्मृतः ॥
1.50.m: Relying on the nose, the throat, the chest, the palate, the tongue, and the teeth, / it is born from these six, and therefore it is remembered as the ṣaḍja.

1.50.s:
vāyuḥ samutthito nābheḥ kaṇṭhaśīrṣasamāhataḥ /
nardatyṛṣabhavadyasmāttasmādṛṣerbha ucyate //
1.50.d:
वायुः समुत्थितो नाभेः कण्ठशीर्षसमाहतः ।
नर्दत्यृषभवद्यस्मात्तस्मादृषेर्भ उच्यते ॥
1.50.m: The wind arising from the navel, striking the throat and the head, / roars like a bull; therefore it is called the ṛṣabha.

1.50.s:
vāyuḥ samutthito nābheḥ kaṇṭhaśīrṣasamāhataḥ /
vāti gandhavahaḥ puṇyo gāndhārastena hetunā //
1.50.d:
वायुः समुत्थितो नाभेः कण्ठशीर्षसमाहतः ।
वाति गन्धवहः पुण्यो गान्धारस्तेन हेतुना ॥
1.50.m: The wind arising from the navel, striking the throat and the head, / blows as a pure carrier of fragrance; for that reason it is the gāndhāra.

1.50.s:
vāyuḥ samutthito nābherurau hṛdi samāhataḥ /
nābhiprāpto madhyavartī madhyamatvaṃ samarśnute //
1.50.d:
वायुः समुत्थितो नाभेरुरौ हृदि समाहतः ।
नाभिप्राप्तो मध्यवर्ती मध्यमत्वं समर्श्नुते ॥
1.50.m: The wind arising from the navel, striking the chest and the heart, / reaches the navel and, dwelling in the middle, attains the quality of madhyama.

1.50.s:
vāyuḥ samutthito nābherurohṛtkaṇṭhakāhṛtaḥ /
pañcasthānotthitasyāsya pañcamatvaṃ vidhīyate //
1.50.d:
वायुः समुत्थितो नाभेरुरोहृत्कण्ठकाहृतः ।
पञ्चस्थानोत्थितस्यास्य पञ्चमत्वं विधीयते ॥
1.50.m: The wind arising from the navel, drawn through the chest, heart, and throat, / coming forth from five places, is designated as the pañcama.

1.50.s:
dhaivataṃ ca niṣādaṃ ca varjayitvā tu tāvubhau /
śeṣānpañca svarāṃstvanye pañcasthānotthitānviduḥ //
1.50.d:
धैवतं च निषादं च वर्जयित्वा तु तावुभौ ।
शेषान्पञ्च स्वरांस्त्वन्ये पञ्चस्थानोत्थितान्विदुः ॥
1.50.m: Excepting both the dhaivata and the niṣāda, / others consider the remaining five notes as arising from five places.

1.50.s:
pañcasthānasthitatvena sarvasthānāni dhāryate /
agnigītasvaraḥ ṣaṅja ṛṣabho brahmaṇocyate //
1.50.d:
पञ्चस्थानस्थितत्वेन सर्वस्थानानि धार्यते ।
अग्निगीतस्वरः षङ्ज ऋषभो ब्रह्मणोच्यते ॥
1.50.m: By abiding in five places, it maintains all places. / The ṣaḍja note is sung by Agni, and the ṛṣabha is spoken by Brahmā;

1.50.s:
somena gīto gāndhāro viṣṇunā madhyamaḥ svaraḥ /
pañcamastu svaro gītastvayaiveti nidhāraya //
1.50.d:
सोमेन गीतो गान्धारो विष्णुना मध्यमः स्वरः ।
पञ्चमस्तु स्वरो गीतस्त्वयैवेति निधारय ॥
1.50.m: The gāndhāra was sung by Soma, and the madhyama note by Viṣṇu; / and ascertain that the pañcama note was sung by you alone [Nārada].

1.50.s:
dhaivataśca niṣādaśca gītau tuṃburuṇā svarau /
ādyaṃsya daivataṃ brahmā ṣaṅjasyāpyucyate budhaiḥ //
1.50.d:
धैवतश्च निषादश्च गीतौ तुंबुरुणा स्वरौ ।
आद्यंस्य दैवतं ब्रह्मा षङ्जस्याप्युच्यते बुधैः ॥
1.50.m: The dhaivata and niṣāda notes were sung by Tumburu. / Brahmā is also declared by the wise to be the deity of the first note, the ṣaḍja;

1.50.s:
tīkṣṇadīptaprakāśatvādṛṣabhasya hutāśanaḥ /
gāvaḥ praṇīte tuṣyanti gāndhārastena hetunā //
1.50.d:
तीक्ष्णदीप्तप्रकाशत्वादृषभस्य हुताशनः ।
गावः प्रणीते तुष्यन्ति गान्धारस्तेन हेतुना ॥
1.50.m: Because of its sharp and blazing brilliance, Hutāśana is [the deity] of the ṛṣabha; / cows are delighted when it is performed, and for that reason it is the gāndhāra;

1.50.s:
śrutvā caivopatiṣṭanti saurabheyā na saṃśayaḥ /
somastu pañcamasyāpi daivataṃ brahmarādrasmṛtam //
1.50.d:
श्रुत्वा चैवोपतिष्टन्ति सौरभेया न संशयः ।
सोमस्तु पञ्चमस्यापि दैवतं ब्रह्मराद्रस्मृतम् ॥
1.50.m: And having heard it, the progeny of Surabhī surely approach without doubt. / Soma is remembered as the deity of the pañcama, O sage-seer [Nārada];

1.50.s:
nihrāso yasya vṛddhiśca grāmamāsādya somavat /
atisaṃdhīyate yasmādetānpūrvotthitānsvarān //
1.50.d:
निह्रासो यस्य वृद्धिश्च ग्राममासाद्य सोमवत् ।
अतिसंधीयते यस्मादेतान्पूर्वोत्थितान्स्वरान् ॥
1.50.m: Like the moon, its decrease and increase occur depending on the grāma; / because it binds together these previously arisen notes,

1.50.s:
tasmādasya svarasyāpi dhaivatatvaṃ vidhīyate /
niṣīdanti svarā yasmānniṣādastena hetunā //
1.50.d:
तस्मादस्य स्वरस्यापि धैवतत्वं विधीयते ।
निषीदन्ति स्वरा यस्मान्निषादस्तेन हेतुना ॥
1.50.m: Therefore the quality of dhaivata is ordained for this note. / Because the notes settle down [into it], for that reason it is the niṣāda;

1.50.s: sarvāṃścābhibhavatyeṣa yadādityo 'sya daivatam //
1.50.d: सर्वांश्चाभिभवत्येष यदादित्यो ऽस्य दैवतम् ॥
1.50.m: And because Āditya is its deity, it overpowers all [other notes].

1.50.s: dāravī gātravīṇā ca dve vīṇe gānajātiṣu //
1.50.d: दारवी गात्रवीणा च द्वे वीणे गानजातिषु ॥
1.50.m: Among the classes of song, there are two vīṇās: the wooden vīṇā and the bodily vīṇā.

1.50.s:
sāmanī gātravīṇā tu tasyāstvaṃ śṛṇu lakṣaṇam /
gātravīṇā tu sā proktā yasyāṃ gāyanti sāmaṅgāḥ //
1.50.d:
सामनी गात्रवीणा तु तस्यास्त्वं शृणु लक्षणम् ।
गात्रवीणा तु सा प्रोक्ता यस्यां गायन्ति सामङ्गाः ॥
1.50.m: The bodily vīṇā belongs to the Sāman; listen now to its characteristics. / That is declared to be the bodily vīṇā on which the Sāman-singers sing,

1.50.s:
svaravyañjanasaṃyuktā aṅgulyaṅguṣṭarañjitā /
hastau tu saṃyatau dhāryauṃ jānubhyāmuparisthitau //
1.50.d:
स्वरव्यञ्जनसंयुक्ता अङ्गुल्यङ्गुष्टरञ्जिता ।
हस्तौ तु संयतौ धार्यौं जानुभ्यामुपरिस्थितौ ॥
1.50.m: Joined with vowels and consonants, illuminated by the fingers and thumb. / The two restrained hands should be kept resting above the knees.

1.50.s:
guroranukṛtiṃ kuryādyathānyā na matirbhavet /
praṇavaṃ prākprayuñjīta vyāhṛtīstadanantaram //
1.50.d:
गुरोरनुकृतिं कुर्याद्यथान्या न मतिर्भवेत् ।
प्रणवं प्राक्प्रयुञ्जीत व्याहृतीस्तदनन्तरम् ॥
1.50.m: One should imitate the teacher so that no other thought occurs. / One should first utter the praṇava, and immediately after that the vyāhṛtis;

1.50.s:
sāvitrīṃ cānuvacanaṃ tato vai gānamārabhet /
prasārya cāṅgulīḥ sarvā ropayetsvaramaṇḍalam //
1.50.d:
सावित्रीं चानुवचनं ततो वै गानमारभेत् ।
प्रसार्य चाङ्गुलीः सर्वा रोपयेत्स्वरमण्डलम् ॥
1.50.m: Then the Sāvitrī and the recitation, and after that one should indeed begin the song. / Extending all the fingers, one should establish the circle of notes.

1.50.s:
na cāṅgulībhiraṅguṣṭamaṅguṣṭenāgulīḥ spṛśet /
viralā nāṅgulīḥ kuryānmūle caitāṃ na saṃspṛśet //
1.50.d:
न चाङ्गुलीभिरङ्गुष्टमङ्गुष्टेनागुलीः स्पृशेत् ।
विरला नाङ्गुलीः कुर्यान्मूले चैतां न संस्पृशेत् ॥
1.50.m: One should not touch the thumb with the fingers, nor the fingers with the thumb; / one should not hold the fingers wide apart, nor touch them at the base.

1.50.s:
aṅguṣṭhāgreṇa tā nityaṃ madhyame parvaṇi spṛśet /
mātrādvimātravṛddhānāṃ vibhāgārthe vibhāgavit //
1.50.d:
अङ्गुष्ठाग्रेण ता नित्यं मध्यमे पर्वणि स्पृशेत् ।
मात्राद्विमात्रवृद्धानां विभागार्थे विभागवित् ॥
1.50.m: Knowing the divisions, one should always touch them at the middle joint with the tip of the thumb, / for the sake of dividing the single-mātrā and two-mātrā increments.

1.50.s:
aṅgulībhirdvimātraṃ tu pāṇeḥ savyasya darśayet /
trirekhā yasya dṛśyate siddhiṃ tatra vinirdiśet //
1.50.d:
अङ्गुलीभिर्द्विमात्रं तु पाणेः सव्यस्य दर्शयेत् ।
त्रिरेखा यस्य दृश्यते सिद्धिं तत्र विनिर्दिशेत् ॥
1.50.m: One should indicate a duration of two mātrās with the fingers of the left hand; / where three lines are seen, one should indicate success there.

1.50.s:
sa parva iti vijñeyaḥ śeṣamantaramantaram /
parvāntaraṃ sāmasu ca ṛkṣu kuryāttilāntaram //
1.50.d:
स पर्व इति विज्ञेयः शेषमन्तरमन्तरम् ।
पर्वान्तरं सामसु च ऋक्षु कुर्यात्तिलान्तरम् ॥
1.50.m: That is to be known as a joint; the rest is interval after interval. / One should make an interval between joints in the Sāmans, and an interval the size of a sesame seed in the Ṛks.

1.50.s:
svarānmadhyamaparvasu suniviṣṭaṃ niveśayet /
na cātra kaṃpayetkiñcidaṅgasyāvayavaṃ budhaḥ //
1.50.d:
स्वरान्मध्यमपर्वसु सुनिविष्टं निवेशयेत् ।
न चात्र कंपयेत्किञ्चिदङ्गस्यावयवं बुधः ॥
1.50.m: One should set the notes well positioned upon the middle joints; / and here the wise person should not shake any part of the limb.

1.50.s:
adhastanaṃ mṛdaṃ nyasya hastamātre yathākramam /
abhramadhye yathā vidyudṛśyate maṇisūtravat //
1.50.d:
अधस्तनं मृदं न्यस्य हस्तमात्रे यथाक्रमम् ।
अभ्रमध्ये यथा विद्युदृश्यते मणिसूत्रवत् ॥
1.50.m: Placing the lower hand lightly, according to proper order in the measure of a hand, / just as lightning is seen in the midst of a cloud like a string of gems,

1.50.s:
pṛṣacchedavivṛttīnāṃ yathā bāleṣukartarī /
kūrmo 'gāni ca saṃhṛtya cetodṛṣṭiṃ diśanmanaḥ //
1.50.d:
पृषच्छेदविवृत्तीनां यथा बालेषुकर्तरी ।
कूर्मो ऽगानि च संहृत्य चेतोदृष्टिं दिशन्मनः ॥
1.50.m: Or as scissors [moving swiftly] among hair in cutting off drops [or tufts], / drawing in one's limbs like a tortoise, directing the mind and gaze with consciousness,

1.50.s:
svasthaḥ praśānto nirbhīko varṇānuñcārayedbudhaḥ /
nāsikāyāstu pūrveṇa hastaṃ gokarṇavaddharet //
1.50.d:
स्वस्थः प्रशान्तो निर्भीको वर्णानुञ्चारयेद्बुधः ।
नासिकायास्तु पूर्वेण हस्तं गोकर्णवद्धरेत् ॥
1.50.m: At ease, tranquil, and fearless, the wise one should utter the syllables. / One should hold the hand forward from the nose, shaped like a cow's ear.

1.50.s:
niveśya dṛṣṭiṃ hastāgre śāstrārthamanucintayet /
samyakpracārayedvākyaṃ hastena ca mukhena ca //
1.50.d:
निवेश्य दृष्टिं हस्ताग्रे शास्त्रार्थमनुचिन्तयेत् ।
सम्यक्प्रचारयेद्वाक्यं हस्तेन च मुखेन च ॥
1.50.m: Fixing one's gaze on the tip of the hand, one should reflect on the meaning of the scripture; / one should properly project the phrase with both hand and mouth.

1.50.s:
yathaivoccārayedvarṇāṃstathaivaināṃ samāpayet /
nātyāhanyānna nirhaṇyānna pragāyenna kaṃpayet //
1.50.d:
यथैवोच्चारयेद्वर्णांस्तथैवैनां समापयेत् ।
नात्याहन्यान्न निर्हण्यान्न प्रगायेन्न कंपयेत् ॥
1.50.m: Just as one begins the syllables, so should one bring them to an end; / one should not strike too hard, nor suppress, nor prolong improperly, nor tremble.

1.50.s:
samaṃ sāmāni gāyeta vyomni svena gātiryathā /
yathā sucaratāṃ mārgo mīnānāṃ nopalabhyate //
1.50.d:
समं सामानि गायेत व्योम्नि स्वेन गातिर्यथा ।
यथा सुचरतां मार्गो मीनानां नोपलभ्यते ॥
1.50.m: One should sing the Sāmans evenly, just as a bird moves in the sky; / just as the path of fishes swimming smoothly cannot be perceived,

1.50.s:
ākāśe vā vihṝṅgānāṃ tadvatsvaragatā śrutiḥ /
yathā dadhini sarpiḥ syātkāṣṭastho vā yathānalaḥ //
1.50.d:
आकाशे वा विहॄङ्गानां तद्वत्स्वरगता श्रुतिः ।
यथा दधिनि सर्पिः स्यात्काष्टस्थो वा यथानलः ॥
1.50.m: Or of birds in the sky, even so is the microtone (śruti) residing in a note. / Just as ghee is present in curd, or fire resides in wood,

1.50.s:
prayatnenopalabhyeta tadvatsvaragatā śrutiḥ /
svarātsvarasya saṃkrāmaṃsvarasaṃdhimanulbaṇam //
1.50.d:
प्रयत्नेनोपलभ्येत तद्वत्स्वरगता श्रुतिः ।
स्वरात्स्वरस्य संक्रामंस्वरसंधिमनुल्बणम् ॥
1.50.m: And is perceived with effort, even so is the microtone residing in a note. / The transition from note to note and the junction of notes should be unobtrusive,

1.50.s:
avicchinnaṃ samaṃ kuryātsūkṣmacchāyātapopamam /
anāgatamatikrāntaṃ vicchinnaṃ viṣamāhatam //
1.50.d:
अविच्छिन्नं समं कुर्यात्सूक्ष्मच्छायातपोपमम् ।
अनागतमतिक्रान्तं विच्छिन्नं विषमाहतम् ॥
1.50.m: Continuous, and smooth, resembling subtle light and shade. / The wise person should avoid a vocal glide (karṣaṇa) that is premature, overdue, broken, or unevenly struck,

1.50.s:
tanvantamasthitāntaṃ ca varjayetkarṣaṇaṃ budhaḥ /
svaraḥ sthānāccyuto yastu svaṃ sthānamativartate //
1.50.d:
तन्वन्तमस्थितान्तं च वर्जयेत्कर्षणं बुधः ।
स्वरः स्थानाच्च्युतो यस्तु स्वं स्थानमतिवर्तते ॥
1.50.m: Or one that trails off into thinness or has an unstable end. / A note that falls away from its pitch and exceeds its proper position—

1.50.s:
vistaraṃ sāmagā brūyurviraktamiti vīṇinaḥ /
abhyāsārthe drutāṃ vṛttiṃ prayogārthe tu madhyamām //
1.50.d:
विस्तरं सामगा ब्रूयुर्विरक्तमिति वीणिनः ।
अभ्यासार्थे द्रुतां वृत्तिं प्रयोगार्थे तु मध्यमाम् ॥
1.50.m: The Sāman-singers call that vistara, and the vīṇā-players call it virakta. / For practice, [use] the fast tempo; for performance, the medium [tempo];

1.50.s:
śiṣyaṇāmupadeśārthaṃ kuryādvṛttiṃ vilaṃbitām /
gṛhītagrantha evaṃ tu granthoñcāraṇaśaikṣakān //
1.50.d:
शिष्यणामुपदेशार्थं कुर्याद्वृत्तिं विलंबिताम् ।
गृहीतग्रन्थ एवं तु ग्रन्थोञ्चारणशैक्षकान् ॥
1.50.m: For instructing pupils, one should use the slow tempo. / Having thus mastered the text, [when instructing] students in reciting the text,

1.50.s:
haste nādhyāpayecchiṣyān śaikṣeṇa vidhinā dvijaḥ /
kruṣṭasya mūrddhani sthānaṃ lalāṭe prathamasya tu //
1.50.d:
हस्ते नाध्यापयेच्छिष्यान् शैक्षेण विधिना द्विजः ।
क्रुष्टस्य मूर्द्धनि स्थानं ललाटे प्रथमस्य तु ॥
1.50.m: A twice-born should teach the pupils by hand according to the pedagogical rule. / The position of the kruṣṭa is in the head, and of the prathama in the forehead;

1.50.s:
bhruvormadhya dvitīyasya tṛtīyasya tu karṇayoḥ /
kaṇṭhasthānaṃ caturthasya mandrasya rasanocyate //
1.50.d:
भ्रुवोर्मध्य द्वितीयस्य तृतीयस्य तु कर्णयोः ।
कण्ठस्थानं चतुर्थस्य मन्द्रस्य रसनोच्यते ॥
1.50.m: Of the dvitīya, between the eyebrows; and of the tṛtīya, in the ears; / the position of the caturtha is the throat; the tongue is said to be [the place] of the mandra;

1.50.s:
atisvarasya nīcasya hṛdi sthānaṃ vidhīyate /
aṅguṣṭasyottame vruṣṭo hyaṅguṣṭaṃ prathamaḥ svaraḥ //
1.50.d:
अतिस्वरस्य नीचस्य हृदि स्थानं विधीयते ।
अङ्गुष्टस्योत्तमे व्रुष्टो ह्यङ्गुष्टं प्रथमः स्वरः ॥
1.50.m: The position of the low atisvārya is prescribed in the heart. / The kruṣṭa is on the top of the thumb, and the prathama note is on the thumb;

1.50.s:
pradeśinyāṃ tu gāndhāra ṛṣabhastadanantaram /
anāmikāyāṃ ṣaṅgastu kaniṣṭāyāṃ tu dhaivataḥ //
1.50.d:
प्रदेशिन्यां तु गान्धार ऋषभस्तदनन्तरम् ।
अनामिकायां षङ्गस्तु कनिष्टायां तु धैवतः ॥
1.50.m: The gāndhāra is on the forefinger, and the ṛṣabha immediately after it; / the ṣaḍja is on the ring finger, and the dhaivata on the little finger;

1.50.s:
tasyādhastāñca yonyāstu niṣādaṃ tatra nirdiśet /
aparvatvādamadhyatvā davyayatvāñca nityaśaḥ //
1.50.d:
तस्याधस्ताञ्च योन्यास्तु निषादं तत्र निर्दिशेत् ।
अपर्वत्वादमध्यत्वा दव्ययत्वाञ्च नित्यशः ॥
1.50.m: And below it, at its base, one should indicate the niṣāda, / because it has no joint, is not in the middle, and is perpetually unchanging.

1.50.s:
mandro hi mandībhūtastu parisvāra iti smṛtaḥ /
kruṣṭena devā jīvanti prathamena tu mānuṣāḥ //
1.50.d:
मन्द्रो हि मन्दीभूतस्तु परिस्वार इति स्मृतः ।
क्रुष्टेन देवा जीवन्ति प्रथमेन तु मानुषाः ॥
1.50.m: The mandra, when subdued, is traditionally remembered as parisvāra. / By the kruṣṭa the gods live, but human beings by the prathama;

1.50.s:
paśavastu dvitīyena gandharvāpsarasastvanu /
andhajāḥ pitaraścaiva caturthasvarajīvinaḥ //
1.50.d:
पशवस्तु द्वितीयेन गन्धर्वाप्सरसस्त्वनु ।
अन्धजाः पितरश्चैव चतुर्थस्वरजीविनः ॥
1.50.m: cattle live by the dvitīya, and gandharvas and apsarases next; / birds and the ancestors indeed live by the caturtha tone.

1.50.s:
mandratvenopajīvanti piśācāsurarākṣasāḥ /
atisvareṇa nīcena jagatsthāvarajaṅgamāḥ //
1.50.d:
मन्द्रत्वेनोपजीवन्ति पिशाचासुरराक्षसाः ।
अतिस्वरेण नीचेन जगत्स्थावरजङ्गमाः ॥
1.50.m: Piśācas, asuras, and rākṣasas live by means of the mandra; / the mobile and immobile world lives by the low atisvara.

1.50.s:
sarvāṇi khalu bhūtāni dhāryante sāmikaiḥ svaraiḥ /
dīptāyatākaruṇānāṃ mṛdumadhyamayostathā //
1.50.d:
सर्वाणि खलु भूतानि धार्यन्ते सामिकैः स्वरैः ।
दीप्तायताकरुणानां मृदुमध्यमयोस्तथा ॥
1.50.m: All living beings are indeed sustained by the Sāmic tones. / Of the dīptā, āyatā, and karuṇā, and likewise of the mṛdu and madhyamā,

1.50.s:
śrutīnāṃ yo viśeṣajño na sa ācārya ucyate /
dīptā mandre dvitīya ca pracaturthe tathaiva ca //
1.50.d:
श्रुतीनां यो विशेषज्ञो न स आचार्य उच्यते ।
दीप्ता मन्द्रे द्वितीय च प्रचतुर्थे तथैव च ॥
1.50.m: he who does not know the distinction between the microtones is not called a teacher. / Dīptā is in the mandra, and in the dvitīya, and likewise in the caturtha;

1.50.s:
atisvare tṛtīye ca kruṣṭe tu karuṇā śrutiḥ /
śrutayo yā dvitīyasya mṛdumadhyāyatāḥ smṛtāḥ //
1.50.d:
अतिस्वरे तृतीये च क्रुष्टे तु करुणा श्रुतिः ।
श्रुतयो या द्वितीयस्य मृदुमध्यायताः स्मृताः ॥
1.50.m: and in the atisvara and the tṛtīya, while in the kruṣṭa the karuṇā microtone is found. / Those which are the microtones of the dvitīya are recalled as mṛdu, madhyā, and āyatā.

1.50.s:
tāsāmapi tu vakṣyāmi lakṣaṇāni pṛthak pṛthak /
āyatātvaṃ bhavennīce mṛdutā tu viparyaye //
1.50.d:
तासामपि तु वक्ष्यामि लक्षणानि पृथक् पृथक् ।
आयतात्वं भवेन्नीचे मृदुता तु विपर्यये ॥
1.50.m: I shall also describe their specific characteristics one by one: / āyatatva occurs in a low note, but mṛdutā occurs in the contrary;

1.50.s:
sve svare madhyamātvaṃ tu tatsamīkṣya prayojayet /
dvitīye viratā yā tu kruṣṭaśca parato bhavet //
1.50.d:
स्वे स्वरे मध्यमात्वं तु तत्समीक्ष्य प्रयोजयेत् ।
द्वितीये विरता या तु क्रुष्टश्च परतो भवेत् ॥
1.50.m: madhyamatva occurs in its own tone; observing that, one should apply it. / That which pauses on the dvitīya and a kruṣṭa occurs beyond it,

1.50.s:
dīptāṃ tāṃ tu vijānīyātprāthamyena mṛduḥ smṛtaḥ /
atraiva viratā yā tu caturthena pravartate //
1.50.d:
दीप्तां तां तु विजानीयात्प्राथम्येन मृदुः स्मृतः ।
अत्रैव विरता या तु चतुर्थेन प्रवर्तते ॥
1.50.m: one should know that as dīptā; because of primacy it is remembered as mṛdu. / That which pauses right here and proceeds by the caturtha,

1.50.s:
tathā mandre bhaveddīptā sāmnaścaiva samāpane /
nātitāraśrutiṃ kuryātsvarayornāpi cāntare //
1.50.d:
तथा मन्द्रे भवेद्दीप्ता साम्नश्चैव समापने ।
नातितारश्रुतिं कुर्यात्स्वरयोर्नापि चान्तरे ॥
1.50.m: likewise in the mandra, is dīptā, and also at the conclusion of a sāman. / One should not make an excessively high pitch, nor between two tones;

1.50.s:
taṃ ca hrasve ca dīrghe ca na cāpi ghuṭisajñake /
dvividhā gatiḥ padāntasthitasaṃdhiḥ sahoṣmabhiḥ //
1.50.d:
तं च ह्रस्वे च दीर्घे च न चापि घुटिसज्ञके ।
द्विविधा गतिः पदान्तस्थितसंधिः सहोष्मभिः ॥
1.50.m: and on a short or long [syllable], nor on what is called a ghuṭi. / Twofold is the movement: a pause standing at the end of a word together with spirants.

1.50.s:
sthāneṣu pañcasveteṣu vijñeya ghuṭisaṃjñakam /
svarāntarāviratāni hrasvadīrghaghuṭāni ca //
1.50.d:
स्थानेषु पञ्चस्वेतेषु विज्ञेय घुटिसंज्ञकम् ।
स्वरान्तराविरतानि ह्रस्वदीर्घघुटानि च ॥
1.50.m: In these five positions it is to be known as having the designation ghuṭi: / unpaused between tones, short, long, and ghuṭa.

1.50.s:
sthitisthāneṣvaśeṣāṇi śrutivatsvarato vadet /
dīptāmudātte jānīyāddīptāṃ ca svarite viduḥ //
1.50.d:
स्थितिस्थानेष्वशेषाणि श्रुतिवत्स्वरतो वदेत् ।
दीप्तामुदात्ते जानीयाद्दीप्तां च स्वरिते विदुः ॥
1.50.m: In all positional resting-places, one should recite in accordance with pitch as with a microtone. / One should know dīptā on an acute (udātta), and they know dīptā on a circumflex (svarita);

1.50.s:
anudātte mṛdurjñeyā gandharvāḥ śrutisaṃpade /
udāttaścānudāttaśca svaritapracite tathā //
1.50.d:
अनुदात्ते मृदुर्ज्ञेया गन्धर्वाः श्रुतिसंपदे ।
उदात्तश्चानुदात्तश्च स्वरितप्रचिते तथा ॥
1.50.m: on a grave (anudātta) it should be known as mṛdu, [as do] the gandharvas for perfection of microtones. / Acute and grave, and circumflex and monotone (pracita),

1.50.s:
nighātaśceti vijñeyaḥ svarabhedaśca pañcadhā /
ata ūrdhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi ācikasya svaratrayam //
1.50.d:
निघातश्चेति विज्ञेयः स्वरभेदश्च पञ्चधा ।
अत ऊर्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि आचिकस्य स्वरत्रयम् ॥
1.50.m: and what is known as low pitch (nighāta)—thus pitch variation is fivefold. / Beyond this I shall declare the threefold pitch of the Ācika recitation:

1.50.s:
udāttaścānudāttaśca tṛtīyaḥ svaritaḥ svaraḥ /
ya evodātta ityuktaḥ sa eva svaritātparaḥ //
1.50.d:
उदात्तश्चानुदात्तश्च तृतीयः स्वरितः स्वरः ।
य एवोदात्त इत्युक्तः स एव स्वरितात्परः ॥
1.50.m: acute, grave, and the third pitch is the circumflex. / That which is spoken of as acute, that very pitch following a circumflex

1.50.s:
pracayaḥ procyate tajjñairna cātrānyatsvarāntaram /
varṇasvaro 'tītasvaraḥ svarito dvividhaḥ smṛtaḥ //
1.50.d:
प्रचयः प्रोच्यते तज्ज्ञैर्न चात्रान्यत्स्वरान्तरम् ।
वर्णस्वरो ऽतीतस्वरः स्वरितो द्विविधः स्मृतः ॥
1.50.m: is termed monotone by the experts, and there is no other different tone here. / A syllable pitch and an unaccented pitch: the circumflex is remembered as twofold.

1.50.s:
mātriko varṇa evaṃ tu dīrghastūñcaritādanu /
sa tu saptavidho jñeyaḥ svaraḥ pratyayadarśanāt //
1.50.d:
मात्रिको वर्ण एवं तु दीर्घस्तूञ्चरितादनु ।
स तु सप्तविधो ज्ञेयः स्वरः प्रत्ययदर्शनात् ॥
1.50.m: A syllable consisting of one measure is thus [so pronounced], while a long one follows the uttered sound. / It is to be known as sevenfold according to the observation of its context;

1.50.s:
padena tu sa vijñeyo bhavedyo yatra yādṛśaḥ /
saptasvarānprayuñjīta dakṣiṇaṃ śravaṇaṃ prati //
1.50.d:
पदेन तु स विज्ञेयो भवेद्यो यत्र यादृशः ।
सप्तस्वरान्प्रयुञ्जीत दक्षिणं श्रवणं प्रति ॥
1.50.m: it is to be recognized by the word, whatever and of whatever kind it may be in a given place. / One should apply the seven notes toward the right ear.

1.50.s:
ācāryairvihitaṃ śāstraṃ putraśiṣyahitaiṣibhiḥ /
uccāduñcataraṃ nāsti nīcānnīcataraṃ tathā //
1.50.d:
आचार्यैर्विहितं शास्त्रं पुत्रशिष्यहितैषिभिः ।
उच्चादुञ्चतरं नास्ति नीचान्नीचतरं तथा ॥
1.50.m: The treatise was composed by the teachers desiring the welfare of their sons and pupils. / There is nothing higher than high, nor anything lower than low.

1.50.s:
vaisvaryasvārasaṃjñāyāṃ kiṃsthānaḥ svāra ucyate /
uccanīcasya yanmadhye sādhāraṇamiti śrutiḥ //
1.50.d:
वैस्वर्यस्वारसंज्ञायां किंस्थानः स्वार उच्यते ।
उच्चनीचस्य यन्मध्ये साधारणमिति श्रुतिः ॥
1.50.m: With the designation 'accentual circumflex' (vaisvaryasvāra), what position is assigned to the circumflex? / That which is in between high and low is said by scripture to be common [to both].

1.50.s:
taṃ svāraṃ svārasaṃjñāyāṃ pratijānanti śaikṣikāḥ /
udātte niṣādagāndhārāvanudātteṃ ṛṣabhadhaivato //
1.50.d:
तं स्वारं स्वारसंज्ञायां प्रतिजानन्ति शैक्षिकाः ।
उदात्ते निषादगान्धारावनुदात्तें ऋषभधैवतो ॥
1.50.m: Students of phonetics recognize that circumflex under the name svāra. / In the acute are niṣāda and gāndhāra; in the grave are ṛṣabha and dhaivata;

1.50.s:
svaritaprabhavā hyete ṣaṅjamadhyamapañcamāḥ /
yatra kakhaparā ūṣmā jihvāmūlaprayojanāḥ //
1.50.d:
स्वरितप्रभवा ह्येते षङ्जमध्यमपञ्चमाः ।
यत्र कखपरा ऊष्मा जिह्वामूलप्रयोजनाः ॥
1.50.m: indeed, these arise from the circumflex: ṣaḍja, madhyama, and pañcama. / Where the spirants are followed by k and kh, having their point of articulation at the root of the tongue,

1.50.s:
tānapyājñāpayenmātrāprakṛtyaiva tu sā kalā /
jātyaḥ kṣaipro 'bhinihita stairavyañjana eva ca //
1.50.d:
तानप्याज्ञापयेन्मात्राप्रकृत्यैव तु सा कला ।
जात्यः क्षैप्रो ऽभिनिहित स्तैरव्यञ्जन एव च ॥
1.50.m: one should direct them also by measure; indeed, that fraction is according to nature. / The innate (jātya), the rapid (kṣaipra), the absorbed (abhinihita), and the stairavyañjana,

1.50.s:
tirovirāmaḥ praśliṣṭo 'pādavṛttaśca saptamaḥ /
svarāṇāmahameteṣāṃ pṛthagvakṣyāmi lakṣaṇam //
1.50.d:
तिरोविरामः प्रश्लिष्टो ऽपादवृत्तश्च सप्तमः ।
स्वराणामहमेतेषां पृथग्वक्ष्यामि लक्षणम् ॥
1.50.m: the tirovirāma, the contracted (praśliṣṭa), and the pādavṛtta is the seventh. / I shall declare the characteristic of each of these pitches separately,

1.50.s:
uddiṣṭānāṃ tathā nyāyamudāharaṇameva ca /
sapakāraṃ savaṃ vāpi hyakṣaraṃ svaritaṃ bhavet //
1.50.d:
उद्दिष्टानां तथा न्यायमुदाहरणमेव च ।
सपकारं सवं वापि ह्यक्षरं स्वरितं भवेत् ॥
1.50.m: as well as the rule and the example for those mentioned: / A syllable containing a 'p' or an 's' that becomes circumflex,

1.50.s:
na codāttaṃ puro yasya jātyaḥ svāraḥ sa ucyate /
iuvarṇo yadodāttāvāpadyete pavau kvacit //
1.50.d:
न चोदात्तं पुरो यस्य जात्यः स्वारः स उच्यते ।
इउवर्णो यदोदात्तावापद्येते पवौ क्वचित् ॥
1.50.m: and before which there is no acute, is called an innate circumflex. / When the vowels i and u, being acute, turn into semi-vowels y and v in some place,

1.50.s:
anudāttaṃ pratyaye tu vidyātkṣaiprasya lakṣaṇam /
eo ābhyāmudāttābhyāmakāro nihitaśca yaḥ //
1.50.d:
अनुदात्तं प्रत्यये तु विद्यात्क्षैप्रस्य लक्षणम् ।
एओ आभ्यामुदात्ताभ्यामकारो निहितश्च यः ॥
1.50.m: and a grave vowel follows, one should recognize the characteristic of the kṣaipra. / When an a is placed after the two acute vowels e and o,

1.50.s:
akāro yatra luṃpati tamabhinihitaṃ viduḥ /
udāttapūrve yatkiñcicchandasi svaritaṃ bhavet //
1.50.d:
अकारो यत्र लुंपति तमभिनिहितं विदुः ।
उदात्तपूर्वे यत्किञ्चिच्छन्दसि स्वरितं भवेत् ॥
1.50.m: and that a is elided, they know that as abhinihita. / Whatever is circumflex in the Veda preceded by an acute,

1.50.s:
eṣa sarvabahusvārastairavyañjana ucyate /
avagrahātparaṃ yatra svaritaṃ syādanantaram //
1.50.d:
एष सर्वबहुस्वारस्तैरव्यञ्जन उच्यते ।
अवग्रहात्परं यत्र स्वरितं स्यादनन्तरम् ॥
1.50.m: this circumflex, which occurs most commonly of all, is called stairavyañjana. / Where a circumflex immediately follows an avagraha pause,

1.50.s:
tirovirāmaṃ taṃ vidyādudātto yadyavagrahaḥ /
ikāraṃ yatra paśyeyurikāreṇaiva saṃyutam //
1.50.d:
तिरोविरामं तं विद्यादुदात्तो यद्यवग्रहः ।
इकारं यत्र पश्येयुरिकारेणैव संयुतम् ॥
1.50.m: one should know that as tirovirāma, if the [vowel before the] avagraha is acute. / Where one sees the letter i joined with the letter i,

1.50.s:
udāttamanudāttena praśliṣṭaṃ taṃ vicāraya /
svare cetsvaritaṃ yatra vivṛtā yatra saṃhitā //
1.50.d:
उदात्तमनुदात्तेन प्रश्लिष्टं तं विचारय ।
स्वरे चेत्स्वरितं यत्र विवृता यत्र संहिता ॥
1.50.m: an acute with a grave, consider that to be praśliṣṭa. / If there is a circumflex on a vowel where there is an open juncture,

1.50.s:
etatpādāntavṛttasya lakṣaṇaṃ śāstranoditam /
tānyaḥ svāraḥ sa jātyena śrutyagre kṣaipra ucyate //
1.50.d:
एतत्पादान्तवृत्तस्य लक्षणं शास्त्रनोदितम् ।
तान्यः स्वारः स जात्येन श्रुत्यग्रे क्षैप्र उच्यते ॥
1.50.m: this is the characteristic of the pādavṛtta taught in the treatise. / The innate svāra is exemplified in tānyaḥ; at the beginning of a phonetic text kṣaipra is stated,

1.50.s:
te manvatābhinitastairavyañjana ūtaye /
tirovirāmo viṣkaṣite praśliṣṭo hīīgovarṇaḥ //
1.50.d:
ते मन्वताभिनितस्तैरव्यञ्जन ऊतये ।
तिरोविरामो विष्कषिते प्रश्लिष्टो हीईगोवर्णः ॥
1.50.m: [as in] te manvata; abhinihita in stairavyañjana ūtaye; / tirovirāma in viṣkaṣite; praśliṣṭa in hīīgovarṇaḥ;

1.50.s:
pādavṛttaḥ kandavidesvarāḥ saptaivamādayaḥ /
uñcādekākṣarātpūrvātsvaraṃ yadyadihākṣaram //
1.50.d:
पादवृत्तः कन्दविदेस्वराः सप्तैवमादयः ।
उञ्चादेकाक्षरात्पूर्वात्स्वरं यद्यदिहाक्षरम् ॥
1.50.m: pādavṛtta in kandavide: thus are the seven pitches and so forth. / Following a high single-syllabled predecessor, whatever vowel syllable is here,

1.50.s:
svārāṇāṃ jātyavarjānāmeṣā prakṛtirucyate /
catvārastvāditaḥ svārāḥ kaṃṣaṃpuṃśphutiśāstrataḥ //
1.50.d:
स्वाराणां जात्यवर्जानामेषा प्रकृतिरुच्यते ।
चत्वारस्त्वादितः स्वाराः कंषंपुंश्फुतिशास्त्रतः ॥
1.50.m: this is declared to be the inherent nature of the circumflexes, excepting the innate ones. / But the first four circumflexes, according to the treatise on tremolo (kampa) and bursting tones,

1.50.s:
udātte caikanīce vā juhvo 'gnistannidarśanam /
ikārānte pade pūrva ukāre parataḥ sthite //
1.50.d:
उदात्ते चैकनीचे वा जुह्वो ऽग्निस्तन्निदर्शनम् ।
इकारान्ते पदे पूर्व उकारे परतः स्थिते ॥
1.50.m: on an acute or on a single low tone: juhvo 'gniḥ is the example of that. / When a word ending in the vowel i precedes and the vowel u stands after it,

1.50.s:
hrasvaṃ kaṃpaṃ vijānīyānmedhāvī nātra saṃśayaḥ /
ikārānte pade caivokāradvayaṃ pare pade //
1.50.d:
ह्रस्वं कंपं विजानीयान्मेधावी नात्र संशयः ।
इकारान्ते पदे चैवोकारद्वयं परे पदे ॥
1.50.m: the wise person should know it as a short tremolo; there is no doubt here. / And when a word ends in the vowel i and two u-vowels follow in the next word,

1.50.s:
dīrghaṃ kaṃpaṃ vijānīyācchāgdhūṣviti nidarśanam /
trayo dīrghāstu vijñeyā ye ca saṃdhyakṣareṣu vai //
1.50.d:
दीर्घं कंपं विजानीयाच्छाग्धूष्विति निदर्शनम् ।
त्रयो दीर्घास्तु विज्ञेया ये च संध्यक्षरेषु वै ॥
1.50.m: one should know it as a long tremolo; chāgdhūṣu is the example. / Three long [tremolos] are to be known, namely those in diphthongs,

1.50.s:
manyā yathā na indrābhyāṃ śeṣā hrasvāḥ prakīrtitāḥ /
anekānāmudāttānāmanudāttaḥ pratyayo yadi //
1.50.d:
मन्या यथा न इन्द्राभ्यां शेषा ह्रस्वाः प्रकीर्तिताः ।
अनेकानामुदात्तानामनुदात्तः प्रत्ययो यदि ॥
1.50.m: such as manyā na indrābhyām; the rest are declared as short. / If there is a grave following several acutes,

1.50.s:
śivakaṃpaṃ vijānīyādudāttaḥ pratyayo yadi /
yatra dviprabhṛtīni syurudāttānyakṣarāṇi tu //
1.50.d:
शिवकंपं विजानीयादुदात्तः प्रत्ययो यदि ।
यत्र द्विप्रभृतीनि स्युरुदात्तान्यक्षराणि तु ॥
1.50.m: one should know it as a auspicious tremolo (śivakampa), if an acute is the following element. / Where, however, two or more syllables are acute,

1.50.s:
nīcaṃ voñcaṃ ca paratastatrodāttaṃ vidurbudhāḥ /
na rephe vā hakāre vā dvirbhāvo jāyate kvacit //
1.50.d:
नीचं वोञ्चं च परतस्तत्रोदात्तं विदुर्बुधाः ।
न रेफे वा हकारे वा द्विर्भावो जायते क्वचित् ॥
1.50.m: and a low or a high note follows, the wise know the acute to be there. / Doubling never occurs in the letter r or the letter h,

1.50.s:
na ca vargadvitīyeṣu na caturthe kadācana /
caturthaṃ tu tṛtīyena dvitīyaḥ prathamena tu //
1.50.d:
न च वर्गद्वितीयेषु न चतुर्थे कदाचन ।
चतुर्थं तु तृतीयेन द्वितीयः प्रथमेन तु ॥
1.50.m: nor ever in the second consonants of a class, nor in the fourth. / A fourth [is doubled] by a third, but a second by a first;

1.50.s:
ādyamantyaṃ ca madhyaṃ ca svārākṣareṇa pīḍayet /
anantyaśca bhavetpūrvo hyantaśca parato yadi //
1.50.d:
आद्यमन्त्यं च मध्यं च स्वाराक्षरेण पीडयेत् ।
अनन्त्यश्च भवेत्पूर्वो ह्यन्तश्च परतो यदि ॥
1.50.m: one should compress the initial, the final, and the medial by an accented syllable. / If a non-final [stop] is initial, and a final [nasal] follows,

1.50.s:
tatra madhye yamastiṣṭhetsvavarṇaḥ pūrvavaṇayoḥ /
vargāntyān śaṣasaiḥ sārddhamantasthairvāpi saṃyutān //
1.50.d:
तत्र मध्ये यमस्तिष्ठेत्स्ववर्णः पूर्ववणयोः ।
वर्गान्त्यान् शषसैः सार्द्धमन्तस्थैर्वापि संयुतान् ॥
1.50.m: there in the middle a yama should stand, possessing its own color of the two preceding sounds. / Seeing class-finals joined with ś, ṣ, and s, or with semivowels,

1.50.s:
dṛṣṭvā yamā nivartante adeśikamivādhvagāḥ /
tṛtīyaśca caturthaśca caturthādiparaṃ padam //
1.50.d:
दृष्ट्वा यमा निवर्तन्ते अदेशिकमिवाध्वगाः ।
तृतीयश्च चतुर्थश्च चतुर्थादिपरं पदम् ॥
1.50.m: the yamas turn back, like travelers lacking a guide. / A third and a fourth, followed by a word beginning with a fourth;

1.50.s:
dvau tṛtīyau hakāraśca hakārādiparaṃ padam /
anusvāropadhāmūlā tān kvacitkramataḥ param //
1.50.d:
द्वौ तृतीयौ हकारश्च हकारादिपरं पदम् ।
अनुस्वारोपधामूला तान् क्वचित्क्रमतः परम् ॥
1.50.m: two thirds and the letter h, followed by a word beginning with h; / anusvāra and upadhmānīya: sometimes one duplicates beyond them.

1.50.s:
rahapūrvasaṃyute cāpyuttaraṃ kramate 'kṣaram /
saṃyogo yatra dṛśyeta rvyañjanaṃ virate pade //
1.50.d:
रहपूर्वसंयुते चाप्युत्तरं क्रमते ऽक्षरम् ।
संयोगो यत्र दृश्येत र्व्यञ्जनं विरते पदे ॥
1.50.m: Also when conjunct with r and h preceding, the subsequent syllable duplicates; / where a conjunct is seen, a consonant with r in a paused word [likewise].

1.50.s:
pūrvāṅgamāditaḥ kṛtvā parāṅgādau niveśayet /
saṃyoge svaritaṃ yatra udvātaḥ pratanaṃ tathā //
1.50.d:
पूर्वाङ्गमादितः कृत्वा पराङ्गादौ निवेशयेत् ।
संयोगे स्वरितं यत्र उद्वातः प्रतनं तथा ॥
1.50.m: Having placed the initial limb first, one should set it before the posterior limb. / Where there is a circumflex [accent] in a conjunct, [it is] elevated and likewise extended.

1.50.s:
pūrvāṅgaṃ tadvijānīyādyenāraṃbhaḥ paraṃ hi tat /
saṃyogāttu vijānīyātparaṃ saṃyoganāyakam //
1.50.d:
पूर्वाङ्गं तद्विजानीयाद्येनारंभः परं हि तत् ।
संयोगात्तु विजानीयात्परं संयोगनायकम् ॥
1.50.m: One should know that to be the prior limb by which the beginning [is made], for that is posterior; / but from a conjunct one should know the posterior to be the chief of the conjunct.

1.50.s:
saṃyuktasya tu varṇasya tatparaṃ pūrvamakṣaram /
anusvāraḥ padāntaśca kramajaṃ pratyaye svake //
1.50.d:
संयुक्तस्य तु वर्णस्य तत्परं पूर्वमक्षरम् ।
अनुस्वारः पदान्तश्च क्रमजं प्रत्यये स्वके ॥
1.50.m: The syllable prior to a conjunct sound follows it; / the anusvāra and word-ending arise from the krama when followed by their own conditioning sound.

1.50.s:
svarabhaktistathārephaḥ pūrvapūrvāṅgamucyate /
pādādau cāpādādau saṃyogāvagraheṣu ca //
1.50.d:
स्वरभक्तिस्तथारेफः पूर्वपूर्वाङ्गमुच्यते ।
पादादौ चापादादौ संयोगावग्रहेषु च ॥
1.50.m: The svarabhakti vowel-fragment and the sound r are called the preceding limb of each prior [sound], / both at the beginning of a verse-quarter and not at the beginning of a verse-quarter, and in conjuncts and pauses (avagraha).

1.50.s:
yaśabda iti vijñeyo yo 'nyaḥsaya iti smṛtaḥ /
pādādāvapyavicchedesaṃyogānte ca tiṣṭatām //
1.50.d:
यशब्द इति विज्ञेयो यो ऽन्यःसय इति स्मृतः ।
पादादावप्यविच्छेदेसंयोगान्ते च तिष्टताम् ॥
1.50.m: It should be known as the sound ya, while that which is other is remembered as saya, / occurring even at the beginning of a verse-quarter without break, and standing at the end of a conjunct.

1.50.s:
varjayitvā rahapāṇāmupādeśaḥ pradṛśyate /
svasaṃyukto gururjñeyaḥ sānusvārā grimaḥ sphuṭaḥ /
aṇuśeṣo hrigo vāpi yugalādiravisphuṭaḥ //
1.50.d:
वर्जयित्वा रहपाणामुपादेशः प्रदृश्यते ।
स्वसंयुक्तो गुरुर्ज्ञेयः सानुस्वारा ग्रिमः स्फुटः ।
अणुशेषो ह्रिगो वापि युगलादिरविस्फुटः ॥
1.50.m: Excluding r and h, the instruction is demonstrated: / one conjoined with itself should be known as heavy; accompanied by an anusvāra, the preceding [syllable] is clear; / having an atomic remnant, or […], the beginning of a pair is indistinct.

1.50.s:
yadudāttamudāttaṃ tadyatsvaritaṃ tatpade bhavati /
yannīcaṃ nīcameva tadyatpracayasthaṃ tadapi nīcam //
1.50.d:
यदुदात्तमुदात्तं तद्यत्स्वरितं तत्पदे भवति ।
यन्नीचं नीचमेव तद्यत्प्रचयस्थं तदपि नीचम् ॥
1.50.m: What is high-pitched (udātta) is udātta; what is circumflex (svarita) is in that word; / what is low-pitched (anudātta) is indeed low; what stands in the monotone (pracaya) is also low.

1.50.s:
agniḥ suto mitramidaṃ tathā vayamayāvahāḥ /
priyaṃ dūtaṃ ghṛtaṃ cittamatiśabdastu nīcataḥ //
1.50.d:
अग्निः सुतो मित्रमिदं तथा वयमयावहाः ।
प्रियं दूतं घृतं चित्तमतिशब्दस्तु नीचतः ॥
1.50.m: ‘Agniḥ’, ‘sutaḥ’, ‘mitram’, ‘idam’, likewise ‘vayam’, ‘ayāvahāḥ’, / ‘priyam’, ‘dūtam’, ‘ghṛtam’, ‘cittam’: the word ‘ati’ is from the low [tone].

1.50.s:
akveṣveva suteṣveva yajñeṣu kalaśeṣu ca /
śateṣu sapavitreṣu nīcāduñcāryate śrutiḥ //
1.50.d:
अक्वेष्वेव सुतेष्वेव यज्ञेषु कलशेषु च ।
शतेषु सपवित्रेषु नीचादुञ्चार्यते श्रुतिः ॥
1.50.m: In words such as ‘akveṣu’, ‘suteṣu’, ‘yajñeṣu’, and ‘kalaśeṣu’, / in ‘śateṣu’, and ‘sapavitreṣu’, the Vedic sound is pronounced from the low [tone].

1.50.s:
hārivaruṇavareṇyeṣu dhārāpuruṣeṣu svaratirephaḥ /
viśvānaronakāraśca śeṣāstusvaritā narāḥ //
1.50.d:
हारिवरुणवरेण्येषु धारापुरुषेषु स्वरतिरेफः ।
विश्वानरोनकारश्च शेषास्तुस्वरिता नराः ॥
1.50.m: In ‘hāri’, ‘varuṇa’, ‘vareṇyeṣu’, ‘dhārā’, ‘puruṣeṣu’, the sound r is accented; / ‘viśvānaraḥ’ has the letter na, and the remaining ‘narāḥ’ are circumflex.

1.50.s:
dvau varuṇau vasvarata uduttamantvaṃ varuṇadhāra caurudhārāmurudhāresvadohate /
mātrikaṃ vā dvimātraṃ vā svaryate yadihākṣaram /
tasyāditor'ddhamātraṃ vai śeṣaṃ tu parato bhavet /
adīrghaṃ dīrghavatkuryāddvisvaraṃ yatprayujyate //
1.50.d:
द्वौ वरुणौ वस्वरत उदुत्तमन्त्वं वरुणधार चौरुधारामुरुधारेस्वदोहते ।
मात्रिकं वा द्विमात्रं वा स्वर्यते यदिहाक्षरम् ।
तस्यादितोर्ऽद्धमात्रं वै शेषं तु परतो भवेत् ।
अदीर्घं दीर्घवत्कुर्याद्द्विस्वरं यत्प्रयुज्यते ॥
1.50.m: Two ‘varuṇas’ are accented: [in the passages] ‘uduttamam tvam varuṇa...’, [and] ‘dhāracaurudhārām...’ / If a syllable of one mora or two morae is accented here, / half a mora of it belongs to the beginning, and the remainder belongs to what follows; / one should make what is non-long like a long [syllable] when two vowels are employed.

1.50.s:
kaṃpotsvaritābhigītaṃ hrasvakarṣaṇameva ca /
nimeṣakālo mātrā syādvidyutkāleti cāpare //
1.50.d:
कंपोत्स्वरिताभिगीतं ह्रस्वकर्षणमेव च ।
निमेषकालो मात्रा स्याद्विद्युत्कालेति चापरे ॥
1.50.m: Tremor, elevated tone, singing out, and the dragging of a short vowel: / the measure of a mora is the time of a wink of the eye, and others say the duration of a lightning flash.

1.50.s: ṛksvarā tulyayogā vā kaiścidevamudīryate //
1.50.d: ऋक्स्वरा तुल्ययोगा वा कैश्चिदेवमुदीर्यते ॥
1.50.m: Vowels of the Ṛgveda or those of equal conjunction are described thus by some.

1.50.s:
samāse 'vagrahaṃ kuryātpadaṃ cātrānusaṃhitam /
yetīkṣarādikaraṇaṃ padāntasyeti taṃ viduḥ //
1.50.d:
समासे ऽवग्रहं कुर्यात्पदं चात्रानुसंहितम् ।
येतीक्षरादिकरणं पदान्तस्येति तं विदुः ॥
1.50.m: One should make a pause (avagraha) in a compound, and the word here is joined in saṃhitā; / they know the operation beginning with the letter ‘iti’ as belonging to the end of a word.

1.50.s:
